zh:
鹳喜欢考一考弟子们，他喜欢和这些年轻的后辈们谈天说地。所说之事，其实常常也并不局限于学问。
遇到了些什么困难？最近流行些什么书？有什么好玩的事？弟子们又给“烂鵙子”这老东西起了什么新的有趣外号？
看着这些后辈，他便想起自己年轻的时候，也会想起很多，回不来的人的年轻时候。
问东问西，甚至许多时候显得古怪啰嗦的老人，当然也不会忘记他最重要的身份——墨山道长老。
他关注着每个弟子的成长，也同时是在关注着这座山中任何的风吹草动。
其实他的同辈中，本有许多许多比他更优秀的人。他年轻时从未想过，有一日会是他成为长老，但如今他确实是长老之一了。
原因也很简单，那许多优秀的人，出山了便没有再回来……
一代一代啊，他的双眸从明亮到浑浊，他的心从不谙世事，到一个个凿出窍来。他如一块苍劲的石，静静垫在这座巨厦的最底部，不起眼，不动摇，就静静望着这墨山道几十年的革易。
新的巨子又来了，是个年轻人。年轻好啊……
这墨城中唯一不变的，就是这些年轻人。总有人年轻着，一代一代……
en:
Stork likes to put the disciples through their paces now and then, but really, he just enjoys talking with the younger generation. And what they talk about is not always limited to learning. What troubles have they run into lately? What books are people reading these days? What amusing things have happened? And what new nickname have the disciples come up with for that old fellow, "Rotten Shrike"?

Looking at these younger faces, he is reminded of his own youth, and of the youth of many who never came back.

This old man, forever asking questions and often coming off as oddly fussy, never forgets his most important identity: he is an elder of Mohist Hill. He watches over every disciple's growth, and at the same time keeps an eye on every stir and shift within the mountain.

In truth, many among his generation were far more gifted than he was. When he was young, he never imagined that one day he would become an elder himself. The reason is simple enough. So many of those outstanding people left the mountain and never returned...

Generation after generation, his bright eyes have grown clouded, and his once unworldly heart has been slowly carved open by experience. He is like an old, weathered stone laid quietly at the very foundation of a great building, unnoticed, unmoving, simply watching over the changes that have passed through Mohist Hill for decades.

And now a new Grandmaster has come, young again. Youth is a fine thing...

The only thing in Mohist City that never really changes is its young people. There is always someone young, generation after generation...

听闻你在祈福法会上受伤，我这几日寝食难安。怀月、索靖虽日日为你延医问药，却始终含糊其辞。

我知你性子倔强，可伤势若真有不妥，万不可硬撑。凉州何神医医术精湛，当年家父重伤垂危，也是他妙手回春。你若需要，我即刻派人快马去请，半日便可到府。

（收信人姓名被墨迹涂污）
en:
□□□,

I have heard that you were injured at the blessing ceremony, and for days now I have been unable to eat or sleep in peace. Huaiyue and Suojing attend to you daily, yet whenever I ask after your condition, they give only vague replies. They say it is nothing serious, but if that were true, why am I not even allowed through the gates? Yesterday I went to look for Huaiding, yet he avoided me as well. Such secrecy only weighs more heavily on my heart.

I know your temperament is stubborn, but if the injury is truly serious, you must not force yourself to endure it. There is a divine physician in Liangzhou whose skill is unmatched. When my father once lay gravely wounded, it was he who brought him back from the brink. If you wish, I will send a rider at once. He can reach your residence within half a day.

Awaiting your reply,
Zhang Qiu

en:
Why toil for lofty dreams in heavenly halls, when one can leisurely train wild boars in a stone chamber? 

Wild boars lie low by day and roam by night, with dark bristly coats and aggressive nature, often appearing in forests. Occasionally, they show up in farmlands, and were nicknamed "Black-faced Fellows" by the people. As one of the six domesticated animals, pigs had close ties with ancient people and symbolized strength. During the Qin, Han, and Six Dynasties, there was a cultural appreciation for wild boars. By the Song dynasty, this trend had faded. However, the Khitan still believed wild boars can bestow mystical power upon man, almost divine in nature.

zh:
【僖中第六】

【经】
十有六年，春，王正月，戊申，朔，陨石于宋五。是月，六鹢退飞，过宋都。
○三月，壬申，公子季友卒。
○夏，四月，丙申，鄫季姬卒。
○秋，七月，甲子，公孙兹卒。
○冬，十有二月，公会齐侯、宋公、陈侯、卫侯、郑伯、许男、邢侯、曹伯于淮。
【传】
十六年，春，陨石于宋五，陨星也。六鹢退飞，过宋都，风也。周内史叔兴聘于宋，宋襄公问焉，曰：“是何祥也？吉凶焉在？”对曰：“今兹鲁多大丧，明年齐有乱，君将得诸侯而不终。”退而告人曰：“君失问。是阴阳之事，非吉凶所在也。吉凶由人，吾不敢逆君故也。”
○夏，齐伐厉，不克，救徐而还。
○秋，狄侵晋，取狐、厨、受铎，涉汾，及昆都，因晋败也。
○王以戎难告于齐，齐征诸侯而戍周。
○冬，十一月，乙卯，郑杀子华。
○十二月，会于淮，谋鄫，且东略也。城鄫，役人病。有夜登丘而呼曰：“齐有乱。”不果城而还。
……
en:
【Xi Zhong, Part Six】

【Classic】
In the sixteenth year, in spring, the king's first month, on Wushen, the first day of the month, meteorites fell in Song, five of them. In this month, six ospreys flew backward, passing over the capital of Song.
○ In the third month, on Ren Shen, Duke Ji You of the son of the ruler passed away.
○ In summer, in the fourth month, on Bingshen, Ji of Zeng, the younger sister of the ruler, passed away.
○ In autumn, in the seventh month, on Jiazi, Gongsun Zi passed away.
○ In winter, in the twelfth month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Count of Xu, the Marquis of Xing, and the Earl of Cao at Huai.
【Commentary】
In the sixteenth year, in spring, meteorites fell in Song, five of them; they were falling stars. Six ospreys flew backward, passing over the capital of Song, due to the wind. The Zhou historian Shu Xing was on a diplomatic mission to Song, and Duke Xiang of Song asked him, saying: "What omen is this? Where do the auspicious and inauspicious signs lie?" He replied: "This year there will be many great mournings in Lu; next year there will be disorder in Qi; you, my lord, will gain the lords but will not see it through." When he withdrew, he told others: "The lord asked wrongly. These are matters of yin and yang, not where auspiciousness or inauspiciousness lies. Auspiciousness and inauspiciousness come from men; this is why I did not dare to go against the lord."
○ In summer, Qi attacked Li but did not overcome it; it rescued Xu and then returned.
○ In autumn, the Di invaded Jin, seizing Hu, Chu, and Shouduo, crossing the Fen River, and reaching Kundu, because of Jin's defeat.
○ The king reported the Rong troubles to Qi, and Qi summoned the lords and garrisoned Zhou.
○ In winter, in the eleventh month, on Yimao, Zheng killed Zi Hua.
○ In the twelfth month, they met at Huai to plan for Zeng and also to expand eastward. They built walls at Zeng, but the laborers were exhausted. One night, someone climbed a mound and shouted: "There is disorder in Qi." So they did not finish the walls and returned.
……

en:
Weiyang City is home to many treasure-hunting cats, but when it comes to appreciating fine treasures, none rival the famed pair—Quanquan and Shang Baobao. 
Shang Baobao, unlike the ever-serious Quanquan, takes delight in life itself. 
Why should one's skills be reserved only for judging antiques? Isn't the world itself full of wonders? 
Baobao admires the breeze by the alley, the lamplight on the street, and, should fate allow, the shapely legs of a passing calico... But if Quanquan catches it in the act, it's two kitten-punches straight to the whiskers. 
What a killjoy! Baobao sulks, though it dares not fight back. 
Ah well. Eat the human's cat food, do the human's job. 
Still... when will another pretty calico stroll by again?

归山。数年未归，昔日居所已赠予徒儿。

长兴元年，九月初九

师弟厚谊，宅中惟设一榻，吾二人同榻而眠。此半床之恩，当……记。
长兴二年，四月初一
归山。师姐程弋赠居所一座。师姐之情当记。
长兴三年，五月初五
归山之日近，吾不知为何心悸。
途径旧址发现一石洞甚是宜居，心中顿觉畅然。
en:
1st Day of the Fourth Month, 924 CE
Returned to the mountain. Having been away for several years, my old quarters had already been given to my disciple.
With no other choice, I lodged with Senior Brother Guan Shanyue for more than a hundred days. This kindness must be remembered.
15th Day of the Eighth Month, 925 CE
Returned to the mountain. Senior Brother Guan Shanyue had just married, and it would not have been proper to trouble him, so I was fortunate enough to stay with Senior Brother Zi'an.
Senior Brother is fond of singing, though sadly he has no ear for pitch. I moved out after ten days. Even so, his kindness must be remembered.
9th Day of the Ninth Month, 930 CE
Returned to the mountain. Stayed in Junior Brother Chuan Jin's quarters.
My junior brother showed me deep generosity. There was only a single bed in the room, so the two of us shared it. This kindness of half a bed must... be remembered.
1st Day of the Fourth Month, 931 CE
Returned to the mountain. Senior Sister Cheng Yi gifted me a dwelling of my own. Senior Sister's kindness must be remembered.
5th Day of the Fifth Month, 932 CE
The day of my return to the mountain draws near, though I know not why my heart is troubled.
Passing an old site on the way, I came upon a stone cave, a place most fit to dwell in. At once my heart grew light.

zh:
如是观音
孙不弃无数次梦见自己在一片血色的海中沉浮。
他无法预测梦的走向是噩梦还是美梦，大多数梦里，身边漂浮的尸体会变作狰狞的梦傀，勒住他的脖颈，将他拖入海底。
少数时候，会有一叶孤舟恰从他面前经过，舟上白纱覆面的素衣菩萨握住他的手腕，让他登船随她一起渡海。
仅有一次，头纱被风掠起，他得以一睹菩萨的真容——
菩萨的脸，就是师父水月的脸。

骤然从梦中惊醒时，才想起自己叛离师门已三月有馀。
往事如同蒙尘的镜，他与小师父当初，不是如今的疏离模样。
一同游历各州，一同施医布药，他甚至想过为她请一尊观音像作生辰礼。
只因他听受救助的人称赞，水月先生貌若观音，慈悲济世。
——啧，哪儿像了。
那时他们正处青州，他去步所能及的每一处寺院转了一圈，那里的菩萨造像大多是慈眉善目、神态安和的微笑样貌。
师父不太一样。
他说不出区别在哪儿，在寺里捡了块木炭，削尖了在竹纸上涂涂抹抹。
生辰礼嘛……亲手给她画幅观音小像聊表心意，也能充个数吧。
他的画技不好也不赖，画完拈起纸张时，拇指上沾的炭灰恰好落在头纱的位置。
白纱沾了污迹，可就不像观音了。他试图擦去那个指印，可越抹越黑。
他把画作揉成一团，随手丢了，这才意识到小师父与那些菩萨造像为何不像——
小师父虽待人温和，却始终不与人全然亲近，也就孙愿那种小孩子能得她几分欣然期许。
他很少见她笑，面上向来少有波澜，甚至眼睛里流露出情绪都极少。
想来是那些无知之人妄自解读，于这份无情中见悲悯、见哀愍，徒作如是观，想来可笑。
唯独那一次，他看清了她眼底翻涌的情绪。

孙不弃想起他在梦中见到的“菩萨”脸上的神情。
他对水月最后的记忆也停留在那里——
金刚怒目，不复低眉。

彻底与水月斩断师徒牵绊后，他反而感到一种解脱。
暗中行事、刻意欺瞒，总是煎熬的。
行迹败露时他甚至有些庆幸，总算不用继续小心翼翼掩藏。
他向来看得分明，是她不明白，一味慈心只能暂缓苍生苦痛，寻常行善治不了世间病根。
可另一种怅痛很快接踵而至——
汉墓的火烧毁了多数记忆，流水带走了剩下的全部。
一无所有中，他只感到空虚的怅惘。
他想，下一个梦里若是再见到孤舟上的菩萨，他要挣脱开她的手，任血红的海水漫过口鼻，梦傀将他包围。
然后他要看着小舟从他正上方漂流而过，而他沉入海底，从此各赴殊途，再无交集。

可这场梦境时隔多年才得以重现。
那个梦里，孤舟上早已不见菩萨身影，撑篙渡海之人是他自己。
汹涌的血海已然干涸，密密麻麻的梦傀高举双臂将他与孤舟凌空托举，将他“渡”向心之所向。
也许那时，可以结束迟来的痛苦。
en:
Guanyin's Visage
Sun Buqi dreamed countless times of drifting and sinking in a sea of blood.
He could never predict whether the dream would turn into a nightmare or something sweeter. In most of them, the corpses floating beside him would twist into hideous sleeping puppets, strangling his neck and dragging him down to the ocean floor.
On rare occasions, a lone boat would drift past him, and upon it, a veiled figure in plain white robes would take his wrist, drawing him aboard to cross the sea together.
Only once did the wind lift her veil, granting him a glimpse of the Bodhisattva's true countenance...
The Bodhisattva's face was the face of his Master, Moonstream.

Jolted awake from the dream, he suddenly remembered it had been over three months since he'd turned his back on his own sect.
The past was like a dust-covered mirror; he and his young master had once been nothing like the distant strangers they'd become.
They had once wandered the provinces together, dispensing medicine side by side. He'd even considered commissioning a statue of Guanyin as a birthday gift for her.
All because he'd heard those he'd helped praise Master Moonstream's face as resembling Guanyin's, compassionate and merciful to the world.
...Tch, as if.
Back then, they were in Qingzhou, and he'd made a circuit of every temple within walking distance. The Bodhisattva statues there mostly wore gentle brows and kind eyes, faces calm and smiling.
His Master wasn't quite the same.
He couldn't say where the difference lay, so he picked up a piece of charcoal from the temple and sharpened it, sketching away on bamboo paper.
For her birthday gift... painting her a small portrait of Guanyin with his own hand to express his feelings would at least count for something.
His painting skills were mediocre at best. When he lifted the finished paper, the charcoal dust on his thumb happened to smudge right over where the veil would be.
The white veil now bore a stain, and it no longer looked like Guanyin at all. He tried to wipe away the fingerprint, but the smear only darkened.
He crumpled the painting into a ball and tossed it aside, only then realizing why his young master never quite resembled those Bodhisattva statues.
Though his young master treated others gently, she never let anyone draw truly close to her. Only a child like Sun Yuan could earn even a flicker of fond expectation from her.
He rarely saw her smile; her expression was almost always still, and even her eyes seldom betrayed any emotion.
He supposed it was only the ignorant who read too much into it, imagining compassion and pity within that emotionless mask. A laughable notion, when he thought about it.
Only once did he see the emotion churning beneath her calm eyes.

Sun Buqi recalled the expression on the "Bodhisattva's" face that he'd seen in his dream.
His last memory of Moonstream stopped right there:
Eyes ablaze with wrath, no longer downcast in mercy.

Now that the bond of master and disciple between him and Moonstream was severed completely, he felt, strangely, a sense of release.
Acting in secrecy, deliberately deceiving her—it had always been agonizing.
When his tracks were finally uncovered, he even felt a measure of relief. At last, he no longer had to tread so carefully to hide himself.
He'd always seen it clearly, even if she never did: mere mercy could only ease the suffering of the world for a moment. Ordinary acts of kindness could never cure the root of its ills.
But another kind of sorrow soon followed close behind:
The fire at the Han Mausoleum had destroyed most of his memories, and the flowing water carried away all that remained.
Left with nothing, all he felt was a hollow, wistful emptiness.
He thought that if he saw the bodhisattva on the lone boat again in his next dream, he would tear his hand free from hers, let the blood-red sea flood over his mouth and nose, and let the sleeping puppets surround him.
Then he would watch the little boat drift past directly above him, while he sank to the ocean floor. From then on, their paths diverged, never to cross again.

But this dream did not recur until many years had passed.
In that dream, the bodhisattva was no longer on the lone boat—he himself was the one poling across the sea.
The surging sea of blood had long since dried up. Countless sleeping puppets raised their arms high, lifting him and the boat into the air, "ferrying" him toward what his heart desired.
Perhaps then, the long-overdue suffering could finally end.

【子张第十九】

子张曰：“士见危致命，见得思义，祭思敬，丧思哀，其可已矣。”
子张曰：“执德不弘，信道不笃，焉能为有？焉能为亡？”
子夏之门人问交于子张，子张曰：“子夏云何？”对曰：“子夏曰：‘可者与之，其不可者拒之。’”子张曰：“异乎吾所闻。君子尊贤而容众，嘉善而矜不能。我之大贤与，于人何所不容？我之不贤与，人将拒我，如之何其拒人也？”
子夏曰：“虽小道必有可观者焉，致远恐泥，是以君子不为也。”
子夏曰：“日知其所亡，月无忘其所能，可谓好学也已矣。”
子夏曰：“博学而笃志，切问而近思，仁在其中矣。”
子夏曰：“百工居肆以成其事，君子学以致其道。”
子夏曰：“小人之过也必文。”
子夏曰：“君子有三变：望之俨然，即之也温，听其言也厉。”
子夏曰：“君子信而后劳其民，未信，则以为厉己也；信而后谏，未信，则以为谤己也。”
子夏曰：“大德不逾闲，小德出入可也。”
子游曰：“子夏之门人小子，当洒扫应对进退则可矣。抑末也，本之则无，如之何？”子夏闻之，曰：“噫，言游过矣！君子之道，孰先传焉？孰后倦焉？譬诸草木，区以别矣。君子之道焉可诬也？有始有卒者，其惟圣人乎！”
子夏曰：“仕而优则学，学而优则仕。”
子游曰：“丧致乎哀而止。”
子游曰：“吾友张也为难能也，然而未仁。”
曾子曰：“堂堂乎张也，难与并为仁矣。”
曾子曰：“吾闻诸夫子，人未有自致者也，必也亲丧乎！”
曾子曰：“吾闻诸夫子，孟庄子之孝也，其他可能也；其不改父之臣与父之政，是难能也。”
孟氏使阳肤为士师，问于曾子。曾子曰：“上失其道，民散久矣。如得其情，则哀矜而勿喜！”
子贡曰：“纣之不善，不如是之甚也。是以君子恶居下流，天下之恶皆归焉。”
子贡曰：“君子之过也，如日月之食焉。过也，人皆见之；更也，人皆仰之。”

en:
【Book 19: Zi Zhang】

Zi Zhang said, "A scholar-official, when he sees danger, is ready to sacrifice his life; when he sees an opportunity for gain, he thinks of righteousness; in sacrifice, he thinks of reverence; in mourning, he thinks of grief. With these qualities, he may be considered complete."
Zi Zhang said, "If one holds to virtue but does not expand it, believes in the Way but is not steadfast in it, how can he be considered to have it? How can he be considered to lack it?"
Zi Xia's disciples asked Zi Zhang about making friends. Zi Zhang said, "What did Zi Xia say?" They replied, "Zi Xia said, 'Associate with those who are worthy, and reject those who are not.'" Zi Zhang said, "This differs from what I have heard. A gentleman respects the worthy and is tolerant toward the multitude; he commends the good and is compassionate toward the incapable. If I am greatly virtuous, whom can I not tolerate? If I am not virtuous, others will reject me. How then can I reject others?"
Zi Xia said, "Even in minor arts, there must be something worthy of observation. But if one pursues them to the extreme, they may become obstructive. Therefore, a gentleman does not engage in them."
Zi Xia said, "To learn daily what one lacks, and monthly not to forget what one has mastered—this may be called loving learning."
Zi Xia said, "Broad learning and steadfast purpose, earnest inquiry and reflection on what is near at hand—benevolence lies in these."
Zi Xia said, "Artisans dwell in their workshops to accomplish their tasks; a gentleman studies to attain the Way."
Zi Xia said, "The faults of a petty man are always glossed over."
Zi Xia said, "A gentleman undergoes three transformations: from a distance, he appears dignified; when approached, he is mild; when listening to his words, he is stern."
Zi Xia said, "A gentleman must gain trust before he tasks his people; without trust, they will think he is oppressing them. He must gain trust before he remonstrates; without trust, they will think he is slandering them."
Zi Xia said, "In great virtue, one should not overstep the bounds; in minor virtues, some leeway is permissible."
Zi You said, "The disciples of Zi Xia are competent in sweeping, responding, and proper conduct. But these are trivial matters. They lack the fundamentals. What is to be done?" When Zi Xia heard this, he said, "Alas, Yan You is mistaken! In the Way of the gentleman, what should be taught first? What should be taught later? It is like plants and trees, which are categorized and distinguished. How can the Way of the gentleman be misrepresented? Only a sage can have both beginning and end!"
Zi Xia said, "When an official excels, he should study; when a student excels, he should become an official."
Zi You said, "In mourning, grief should be expressed to the appropriate degree and then stop."
Zi You said, "My friend Zhang is capable of difficult things, yet he has not attained benevolence."
Zengzi said, "How imposing is Zhang! It is difficult to practice benevolence alongside him."
Zengzi said, "I heard from the Master that no one fully expresses their emotions except in mourning for parents."
Zengzi said, "I heard from the Master that Meng Zhuangzi's filial piety is such that other things may be possible, but not changing his father's ministers and his father's policies—this is truly difficult."
The Meng family appointed Yang Fu as chief judge, and he asked Zengzi for advice. Zengzi said, "Those above have lost the Way, and the people have been scattered for a long time. If you uncover the truth of their cases, show compassion and do not rejoice!"
Zi Gong said, "The wickedness of King Zhou was not as extreme as people say. Therefore, a gentleman dislikes being in a low position, for all the evils of the world are attributed to him."
Zi Gong said, "The faults of a gentleman are like eclipses of the sun and moon. When he errs, everyone sees it; when he corrects himself, everyone looks up to him."

He ate it for over ten years without growing tired of it. Some advised him that eating meat would hinder his cultivation, but the nameless Daoist laughed and said, "I enjoy eating fish. I am helping them cultivate, and one day, we will ascend to the immortal realm together." As the Daoist grew old and neared the end of his life, he suddenly had a dream. In the dream, the mountain spirit took physical form and scolded him for being unfair, only being kind to the fish and leaving it behind. The mountain spirit promised to take him to the immortal realm. Upon waking, the Daoist went into the mountains and gathered all the spirits he had seen in his dream. en: To seek learning at the Inkbound Order is to find rest from one's journey here. Pine breezes blow beside the Canglang waters, and the disciples of the Inkbound Order share their eaves with visitors from all around the world. On the Cuju Field, they dash about swift as the wind; at the Mo Pool, brush and inkstone stir up their own quiet tide. In the still chamber one may sink into deep thought; in the resting hall one may pass the time in easy conversation. From the Tidegazing Pavilion, one watches the tide rise; in Haoran Court, one hears the surge of voices and waves. Sundry goods and curious wares stand ready for the needs of each day; the smoke and fire of the Dining Hall offer the greatest comfort to a hungry belly. Today, the sound of strings and recitation fills the air between us. Tomorrow, we part ways upon the roads of the Jianghu. Folks from all the realm share the shelter of this single roof.

zh:
要找到那些背后的人，并不容易。但姜隗有他的法子。
他对镜贴妆，描唇画眉，嫁衣一披，比身后床榻上那惶恐落泪的女子还要美上几分。
“躲起来。”他笑得妩媚而温柔，“等花轿落地，再没人会来找你。”
他说到做到。每一次花轿落地，就是他出手之时。

只可惜，人心的欲望永无止境，而与欲望相比，人命实在太轻贱。
他花了好些年，也终究没能兑现他的诺言。
找到阿姐尸骨的那晚，他跪倒在地，强撑了这许多年，终于还是受不住了。
“阿姐，我已经分不清，我是那超度者，还是那已亡人。”
en:
Tracking the ones behind it all was no easy task. But Jiang Kui had his ways. 
Before a mirror, he painted his face, lined his lips, and arched his brows. Then he draped himself in bridal red. When he was done, he looked even more beautiful than the weeping girl trembling on the bed behind him. 
"Hide," he said with a soft, enchanting smile.
"Once the wedding sedan lands, no one will come looking for you again." 
And he always kept his word. Every time the bridal sedan touched the ground, he struck. 

But desire knows no limit, and compared to desire, a human life is lighter than feather. 
He spent years chasing his vow. And still, he never fulfilled it. 
The night he finally found his sister's remains, he collapsed to his knees. After all those years holding himself together, he could no longer bear it. 
"Sister," he whispered, "I don't even know anymore. Am I the one who lays the dead to rest, or one of the dead myself?"

黄河水泛滥的时候，杨义深的小鱼摊被冲得干干净净。
半辈子勤扒苦做，一场大水就什么也不剩。小女儿来不及跑，就这么顺着水被冲走，连尸体都找不到。
杨义深丢了神，挤在逃荒的人群中，本能地挪动着脚步。
不知去向何方，也不知走了多久，直到遇到一群衣衫褴褛的流民。
那些人喊杨义深跟着他们往前走，一起去寻神女庇佑的福地。
据说那神女会在福地接引走投无路之人去往桃源——洪水凶险，但桃源在天上，淹不着。
杨义深本不信神鬼，但他见这些人的眼睛里燃烧着狂热的光，像是看见活路似的。
既然横竖都无处可去，为了哄骗自己活下去，杨义深把心一横，就这么跟着他们走了。
en:
The Yellow River rose and erased Yang Yishen's world in a single night.
His fish stall, his living, his past—washed away as if they'd never been there. His youngest daughter never made it out. The river took her hand and would not let go. No corpse. No grave. Not even a place to kneel and cry.
He was swallowed by the tide of refugees, legs shuffling forward while his spirit lagged somewhere far behind. He didn't know where the road led. He didn't care.
At some point, he fell in with a pack of refugees dressed in rags and mud.
They told him to follow them, to keep moving forward together, toward a blessed land watched over by a Goddess.
They said she would guide the desperate to the Haven. Floods could drown the earth, but Haven lay in the heavens, far beyond the reach of water.
Yang Yishen had never believed in gods or spirits. But when he looked into their eyes, he saw a feverish light, like people staring straight at their last way out.
With nowhere left to go, and nothing left to lose, he hardened his heart. If believing this lie would keep him alive, then so be it. And so he followed them onward.

zh:
姜隗找到那群人的时候，是个雨夜。
鲜血很快染红了大片的土地。但他已无法停下。直到一只细嫩泛白的手拉住了他的衣摆。
他回头，大雨中，那女子的脸几乎与他阿姐的脸重叠。
“光杀了他们，没用的。”那身穿大红嫁衣的女子奄奄一息，“还有很多，很多像他们这样的人。也还有很多，很多像我们这样的人。”
姜隗弯腰蹲下，擦去那女子脸上的血污，动作几近温柔。
“没关系，他们这样的人，有多少，我便杀多少。“
”你们这样的人，有多少，我便救多少。”
en:
It was a rainy night when Jiang Kui found them. 
Blood quickly soaked the earth. But he couldn't stop. Not until a pale, delicate hand tugged at the hem of his robe. 
He turned back. In the downpour, the woman's face overlapped so perfectly with his sister's. 
"Killing them... isn't enough," she whispered, barely clinging to life in her crimson wedding gown.
"There are so many more like them. And so many more like us." 
Jiang Kui knelt beside her. Gently, almost tenderly, he wiped the blood from her face. 
"It's alright," he said.
"For every one of them, I will kill them. 
And for every one of you... I will save you."

zh:
温无缺是被低低的诵经声吵醒的。
身体的疼痛先于记忆的碎片从五脏六腑涌了出来，她咬紧牙齿，她知道来自记忆的痛苦将更难承受。
未央城的倒戈，温无痕的大笑，经脉震断之痛，母亲挡住那些人时身体喷涌出的鲜血……
至于怎么逃出未央城的，她已经记不太清了。她的脑中一片空白，只有一个清晰的声音——活下来，绝不可以辜负母亲。

她卖力睁开眼睛，这是一个破旧至极的屋子，屋里有一个头发花白的老太太，她跪在那里，求满天神佛能救救她的女儿。
老太太的声音卑微而恳切，她默默地听着，就好像在穿越时间倾听母亲从未对她说过的那些话，直到泪水打湿了枕席。

老太太听到她醒了，忙往这边扑来，跪久了的腿哪支撑得了这一扑，她登时跪在地上，最后是连滚带爬地来到了床边。
“盈盈，俺的盈盈！是佛祖，是神仙！他们把你还给娘了。”
温无缺清醒地知道，生死之事，失去的便永远失去，哪有谁能被还来。
可这一刻她只想做盈盈，于是她安心倒在那位母亲的怀里。在那昏暗的房间中，她们就像两块破损的玉，却恰好嵌合在一起。
en:
Wen Wuque was roused by the low murmur of sutras. Pain surged from her internal organs before the fragments of memory could surface. She gritted her teeth, knowing the agony of recollection would be harder to bear.
The betrayal in Weiyang City, Wen Wuhen's mocking laughter, the searing pain of shattered meridians, the blood spraying from her mother's body as she shielded her daughter from attackers...She could barely recall how she'd escaped Weiyang City. Her mind was blank, save for one clear command: Survive. Do not fail your mother.

She forced her eyes open. A crumbling hut. A white-haired old woman on her knees, begging every god she knew to save her daughter. 
The words were humble, desperate, and for a moment, Wuque could almost pretend they came from her own mother, speaking all the love she'd never had time to say. Tears soaked the thin pillow.

Hearing her stir, the old woman lunged toward the bed, her knees too numb from kneeling to support her weight. She collapsed to the floor, crawling the rest of the way to Wen Wuque's side.
"Yingying, my Yingying! The Buddha has answered, they've returned you to me!"
Wen Wuque knew the finality of death: what is lost is lost forever. No one is "returned".
But in that moment, she wanted nothing more than to be Yingying. So she sank into the woman's embrace, two broken pieces of jade fitting perfectly together in the dim light.

Haohao is terrified of disappointment in his owner's eyes.
His owner teaches him to lie down. Haohao learns. His owner pats his head and says, "Good dog, good dog."
His owner teaches him to sit. Haohao learns. "Good dog, good dog."
Then his owner tries to teach him to beg, with paws up. Days pass. Nights pass. Haohao practices and practices, but he just can't get it.
As the rooster crows, Haohao looks nervously at his owner. His owner just pats his head, the same as always. "Good dog, good dog." Haohao's front paws are sore, but his tail wags furiously.
So this is it. Even without learning to beg, he is still his owner's good dog. He is so happy.

zh:
揉着隐隐作痛的额角，望着院里挤作一团的山民——不过七八个人，却嚷出了百来人的喧哗，叽叽喳喳，活像一树惊雀。
“甄大人，您可得给俺们做主啊！孩他爹三舅公那头的二姨夫，愣是把俺家下蛋的老母鸡给炖了！说赔俺一只木鸢，这都啥时候了，影儿都没有！”
——这是拿他当青天老爷告状来的。
“甄大人，这旧板子您咋说不要了吧？我家那屋头，山风呼呼往里灌，正缺块板子挡挡……”
——好嘛，这是来顺手牵羊的。
“甄大人，上回您帮抓的药不咋灵啊，您瞅俺这腿还瘸着——”
——得，这位更是连门都没找对。
“甄大人……”
山民的抱怨和诉求混杂在一起，总是一口气倒给甄贵。甄贵的手指敲着掉漆的木桌，嘴里嗯嗯啊啊地应付着，目光却早已溜出窗子，黏在了西沉的落日上。
三，二，一，甄贵在心里算着时辰。真没想到这人生都跌至荒郊野岭里，胸中热血凉了，却还掌握了望日读秒的能力，这怎么能不算一种塞翁失马呢？
落日藏进山后的瞬间，甄贵蹭地一下站起来，“日落了，今日下值了，诸位乡亲请回吧！诶，说你呢！那木板留下，上面‘解忧司’三个大字没瞧见吗？”
“借、油、肆？这名儿好啊，娃儿，回去让你娘不要摆弄什么油菜了，以后咱都上这儿借油来！”山民们嘟嘟囔囔的，带着满意的笑容离开了。

什么借油肆，真是没文化，明明是“解常人不能解之忧”的解忧司。甄贵爬上梯子，准备把这块从山民手里夺回来的牌匾重新钉上。
要是早知今日会窝憋在这山沟沟里，从前的自己何必那么拼命呢。错了，真是错了。
说什么不见山特别牙门缺个经验丰富的老手坐镇、说什么甄贵这人虽无机巧之能，但一心办案明察秋毫的本事正是这山野所需，结果呢？案子呢？这里事小活又多，人财皆不俱，连这牌子都得亲自写。
这儿的人吧……也不太爱讲道理。
不管他强调多少遍，他们仍一口一个“大人”喊着。
仿佛他真是个什么了不得的人物，而不是那个因为对某桩大案过于深入被各路针对，为了保命不得不改名换姓、背井离乡的中年捕头。
讽刺得很啊，他曾替多少人鸣不平，如今自个儿的冤屈只能埋在心底。罢了罢了，要不是后来被某人引荐进不见山，估计现在早就身首异处了。想到这，甄贵一走神，木板上没磨平的毛刺猝不及防扎进食指，隐隐生疼。
不碰了，以后都不碰了！啥事情都不碰了！大事小事都不碰了！
甄贵恨恨地钉好这块木板。从今往后，他决心要和那些轻易放过自己的圆滑狗官一样——天塌下来有高个子顶着、鸡毛蒜皮的就随它去、至于剩下的麻烦事儿，没有啥是不能拖一拖，等着它自个儿拉倒的。
彪子！就这么办！劳累个半辈子，明天先睡它个三竿再说！

夜沉了，山风带着凉意。甄贵点上灯，举着手，正龇牙咧嘴地想把那根作祟的木刺挑出来，窗外却又响起一阵窸窸窣窣的动静。
他自然知道有人会来。哼，来这之后，就没有一个夜里消停过。大案要案是没有的，山民家常是唠不尽的，今晚不知道又要听谁家的陈年往事到几更。
推门一看，竟是两三个小孩推推搡搡、怯生生走上前来。
“大…大人，俺爹让送这个药油给您……下午他来的时候，看见您老是搓眉头，这个治头痛管用……”带头的是陈家的小儿子，声音比蚊子还细。
晚风拂过，送来药油清涩的草木香气，融进山间沉静的夜色中。
甄贵微微一怔，伸手接过那只粗陶瓶，转身回屋把油灯拿给了孩子们。
他站在门口，望着那一簇小小的光点摇摇晃晃，渐渐被夜色吞没。这时，耳边又传来几声鸟鸣。
甄贵抬起头，只见那残了一半的屋檐下，不知何时竟新筑了一个鸟巢，小小的，却扎实地偎在梁下。
哎，真是奇了，满腔热血明明已经凉了……
可此时此刻，心里怎么却又泛起另一种熟悉的、温暖的感觉呢？
好吧，这解忧司再待几天也成，就几天。
en:
Rubbing his throbbing temples, Zhen Gui surveyed the villagers crowding his yard. There were barely eight of them, yet they kicked up a racket fit for a hundred, chirping and squawking like a flock of startled sparrows.

"Lord Zhen, you gotta give us justice! My husband's third-uncle-in-law's second-cousin-twice-removed... well, that man went and stewed my best laying hen! Said he'd pay me back with a wooden eagle, but I haven't seen a splinter of it!" 
They were treating him like some legendary magistrate, coming to him to settle their petty squabbles.

"Lord Zhen, you said you were done with this old plank, right? The wind is howling right through my shack, and I desperately need a patch..." 
Wonderful. This one was just here to scavenge.

"Lord Zhen, that medicine you helped me get last time didn't work so well. Look, my leg is still limping!" 
Great. This one was at the wrong door entirely.

The villagers' complaints and pleas poured out in a chaotic, endless stream. Zhen Gui's fingers tapped an idle rhythm on the peeling wooden table. He grunted the occasional hum to keep them going, but his gaze had long since slipped out the window, glued to the setting sun.

Three, two, one. Zhen Gui counted the heartbeats in his head. 
Who would have thought his life would tumble into this godforsaken wilderness? His old passion had cooled to ash, leaving him with nothing but the strange talent of counting sunsets down to the second. Surely, that counted as a blessing in disguise.

The moment the sun dipped behind the mountain, Zhen Gui sprang to his feet. "Sun's down! I'm officially off the clock. Go on home, folks! Hey, you! Leave that plank alone! Can't you see the characters for 'Bureau of Relief' carved right there?"
"Bureau of Beef? Now that's a fine name! Lad, go tell your mother to stop messing with that ox. We'll just come here to borrow our beef from now on!" The villagers mumbled, wandering off with satisfied grins.

Bureau of Beef? What absolute nonsense. It was the Bureau of Relief, a place meant to solve the troubles that ordinary people could not. Zhen Gui climbed up a ladder, preparing to nail the wooden sign he had just snatched back from the villager.

If he had known he would end up rotting in this mountain crevice, why did his younger self ever work so hard? It was a mistake. A huge mistake. 

All that talk about how the Special Office of Hidden Mountain needed a seasoned veteran to hold the fort. They told him that although Zhen Gui lacked mechanical ingenuity, his keen eye for detail and relentless pursuit of the truth were exactly what these wilds required. And where were the cases? Just endless trivial chores and zero resources. No manpower, no funding. He even had to carve the signboard himself.
And the people here... they simply lacked any sense of reason.

No matter how many times he corrected them, they still called him "Lord" as if he were truly some high dignitary. In reality, he was just a middle-aged head constable who had dug too deep into a major case, made enemies everywhere, and was forced to change his name and flee just to keep his head attached to his neck.

What a cruel irony. He had spent his entire life seeking justice for others, yet his own grievances had to remain buried forever in his heart. Enough of that. Had a certain someone not recommended him to Hidden Mountain, his head would be hanging from a city gate by now. 

As his mind wandered, a stray splinter from the rough wood jabbed sharply into his index finger. A faint, throbbing ache followed.
I'm done with it! No more meddling! I won't lift a finger for anything ever again! Not the big cases, and certainly not the small ones!

Zhen Gui hammered the board home with a spiteful thud. From this day forth, he swore to be like those slippery, corrupt officials who never let a conscience trouble them. If the sky falls, let the tall men catch it. Let the petty trifles slide. As for the rest of the mess, if you stall long enough, it will simply rot away on its own. 
Smart! That was the way. Half a lifetime of exhaustion was more than enough. Tomorrow, he would sleep until the sun burned his backside!

...

Night fell, bringing a chill mountain breeze. With the lamp lit, Zhen Gui held up his hand, grimacing as he tried to pry out the offending splinter. Suddenly, a faint rustle stirred outside the window.
He knew someone was out there. He always knew. Hmph. Ever since he had crawled into this forgotten corner, he had not enjoyed a single night of peace. There were no grand cases here, only endless family drama. God knows whose ancient history he would have to endure until midnight this time.

He swung the door open, only to find a few children nudging and shoving one another, creeping forward with timid steps.

"L-Lord Zhen... my dad asked me to bring you this... medicine oil. He saw you rubbing your forehead this afternoon, and said this works great for headaches..." The boy at the front spoke in a voice smaller than a mosquito's.

A night breeze drifted past, carrying the raw, herbal scent of the oil into the quiet mountain darkness.
Zhen Gui froze. He reached out and accepted the crude earthenware bottle, then turned back inside to fetch his oil lamp for the children.

Standing at the threshold, he watched that tiny speck of light sway and bob until the vast night finally swallowed it whole. Right then, a few birds called out nearby.

Zhen Gui looked up. Beneath the crumbling edge of the eaves, a new nest had appeared. It was small, yet firmly nestled against the wooden beam.
Strange. He could have sworn the hot blood in his chest had long since turned to ash... 
Yet at this very moment, why did that old, familiar warmth come flooding back?

Fine. Perhaps he could tolerate this Bureau of Relief for a few more days. Just a few.

玩家的技能大多都可以以卸势应对，破防奇术不仅不会被卸势，在命中处于防御或在释放卸势技能的目标时，反而有更好的效果，但其可以被任意技能打断。

1.存活玩家数量更多的一方获胜；

en:
Participate in the 5v5 Arena to make friends through martial arts. In this 5v5 competitive mode, players can form teams of five to engage in strategic battles.
 5v5 Arena is open daily, with entry available from 19:45 to 20:00. Be sure to join in on time.
 Once the match begins, up to four teams with similar ranking points will be grouped into a round-robin bracket. Each group will play three matches, with each match using a best-of-three format. Teams that win a match will earn season points and Activity Points.

 In this mode, healing effects are reduced by 70%. After a certain time in battle, players will deal increased damage while the healing effect is further reduced. Using Deflect consumes Endurance, while finishing Execute restores Endurance.

 Most player skills can be deflected. Defense-breaking Mystic Skills not only ignore deflect but also deal enhanced effects when hitting targets who are defending or deflecting. However, these Mystic Skills can be interrupted by any skill. Player skills, including Mystic Skills and Charged Skill, can interrupt Light and Heavy Attacks, but not vice versa. Effective use of Control-breaking Skills can turn the tide. The side that defeats all opponents first within the time limit wins. If the timer runs out without a decisive outcome, the winner is determined by the following priorities: 1. The side with more surviving players wins; 2. If the number of surviving players is equal, the side with the higher total damage dealt wins; 3. If the total damage dealt is equal, the side with the higher total healing amount wins.

zh:
汉时，墨门避世，将金人躯体一同带入山中封存。数百年来，仍时有门人钻研这前人伟业，或有所得，或撼心神。
距金人铸成，已有千年，技艺又有多少进益？一望墨者前路，竟如暗夜，不见星火。
今之飞天城，不恰如往昔之金人？本为铸太平器，或终效帝王家，做瞻仰奇物，徒为祸苍生。
若无可救，何必自守山中，皓首穷技？可若不守山中，又该去何处？
墨者一途，有何可用处？
en:
During the Han dynasty, the Mohist Sect withdrew from the world, taking the chassis of the Golden Colossus into the mountains to be sealed away. For centuries, disciples have continued to study this monumental achievement of their predecessors. Some gain fleeting enlightenment, while others find their minds entirely shaken.
A thousand years have passed since the Colossus was first forged, but how much has their craft truly advanced? Looking ahead, the path of the Mohists seems like a dark night devoid of a single spark.
Is today's Skyward City not exactly like the Colossi of the past? They were originally forged as instruments of peace, only to ultimately serve imperial ambitions or become mechanical marvels for the elite to admire, bringing nothing but disaster to the common folk.
If the world is beyond saving, why stubbornly guard the mountains and exhaust one's entire life mastering a skill? But if they do not guard the mountains, where else can they possibly go? 
On this path of the Mohist, what true purpose is left to serve?

zh:
古之诲蒙者，多授以书。然山川风物之趣，非书所能尽。郦道元注水经，必躬涉江河；陆鸿渐著茶经，遍尝天下之泉。盖耳目所亲，胜于纸上百倍，此自昔而然者也。
有朋自远方来，笔者念其年少初至，举目皆生，湖山虽近在咫尺，亦同隔岸，徒令佳景空老，岂不可惜？故笔者夜取闲纸，篝灯而录。
所记非经非史，惟平生行湖所见，其难言者，则留与其自往验之——盖江南光景，须亲临乃知，非言语所能代。
en:
In ancient times, teachers often taught the young from books. Yet the delights of mountains, rivers, and local wonders cannot be fully captured on paper. When Li Daoyuan annotated the Water Classic, he journeyed the rivers himself; when Lu Hongjian composed the Classic of Tea, he tasted every spring beneath the heavens. What you see and hear yourself is worth a hundred pages; it has always been so.
A friend has come from afar, and everything is strange to his eyes. The lakes and mountains sit at his door, yet may as well be on distant shores. It would be a shame to let such views grow old unseen. So I took up spare paper by lamplight and wrote this down.
I record neither classic nor history, only what I have seen on the lake in a lifetime. Where words fail, I leave for him to see for himself, for the beauty of Jiangnan must be lived, not merely read.

zh:
群策共有#Y三人/四人/五人#E三种模式，少侠可以直接匹配或组成队伍进行匹配，三种模式均为#Y3局2胜制#E，共享积分段位。

「第一局」特殊2v2：
每队需要#Y2名#E玩家上阵，分别进行#Y1v1#E比赛，若2场比赛获胜者来自同一队伍，则该队伍获得第一局胜利；若2场比赛获胜者来自不同队伍，则2名胜者需以#Y当前状态#E进行对决，获胜方队伍获得第一局胜利；若1v1比赛倒计时结束时有未分出胜负的比赛，则场上所有幸存玩家需以当前状态进行对决，获胜方队伍获得第一局胜利

「第二局」3v3/5v5
三人/四人模式下，每队需要#Y3名#E玩家准备，进行#Y3v3#E比赛，获胜方队伍获得第二局胜利
五人模式下，每队需要#Y5名#E玩家准备，进行#Y5v5#E比赛，获胜方队伍获得第二局胜利

「第三局」1v1
每队需要#Y1名#E玩家准备，进行#Y1v1#E比赛，该玩家与第一局的2名玩家#Y不能重复#E

群策玩法中少侠的战斗属性将进行部分调平（角色自身装备套装/调律/定音效果生效；真气、精元、耐力均为满值，武学等级为100级，奇术为六重35段，心法为六重，止戈天赋除自选属性外全部点亮。食物和符帖效果在玩法中不生效。其中若少侠已经领悟奇术变招，则对局中的奇术效果将与对局外设置保持一致；若尚未领悟，则可在奇术培养界面设置是否试用奇术变招。）。少侠可以直接匹配或组队进行匹配。群策第一、三场对局中，玩家造成的治疗效果将降低70%，对目标的气血护盾造成的伤害提升100%，箭矢使用上限为20支，进入战斗一段时间后，玩家伤害将获得提升。群策第二场对局中，少侠可以复活队友，但玩家造成的治疗效果将降低70%。箭矢使用上限为20支。

玩家的技能大多都可以以卸势应对，破防奇术不仅不会被卸势，在命中处于防御或在释放卸势技能的目标时，反而有更好的效果，但其可以被任意技能打断。玩法中释放卸势会消耗耐力，而处决命中时会回复耐力。

玩家的各类技能（包括奇术和蓄力技）能够打断轻重击，而反过来则不行。解控技能清风霁月可在受击或控制状态下使用，活用可以有效扭转劣势。

移动端与PC端为独立的匹配池。组队参与玩法时，匹配逻辑遵循以下规则：系统将检测队伍内所有成员的设备类型。一旦检测到存在PC端设备，该队伍会被纳入PC端匹配队列。若玩家在移动端匹配成功后出现跨平台顶号等异常行为，则该玩家后续匹配被归入PC端队列。

在限定时间内，率先击败对方全部玩家的一方获胜，若倒计时结束未分胜负，按以下优先级依次判定：
1.存活玩家数量更多的一方获胜；
2.若存活玩家数量相同，则总伤害量更高一方获胜；
3.若总伤害量相同，则总治疗量更高一方获胜。
en:
Group Strategy features three modes: #Y3-Player, 4-Player, and 5-Player#E. Wanderers can match directly or form a team to match. All three modes are #YBest of 3#E and share the same points and rank.

[Round 1] Special 2v2:
Each team fields #Y2#E players for separate #Y1v1#E matches. If both winners are from the same team, that team wins Round 1. If the winners are from different teams, the 2 winners duel in their current state, and the winning team takes Round 1. If a 1v1 match ends in a draw when time runs out, all surviving players on the field duel in their #Ycurrent state#E, and the winning team takes Round 1.

[Round 2] 3v3/5v5:
In 3-Player/4-Player modes, #Y3#E players per team prepare for a #Y3v3#E match. The winning team takes Round 2.
In 5-Player mode, #Y5#E players per team prepare for a #Y5v5#E match. The winning team takes Round 2.

[Round 3] 1v1:
Each team fields #Y1#E player for a #Y1v1#E match. This player #Ycannot be one of the two who fought in Round 1#E.

In Group Strategy, Wanderers' combat attributes are partially balanced (character's own Gear Set, Tuning, and Attuning Effects remain active; Qi, Vitality, and Endurance are maxed; Martial Arts Level is set to 100; Mystic Skills are Tier 6, Stage 35; Inner Ways are Tier 6; Arena Talents are fully unlocked except for custom attributes). Wanderers can match directly or in teams. If Mystic Skill Variations are already unlocked, the in-match effects match the out-of-match effects; if not unlocked, Mystic Skills use the default effect. In Rounds 1 and 3, Healing dealt is reduced by 70%, damage to HP Shields is increased by 100%, arrows are capped at 20, and damage increases after a certain duration in combat. In Round 2, Wanderers can revive teammates, but Healing dealt is reduced by 70%. Arrows are capped at 20.

Most player skills can be countered by Deflect. Defense-breaking Mystic Skills cannot be Deflected and are more effective against targets who are defending or using Deflect, but they can be interrupted by any skill. Using Deflect consumes Endurance, while landing an execution hit restores Endurance.

Player skills (including Mystic Skills and Charged Skills) can interrupt Light and Heavy Attacks, but not vice versa. The break control skill, Serene Breeze, can be used while being staggered or controlled; use it wisely to turn the tide.

Mobile and PC platforms have separate matchmaking pools. When participating as a team, the system checks the device types of all members. If a PC device is detected, the team is placed in the PC matchmaking queue. If a player exhibits cross-platform login behavior after a successful match on mobile, their subsequent matches will be assigned to the PC queue.

The first side to defeat all opposing players within the time limit wins. If the countdown ends without a winner, the result is determined by the following priority:

1. The side with more surviving players wins.
2. If the number of survivors is equal, the side with higher Total Damage wins.
3. If Total Damage is equal, the side with higher Total Healing wins.

zh:
选手须遵守《燕云十六声》通用赛事规则，详见燕云十六声官网赛事中心【通用赛事规则】一栏。

「风雷赛」采用调平模式，游侠与首领的属性（首领气血除外）与「试炼」鬼神愁难度一致，武学、心法、奇术可在挑战前自由搭配，挑战开始后可在准备阶段切换武学搭配和天工开物。

海选赛中选手需依次挑战3名指定首领（「皮影·幕起」「无名将军」「伊刀」），每名首领拥有3次挑战机会，完成当前首领全部挑战后，方可解锁下一名首领，并以3次挑战中的最短用时作为其最优成绩；该最优成绩所使用的武学组合将被锁定，禁止在后续首领挑战中重复使用。总成绩为三名首领最优成绩的用时之和，选手可通过「试炼」玩法进行训练。

淘汰赛中选手需连续挑战三名固定首领（淘汰赛为「皮影·幕起」「无名将军」「伊刀」），单次挑战内血量与药品数量全程继承不重置，且不同首领需使用完全不同的武学（仅单次挑战内限制），每个首领准备阶段可通过培养和背包切换武学及天工开物，完成准备后会自动传送开始战斗，共3次挑战机会，最终取最短用时作为成绩。

决赛的挑战规则同淘汰赛，最后一名首领决赛当日公布。
en:
Players must abide by the Where Winds Meet General Tournament Rules. See the "General Tournament Rules" section on the official Where Winds Meet Tournament Center website. 

The "Tempest" uses a balanced mode. Attributes for Wanderers and Bosses (excluding Boss HP) match the "Trial" Abyss difficulty. Martial Arts, Inner Ways, and Mystic Skills can be freely configured before the challenge. After the challenge starts, you can switch Martial Arts and Divinecraft during the preparation phase. 

In the Qualifiers, players must challenge 3 designated Bosses in order ("Puppeteer - Overture", "General Nameless", "Yi Dao"). Each Boss has 3 challenge attempts. You can only unlock the next Boss after completing the challenge for the current one. The shortest time among the 3 attempts is recorded as the best result; the Martial Arts combination used for this best result will be locked and cannot be reused in subsequent Boss challenges. The total score is the sum of the best times for all three Bosses. Players can train via the "Trial" mode. 

In the Elimination Stage, players must consecutively challenge three fixed Bosses (Elimination Bosses: "Puppeteer - Overture", "General Nameless", "Yi Dao"). HP and medicine counts are inherited throughout the single run and do not reset. Completely different Martial Arts must be used for different Bosses (restriction applies only within a single run). Martial Arts and Divinecraft can be switched via Training and Bag during each Boss's preparation phase. Combat starts automatically after preparation. There are 3 challenge attempts, with the shortest total time taken as the final score. 

The Finals follow the same rules as the Elimination Stage. The final Boss will be announced on the day of the Finals.
Junjiang Yun

第四，也是最重要的一点！你很富有，这些年你偷偷藏了很多宝贝，要是都忘了，那你的头就会更疼啦。
所以，赶快去看看你的宝贝吧。它们就在#Y风车之上、倒悬之底、七色之畔#E。

Hey, Xiaoba!
If you're reading this, it means you still remember how to read. Good for you! Or maybe you're just curious why there's a big smiling clock on this page. That makes sense too. Curiosity suits you.
But there are four things you absolutely can't forget.
First: You're incredible. Not everyone can prance around with a copper pate and so much pluck!
Second, you love the Bell Toller, Little Xiaoba. Make sure to take him out to soak up the sun in the sea of flowers every day.
Third, you're lucky. If it weren't for those three masters, you wouldn't be here. Be grateful.
And fourth, the most important, you're rich. You've secretly gathered many treasures over the years. Forgetting them? That'll only give you a bigger headache.
So go check your treasures. They're waiting #Yabove the windmill, beneath the Overturned House, and by the Seven-Hued Plain#E.

zh:
那一日的天色倒是好，屋内窗户半开，院内有些风，甚至有点鸟叫。

沈玉将那笛子放在桌上，抬起头，面前的铜镜与她对视。
她头一次这般仔细地打量自己。
她看向铜镜里的那张脸，她看向那张脸上，多年以来无法改变的笑容，恍惚记起十二岁那年的池面。
此刻，她手中并无石子。

于是，她安静地抬了抬手，砸碎铜镜，等待着即将响起的脚步声。
她看见许多人被响声惊动，匆匆忙忙跑进屋内，他们的声音嘈杂，询问着发生了何事，但那些很近很近的声音，在那一刻，却似乎离沈玉很远很远。

沈玉没有回应，只是盯着那一片一片的镜面。
镜面之中，虚假的笑容四分五裂，连同她自己的倒影，连同过去的自己。
她听见一个很近很近的声音。
那是过去的沈玉在她耳边呢喃——若见到我让你如此痛苦，那愿你我，他日不重逢。

她抬起头，终于听见她们诧异地询问那放置在桌面上的笛子。
她抬起头，先看向那笛子，语调平静：“叫爹爹来吧。”

“就说今日，我有一个故事，要告诉他。”
en:
The sky that day was surprisingly clear. The window in the room was half open.
There was a breeze in the courtyard—
even a few birdsong notes.

Shen Yu placed the flute gently on the table. Then she looked up, meeting the gaze of the bronze mirror before her.

For the first time, she truly studied her own reflection.

She looked at the face in the mirror—
and at the smile she had worn for so many years, unchanged. She recalled the surface of the pond when she was twelve.

But this time, there was no stone in her hand.

So, in silence, she lifted her arm—
and shattered the mirror. Then waited for the sound of footsteps.

She saw people come rushing in, startled by the noise, their voices loud, cluttered, questioning what had happened. But in that moment, those voices were so close yet they felt distant. Very, very distant.

Shen Yu said nothing. She simply stared at the shards of glass. In those fragments,
the false smile had broken into pieces—
along with her reflection, along with the girl she used to be.

Then she heard a voice, very close.

It was the old Shen Yu, whispering in her ear: 

"If seeing me brings you this much pain, then may you and I never meet again."

She raised her head and heard them asking about the flute resting on the table.
She raised her head again, looked at it calmly, and said,

"Tell Father to come."

"Tell him that today, I have a story to tell."

说到烤肉品鉴，肉肉很有发言权。曾有两个人类把烤肉摆在它面前，它抖抖胡子嗅闻片刻，伸出爪子抓走其中一块，有人笑了，有人垂头丧气。它只觉得烤肉好吃，吃得满脸油光发亮。
前几天暴雨夜，它团在石堆下睡觉，尾巴规规矩矩收拢，免得被雨水打湿皮毛。忽然有人类带着两串烤肉来找它，给它闻了闻有猫味的东西，满脸焦急。
它懂了，又有猫跑丢了。这些有家的猫总想当野猫，是该狠揍一顿。
它拎着猫回来，人类很高兴，撑伞回家了。它舔舔嘴角烤肉余香，缩回石堆底下睡觉。
希望梦里永远是晴天和烤肉。
en:
Chubby considered herself the village's most capable cat. Sure, she could catch mice like any house cat, but she could also judge a barbecue competition and, for a fee of one lightly salted grilled skewer, find lost cats.
Her palate was legendary. She once settled a bet between two men by choosing the superior piece of meat with a single, decisive paw.
One night, during a rainstorm, she was curled under a rock when a frantic human appeared with two fragrant skewers and a piece of cloth that smelled of another cat.
She understood: another cat had run off. These house cats always wanted to be strays; they deserved a good scolding.
The human was overjoyed and walked off under his umbrella. She licked the last of the grilled meat from her whiskers and curled back up, hoping her dreams would always be this sunny and delicious.

zh: 参照《敦煌曲谱》第3首《倾杯乐》。《敦煌曲谱》原藏于莫高窟藏经洞，其正面为《长兴四年中兴殿应圣节讲经文》，背面即为抄录的25首曲谱。一般认为是琵琶谱，抄写时期为晚唐至五代。它采用半字符号记写，被称为燕乐半字谱，因古奥难识，有“音乐天书”之誉。该乐谱于1908年被法国汉学家伯希和从敦煌藏经洞带走，现收藏在法国国家图书馆，编号为P.3808。
en: Refer to Pouring out the Cup, the 3rd piece in the Dunhuang Music Score. The Dunhuang Melody Scroll was originally housed in the Sutra Cave of the Mogao Grottoes. Its front side bears the Sermon for the Sacred Festival at the Zhongxing Hall in the Fourth Year of Changxing, while the reverse side contains transcriptions of 25 melody scrolls. Generally believed to be a pipa score, it dates to the late Tang or Five Dynasties period. The notation system used is a semi-symbolic script known as semi-character notation of Yan's Melody, famed for its enigmatic nature, earning it the nickname "the gobbledy-gook of music." The scroll was taken from Dunhuang by French sinologist Paul Pelliot in 1908 and is now held in the Bibliothèque nationale de France, catalogued as P.3808.

文津馆立于青州，以藏书研学为务。馆藏万卷，涉猎百家；承先儒之遗绪，续往圣之绝学。自春秋以降，文脉相承，未尝断绝。
又有古寺，隐于枣林深处，晨钟暮鼓，梵音时闻；有涌泉，蜿蜒石砌之间，清冽如鉴，石罅泠泠。东望沧海，洪波涌日，偶见白鸥数点，出没空蒙。南眺岱岳，苍崖摩云，叠巘积翠，朝岚夕霭，瞬息万变。
四时风物，蔚为可观，而尤以今朝为最。山色正佳，诸君何妨往青州一行？登岱宗而观日，访古寺而采枣，赏涌泉而食鲤，拏扁舟而望潮。坐卧随心，兴尽而返，不亦快哉！
又，泰山脚下一饺馆，酉时开肆，味佳。诸君若至，可往一尝。
en:
Let this winged messenger bring tidings to all: The Inkbound Order shall open its doors to welcome wanderers from every sect and embrace the brightest minds across the realm.
Nestled in Qingzhou, the Inkbound Order is a sanctuary of scholarship and a guardian of ancient texts. Its halls hold tens of thousands of scrolls spanning every school of thought, preserving the profound wisdom of the ancient sages. Here, the fires of our cultural heritage have burned unbroken since antiquity.
Hidden deep within a tranquil jujube grove rests an ancient temple. Listen closely, and you will hear the chime of morning bells, the beat of evening drums, and the faint chanting of sutras. Crystal springs weave through the rocks, clear as glass, singing a silvery tune. Cast your gaze eastward to the boundless sea, where sunlit swells rise and white gulls dart through the hazy horizon. Look to the south, and the majestic peaks of Mount Tai pierce the heavens, an endless sweep of emerald cliffs where the morning mists and twilight clouds shift in a breathtaking dance.
Though Qingzhou is beautiful in all four seasons, its splendor is most radiant today. With the mountains bathed in such glorious light, why not make the journey? Ascend Mount Tai to greet the sunrise, wander the ancient temple to gather sweet jujubes, linger by the springs while savoring fresh carp, or take a skiff out to ride the ocean tide. Walk when you wish, rest when you please, and let your heart be entirely free. Is that not the truest delight?
One last thing. At the foot of Mount Tai sits a dumpling house. They open their doors at You Hour, and the fare is truly divine. Should your travels bring you near, pull up a chair and tuck in.

银婆婆从前是十八里乡间最受欢迎的小娘子。
她那一双好手啊，穿针引线，只消半晌，便能化腐朽为神奇，化敝屣为珍宝。
但后来，贼人打进了城。城没了，家没了，人也没了。而没了人，她那副好手艺，自然也就派不上用场了。

但她不甘心，总想给自己寻些事情做。后来，还真叫她寻着了。
人活着，求个体面。人死了，也想求个全尸。
而她那双手啊，穿针引线，只消半晌，便能将那些断肢残体，缝合到一块去，缝合出，一个与生前无异的人样来。

再后来，战乱平息，那些伤痛被隐于暗中。但她的恨意，却无从平复。
她成了江湖上最令人畏惧的缝衣娘。
起先是那些在战乱中逃走的贼寇，后来是那些在战中趁乱作恶的歹人，再后来，所有行凶者，都成了她的针下亡人。
她将他们一寸寸撕裂，又一寸寸缝合。她要重塑他们，重塑他们的人样，也试图重塑他们腐烂的内心。
但薛丑拦住了她。再怎么缝补，恶还是恶，善也回不到从前。他不希望银婆婆在扭曲的恨意中将自己丢了。

银婆婆于是成了鬼市子一家衣裳铺子里的缝衣娘。
她的头发都已花白，她那一双好手啊，也已开始发颤。
但她穿针引线，又开始化腐朽为神奇，化敝屣为珍宝了。
en:
Grannie Yin had once been the most beloved young woman in the nearby villages.
Her skilled hands worked magic with needle and thread, turning rags to riches, scraps to treasures in mere moments.
But then the bandits stormed the city. Homes fell, lives were lost, and with no one left to tailor for, her talents seemed wasted.

Yet she refused to yield, determined to find purpose. And she did.
The living crave dignity. The dead deserve wholeness.
And those same hands, once skilled with silk, now stitched severed limbs back together, reconstructing faces until they looked almost alive.

When the wars ended, wounds were buried, but her hatred festered.
She became the jianghu's most feared seamstress. 
First, the bandits who had fled justice. Then the opportunists who had thrived in chaos. Finally, anyone who harmed the innocent became fabric for her needle.
She'd tear them apart, stitch them back together, remaking their bodies and hoping to mend their rotten souls.
But Xue Chou stopped her. No amount of stitching can turn evil to good, or revive the past. He feared she'd lose herself in vengeance.

So Grannie Yin became a seamstress once more, this time in a shop in the Ghostlight Market.
Her hair had gone white. Her legendary hands now trembled.
Yet with needle in hand, she still works wonders, breathing new life into decay, transforming dross to delight.

zh: 武威市磨嘴子汉墓出土。木俑为松木雕成。为两位跪坐对局的老者形象。二位老者间设二层台棋盘，棋盘面上以黑色作底，白线勾格。局旁的空余盘面为掷骰之枰。二俑均梳椎髻，身着右衽交领长袍。面部及双手敷白粉，其上墨绘五官、髭和髻发。俑身以灰色作底，绘白色粗线条以章服饰，领、襟、袖口施以重墨。二俑手势略有不同，一俑右手放膝上，左手举于胸前；另一俑右臂向前下伸，握一筹。两位老者神情凝滞，蓄势待发，正在针锋相对的对弈之中。这件六博俑情趣盎然，以简中有繁渲染出一派蓄势待发的搏杀氛围，是汉代木雕艺术中的精品之作。
en: Unearthed from the Han Dynasty tomb at Mozuizi in Wuwei City. The wooden figurines are carved from pine wood, depicting two elderly men kneeling and playing a board game. A two-tiered chessboard is placed between them, with a black base and white lines forming grids on the surface. The remaining space beside the chessboard is used for rolling dice. Both figurines wear cone-shaped buns and cross-collar robes with right-side closures. Their faces and hands are painted white, with facial features, beards, and hair painted in black. The bodies are painted gray with thick white lines outlining the costumes, and the collars, lapels, and cuffs are painted with heavy black ink. Their gestures are slightly different, one places his right hand on his knee and raises his left hand to his chest; the other stretches his right arm forward and downward, holding a game piece. The two elderly men have focused expressions, ready for action, engaged in an intense chess match. This six-player chess figurine is full of charm, creating an atmosphere of imminent competition through simple yet intricate details, and is a masterpiece of Han Dynasty wood carving art.

1. Card Types
#Y· Gab Cards#E
#YBasic cards#E that transform into barrages when played and fly toward the opponent. Breaking through enemy barrages' defense damages Inner Bastions.
#Y· Quip Cards#E
#YSpell cards#E that activate instantly. They can Silence the opponent, reduce Inspiration Point costs, or copy barrages to control the board.
#Y· Maxim Cards#E
#YPowerful cards#E that you can bring up to 3 per battle. Each provides a persistent, potent aura but can only be used once per match. Play them at the perfect moment!

#Y· The Hidden Channel (Detour)#E
When Gab Cards clash, they can detour to an adjacent lane and continue forward. Each successful detour further boosts their attack.
#Y· Chatterbox (Fluff Card)#E
When Gab Cards are destroyed in a clash, they leave behind Fluff Cards in their lane, piling up as a shield in front of your Inner Bastions.
#Y· Play the Field#E
Place Gab Cards in certain lanes for an extra attack bonus.
#Y· Heartrend#E

zh:
大辽会同九年 十二月
大辽起兵伐晋……过孟津浮桥……直取开封。今日，我偶得一鼠，颇有灵性，似能懂人语……

大辽会同十年 正月
汉人的年节，多是亲人相聚，宴饮一番。不过今年，汉人和我们都没有过节的兴致。他们的亲人在底下，我们的亲人在北边。
还好，有阿灰陪着我……也算是一个年节。

大辽会同十年 三月
城里的热闹，同我们城外不同。老大说，守住天上来就是守住回家的路。可……大汗已经把这当做了家，我们还能回去么……
阿灰……这里是你的家，你愿意和我回我的家么。

大辽会同十年 四月
汉地的天气……慢慢热起来……天上来的汉人越来越多。汉人……是从庄稼地里种出来的么，怎么杀也杀不完。
我好累……阿灰……我想回家。

大辽会同十年 五月
最近的黄河……瓠子堤常常有奇怪的声音……
九流门和龙蛟帮那么难缠，大汉怎么还没让我们走？
张家人不可信，万一……黄河……
阿灰……我们还怎么回家？

大辽会同十年 六月 
水！水！张家人！
大家都……
阿灰，快走！
en:
December, the Ninth Year of the Huitong Era, Great Liao
The army has crossed the Mengjin Floating Bridge, heading for Kaifeng. Caught a strange mouse today—it almost seemed to understand me.

Zhengyue, the Tenth Year of the Huitong Era, Great Liao
The Han people's New Year feels hollow—both sides mourning lost loved ones. At least Hui's here; that makes it bearable.

March, the Tenth Year of the Huitong Era, Great Liao
City's chaos feels different from the countryside. The leader said, "Holding Heavenfall is holding the way home." But the Khitans have settled here. Can we still return? Hui, this is your home now. Will you come with me?

April, the Tenth Year of the Huitong Era, Great Liao
The Han keep coming as if they grow from the fields. No matter how many we kill, they never stop. I'm exhausted. Hui, I want to go home.

May, the Tenth Year of the Huitong Era, Great Liao
Strange noises near the Yellow River dike... The Nine Mortal Ways and Dragon Hall cause trouble. Why haven't the Han forced us out? The Zhang family's untrustworthy... What if the river... Hui, how will we ever get home?

June, the Tenth Year of the Huitong Era, Great Liao
Water! Water! The Zhang family! Everyone's... Hui, run—now!
Oh? And why is that?

en:
To General Wang,

I, Zhao Tie, a commoner of Luancheng, take the liberty of writing to you, for I have one humble request.
My son Buyi is twelve this year. Since childhood, he has admired the General's bearing. He often carves wooden swords and drills in the courtyard from morning till night, saying, "I will follow the General's example and bring peace to the realm." For several birthdays now, his dearest wish has been to see the General with his own eyes.
A child with such high aspirations fills me with both joy and shame. I rejoice in his spirit, yet am ashamed of my own poor circumstances, for I cannot help him travel far. Now that his birthday draws near, there is little I can do for him. And so, I humbly beg you to come to Luancheng and grant him this one wish.

zh:
一方无名的灵牌，静静置于树下。
那是她离宫之时从宫中偷偷带出的陪嫁之物，也是她无名的母亲最后存世的痕迹。

阿娘曾哼着歌谣，看着她在禁庭花苑中翩然起舞。
温柔而懦弱的宫妇只希望，自己的孩子能得佳偶，在皇都平安一生。

可她不愿成为温室中娇艳的牡丹。她想用自己的力量，去自己想去的地方盛开。
哪怕风摧霜欺，也要一次一次盛开。

她穿越了漫漫黄沙与风雪，她用自己的勇气和智慧安定了异邦。
若是母亲还在，想必也会安心，或是为自己骄傲吧。
可惜，母亲再也看不到了。
皎皎月夜，她提起裙摆，褪去钗环，于母亲的灵牌前跳起昔年的那支舞。
en:
A nameless spirit tablet rests quietly beneath a tree. 
It was part of her dowry, smuggled from the palace when she left—the last trace of her unnamed mother in this world. 

Her mother once hummed a song, watching her dance gracefully in the palace gardens. 
That gentle, timid palace woman only hoped her child would find a good match and live safely in the capital. 

But she refused to be a peony in a hothouse. She wanted to bloom where she chose, with her own strength. 
Even if wind and frost assailed her, she would bloom again and again. 

She crossed endless yellow sands and snowstorms, using courage and wisdom to bring stability to a foreign land. 
If her mother were still here, she would be at peace—or proud. 
But her mother would never see it. 
Under a bright moon, she lifted her skirts, removed her hairpins, and danced that childhood dance before her mother's spirit tablet.

zh:
周叔曾经以为自己的女儿周红线，是天上的文曲星下凡。
毕竟，谁家的孩子会像红线一样，梦里还喃喃不止，念叨着什么孔子老子、之乎者也？
周叔大喜过望，花重金二十文，买了鲜活小黄鱼两条，偷偷拎去给岑夫子，让他着重培养培养他家红线。
岑夫子看看鱼，又看看红线一窍不通的功课，纳了闷。

红线也很纳闷。爹爹突然在她身上，寄予了一大堆莫名其妙的期望。
话本子给换成了论语诗经，每日要比其他人更早半个时辰去学堂、和夫子大眼瞪小眼，连出去找老大玩的时间都被减了一半……
等到红线终于忍无可忍、大声哭诉之时，爹爹却很诧异：
你不是最爱这些吗？前几日、梦里，都还在背书呢。
红线猛然想起，那几日替又一次逃跑被抓的老大抄书的事情，住了口。

最后，周叔将这一事归结为梦中有鬼上身，找人给红线洒了三日符水，便算了结。
红线么，自然守口如瓶，将替老大抄书的事，藏做一个谁也不知道的秘密。
en:
Uncle Zhou once believed his daughter Zhou Ruby was the Literary Star descended from heaven.

After all, who else's child would mumble in their sleep, murmuring about Confucius, Laozi, and classical phrases?

Overjoyed, Uncle Zhou spent twenty valuable coins to buy two fresh yellow fish, secretly delivering them to Cen Fuzi and asking him to give special attention to his daughter.

Cen Fuzi looked at the fish, then at Ruby's utterly bewildering schoolwork, and was baffled.

Ruby was equally confused. Her father had suddenly placed strange expectations upon her.

Storybooks were replaced with the Analects and Classics of Poetry. She had to arrive at school half an hour earlier than others to stare awkwardly at the teacher, and her time for playing with the her elder cousin was cut in half...

When Ruby finally couldn't bear it anymore and cried out in protest, her father was surprised:

"Don't you love these texts? Just days ago, you were reciting them in your sleep."

Ruby suddenly remembered copying texts for her cousin, who had once again been caught trying to escape, and fell silent.

In the end, Uncle Zhou concluded that a ghost had possessed his daughter in her dreams. He had some Daoist sprinkle holy water on Ruby for three days, and considered the matter closed.

As for Ruby, she naturally kept quiet. The task of copying texts became a secret known to no one.

zh:
归望野小屋外，几位文津馆弟子正在讨论几座石狮子的来历。有人觉得那里是帝王陵墓的神道，有人说那不过是匠人炫技的雕饰，也有人相信那之下藏着失传的秘宝。见你到来，几位弟子纷纷围过来，七嘴八舌地说着自己的看法，并问你怎么看。……
#Y【是来日之约。】你相信这是画睛兄留下的约定。画睛兄说过，朋友就是在梦里也会相见。你想，这座狮子便是画睛兄的记号。——因为你就是他梦里的狮子。#E
听闻你所言，几位弟子面面相觑。他们挠挠头，半晌才开口说道，此处过去不过是一片荒野，如今赫然出现石狮子，或许是地气地脉异动；另一位则坚持认为此地有帝陵，那狮子便是引路标……见无人与你接话，你也只得暗自苦笑。你回头看了看那只最大石狮子，它依然安静地昂首迎风而立，岿然不动，千古如一。
en:
Outside the little hut at Homeward Wilds, several Inkbound Order disciples are in the middle of a lively debate over the origins of the stone lions. One is certain they once stood along the spirit way of an imperial tomb; another insists they are merely an artisan's flourish, nothing more than a display of skill; a third is convinced that some long-lost treasure must lie hidden beneath them. The moment they spot you, they crowd around at once, chattering over one another to offer their theories and ask what you think...
#Y[A promise of days to come.] You believe this is a promise left behind by Huajing. He once said that true friends will meet even in dreams. And so you think this lion is the mark he left behind because you are the lion in his dream.#E
At your answer, the disciples fall briefly silent and trade bewildered glances. They scratch their heads, and after a long pause, someone ventures that this place used to be nothing but wilderness, so perhaps the sudden appearance of the stone lions is due to some strange stirring in the earth's veins; another still refuses to yield, insisting there must be an imperial tomb here, with the lions marking the way... With no one quite able to follow your meaning, you can only let out a wry, inward smile. Turning back, you look once more at the largest stone lion. It still stands there quietly as ever, head lifted proudly into the wind, immovable, timeless, unchanged through the ages.

zh:
涌泉镇的人都知道，周家出了个神童。
三岁识字，五岁诵诗，七岁那年，诸葛先生随手翻开一页《尚书》，周怀民站起来背得一字不差。诸葛先生问他：“你读过多少书了？”周怀民挺直腰板，说：“蒙学馆藏书，已读十之七八。”诸葛先生笑道：“看来你已经可以当先生了。”同学们笑倒一片，起哄唤他“周先生”。他红着脸站在孩童中间，说不清是骄傲还是害羞。
既然成了同学们口里的先生，自然要有先生的样子。别的孩子下了课去追蝴蝶、斗蛐蛐、在庭院里疯跑。周怀民不去。他坐在凉亭里，捧着书卷，摇头晃脑地念：“克己复礼为仁。一日克己复礼，天下归仁焉。为仁由己，而由人乎哉？”
有学童跑来拉他去玩，他板着脸说：“玩物丧志，尔等可知这四字出自何处？”学童摇头。他便得意地背出《尚书》中的原文，还要逐字讲解。学童听得打哈欠，早跑远了。周怀民望着他们的背影，摇摇头，继续读书。人人都说，周怀民越来越有先生的样子了。
后来木先生整理学童的课业，无意中翻到周怀民的书卷。书页间夹着一张纸，上面画着一只九尾狐。那狐狸画得活灵活现，尾巴根根分明，旁边还用小字写着：“青丘之山，有兽焉，其状如狐而九尾。”
木先生把纸重新夹好，没有声张。
凉亭外那棵银杏树，叶子黄了又绿，绿了又黄。周怀民还是日日坐在那里读书，还是摇头晃脑，还是嫌同窗幼稚。只是他的书卷里，夹的纸越来越多了。
en:
Everyone in Wellspring Town knew the Zhou family had a prodigy on their hands.
He was recognizing characters by three and reciting poetry by five. When he was seven, Master Zhuge flipped to a random page in the Book of Documents. Zhou Huaimin stood up and recited it flawlessly, word for word. "Just how many books have you read?" Master Zhuge asked. Zhou Huaimin straightened his back. "I have read nearly eighty percent of the entire collection of the Primary Hall," he declared. Master Zhuge chuckled. "It seems you're ready to teach the class yourself." The room erupted into giggles, and his classmates began teasingly calling him "Master Zhou." Standing amidst the laughter with a flushed face, the boy couldn't quite tell if he was feeling proud or embarrassed.
But since he was now a "master" in their eyes, he felt obligated to look the part. While the other kids spent their free time chasing butterflies, battling crickets, or running wild in the courtyard, Zhou Huaimin stayed behind. He would sit alone in the pavilion, scroll in hand, swaying his head to a scholarly rhythm as he chanted the classics. "To subdue the self and return to propriety is perfect virtue. The world will recognize it, but the choice to be good belongs entirely to you."
Whenever a classmate tried to drag him out to play, Zhou would put on a stern face. "Frivolous play saps a man's ambition. Do you even know what book that proverb comes from?" When the boy shook his head, Zhou would smugly recite the original text, breaking it down word by word. Bored to tears, the classmate would quickly slip away. Zhou Huaimin would simply shake his head at their retreating backs and return to his reading. The adults all agreed: Zhou Huaimin was looking more like a proper master every day.
Then, one day, while organizing the students' coursework, Mr. Mu happened to unroll one of Zhou Huaimin's texts. A loose sheet of paper was tucked inside. On it was a vivid, lifelike sketch of a nine-tailed fox, every single tail drawn with painstaking care. Next to it, written in neat, tiny script, was a line from a book of myths: "Upon the Mountain of Qingqiu, there dwells a beast shaped like a fox, but with nine tails."
Mr. Mu quietly slipped the drawing back between the pages and kept the secret to himself.
Outside the pavilion, the leaves on the ginkgo tree turned from yellow to green, and back to yellow again. Day after day, Zhou Huaimin still sat there reading, still swaying his head to the rhythm of his chants, and still turning up his nose at the childishness of his peers. But as the seasons passed, the stack of secret drawings hidden inside his scrolls only grew thicker.

zh: 羽衣楼，地处开封城东，本潘楼之地。建隆三年，江南客省使翟如壁，奉江南国主之命，携金银珠玉、锦绣文绮入汴纳贡。因不堪驿馆清苦，遂置潘楼，以备下榻，易名羽衣楼。羽衣楼之业，广纳诸般江南布帛。其四色绫锦，绮丽妙曼、光华溢彩，与北地古雅之风迥异，一夕间风靡汴河两岸。汴京名流巨贾、诸国使节咸集于此。楼中清雅寂然，只见金纱掩映，香麝如云，隔牖风摇珠翠，临窗月映琉璃，如观玉台，如游阊阖。期间亦有弦歌曼妙，令人心神俱醉。
en: The Silken Veil Society stands east of Kaifeng, on the former site of Pan Tower. In the 3rd year of the Jianlong Reign (962 CE), Zhai Rubi, Commissioner of the Jiangnan Province, entered Bian (Kaifeng) to offer tributes—gold, jade, silks, and brocades—on behalf of the Jiangnan ruler. Displeased with the post station's harsh conditions, he refurbished Pan Tower as his residence, renaming it Silken Veil Society. The tower specialized in Jiangnan textiles, especially its four-color brocade—resplendent, iridescent, and wildly different from northern China's austere style. Overnight, it became the craze along the Bian River. Elites, merchants, and envoys from across the realm flocked here. Inside, golden gauze shimmered, musk scents swirled, and wind rustled pearl-adorned screens by latticed windows. Moonlight glazed the colored glass, creating an otherworldly atmosphere like a jade palace or the Heavenly Gate. Melodious music only deepened the enchantment.

zh: “吾家有狸奴，其名唤雪素。”雪素是某位郎君的猫，通体雪白，毛质细腻柔软，抚之如丝绸锦缎，因而得了这个雅致名字。主人家世代显贵，此猫也算得杭州城里生活最安逸的小猫之一。雪素不仅貌美，脾气也是顶好的，家中上下对这只猫儿都是极尽宠爱。雪素每日从专属的织金锦茵上醒来，爪边已有当日新鲜的鱼饭——喵？怎么今朝饭少了些？雪素有些疑惑，迈着优雅得体的猫步走到主人身边，蹭了蹭他的衣角。郎君面露愧色，半蹲下来摸了摸雪素毛茸茸的脑袋，又手法熟练地挠了挠它的下巴。“对勿住我们雪素，这两日手头吃紧，待吾友赚得了钱，想吃多少鱼饭都使得。”雪素呼噜呼噜抬起下巴，琉璃般的蓝眼睛认真望向自家主人，慢慢眨了眨，好像能听得懂一样。郎君自是不忍雪素吃一点苦头，站起身时已在盘算怎样补上猫餐的窟窿。猫儿天真、宽宏大量，只当是主人今朝打猎不尽如人意，冲着主人的背影喵喵两声以示理解，却不知接下来有段日子，鱼饭的分量都要少些下去了。
en: "In my house there dwells a cat, and Flurry is its name." Flurry belonged to a certain young gentleman, pure white from head to tail, its fur so fine and soft that to stroke it felt like touching silk brocade, and so it came by this elegant name. Its master's family had been persons of standing for generations, and this cat was counted among the most comfortably kept cats in all of Hangzhou. Not only was Flurry beautiful, its temperament, too, was also among the finest, and everyone in the household doted upon it without limit. Each day Flurry would wake upon its own gold-threaded brocade cushion, to find beside its paw a plate of fresh fish meal, freshly prepared for that very day. Meow? But why did today's portion seem a touch smaller? Puzzled, Flurry padded over to its master with graceful, elegant steps, and rubbed against the hem of his robe. The young gentleman's face showed a flash of shame. He crouched down halfway, stroked Flurry's fluffy little head, and with a practiced hand scratched beneath its chin. "Forgive us, my dear Flurry. These past few days our purse has run rather thin. Once we have earned money again, you may eat all the fish you please." Flurry purred and lifted its chin, its glassy blue eyes gazing earnestly up at its master, blinking slowly, as though it truly understood every word. The gentleman, unable to bear letting Flurry suffer even the smallest hardship, was already turning over in his mind how he might make up for the shortfall in its meals as he rose to his feet. The cat, innocent and generous of heart, simply assumed its master's hunt had gone poorly that day, and offered a couple of soft meows toward his retreating back by way of understanding, never suspecting that for some days yet to come, its portion of fish meal would remain rather smaller than before.

en: The Temple of the Martial King, also known as the Martial Temple, stands outside Kaifeng's city walls, enshrining military generals of past dynasties. Built into the mountainside with tiered depth, the temple mirrors the Confucian Temple in layout, featuring a central Saint, ten Philosophers, and seventy-two Generals in solemn ranks. Heavily guarded around the clock, it conceals an underground chamber—an exact replica of the temple above, housing weapons and armors of Later Zhou warlords. Strangely, the God of Slaughter's statue occupies the Saint's throne, and the foremost seat among the Ten Philosophers belongs to Li Jun, a general who rebelled against the Song dynasty at its founding and perished by self-immolation.

这个名字和那口旧衣箱有关。
那口旧衣箱不知最初是谁放的。箱子没锁。里头有些没用完的物什，几件还很新的冬袍，约莫是哪几位前辈下山前留下的。
后来这箱子再没空过，旧的被取走，新的又填进来，像一汪泉水。年轻人嘛，难免有窘迫的时候。
它就是这汪泉水里冒出来的。
没人说得清是哪一年。只记得有一晚，箱子盖自己顶开了。它探出头，打了个喷嚏。
有人说，它是箱子里的旧衣裳养出来的。那些衣裳里存着主人的记忆：领口的墨痕，是抄书抄到睡着的；袖口的毛边，是趴在案上打盹时蹭出来的……零零碎碎的记忆，在箱子里聚在一起，捂久了，便有了心跳。
平日里，它一直团在旧衣箱的盖上。
有人来放东西、取东西，它就伸个懒腰，“啪嗒”，把箱子让出来。人走了，又团回去，“啪嗒”，把箱子盖上。
“锁扣”这个名字，就这么叫开了。
旧物里冒出来的猫，比寻常的猫更怕冷。天一凉，它就开始四处找人。
它专找刚从箱子里取了衣裳的人，夜里钻进那人的被子，贴着人后背蜷成一团，呼噜打得像山谷里闷闷的雷。
被选中的人，那晚会睡得格外踏实。
梦里好像有人远远叫喊了自己的名字。有人梦见的是老师，有人梦见的是师兄师姐，有人梦见的是早已下山的某位同窗。
醒来枕边空空的，只余一撮猫毛，挠得鼻子微微发痒。
en:
The name has to do with an old clothing chest.
No one knows who first placed it there. The chest had no lock. Inside were a few things left over from those who had gone before: some unfinished odds and ends, several winter robes still quite new, likely left behind by elder disciples before they descended the mountain.
After that, the chest was never empty again. Old things were taken, new things put in their place, like a spring that never runs dry. Young men, after all, are no strangers to hardship.
And it was from this spring that the cat emerged.
No one could say quite which year. Only that one night, the lid of the chest lifted itself open. A head poked out, and sneezed.
Some say it was nursed into being by the old garments inside the chest, that those clothes still held the memories of their owners: an ink stain at the collar from copying texts until one fell asleep; a frayed cuff worn away from dozing in a nap with one's arms folded on the desk... All those scattered fragments of memory, gathered together inside the chest, kept warm long enough, until a heartbeat stirred within them.
In the ordinary way of things, the cat remained curled upon the lid of the old chest.
Whenever someone came to place something in or take something out, it would stretch with a lazy yawn, and yield the chest with a thud. When they left, it would curl back and close the lid again, with another thud.
And so, the cat came to be called Latch.
A cat born of old things fears the cold more than other cats. When the air turned chill, it would begin seeking people out.
It sought in particular those who had just taken clothing from the chest, creeping into their bedding come nightfall, curling tight against their back, purring like muffled thunder rolling through a mountain valley.
Whoever was chosen would sleep uncommonly soundly that night.
In their dreams, it seemed as though someone called their name from far away. Some dreamed of their teacher; some of a senior brother or sister; some of a fellow student who had long since descended the mountain.
Upon waking, they would find the pillow beside them empty, save for a tuft of cat fur, just enough to set the nose to a faint, gentle itch.

zh:
在我刚入门时，我十分热爱烹饪，享受用食物让人快乐，但随着担子加重，我已经很久没有去在意研究外的事情。
这次久违地为流民烹饪，为弟子授课，我注意到了太多长期以来被忽视的事。
弟子们越来越缺乏历练，不珍惜身体，而民间的智慧也在被忽视......身为孩子们的师长，墨山道的长老，此事在我，未能以身作则，蹉跎光阴，如今千头万绪，却已是残躯。
写信于你，望惜取少年时。
en:
When I first entered the order, I loved to cook. There was something deeply satisfying about making people happy with food. But as the burden grew heavier, I stopped noticing anything outside my research.
This time, cooking again for the refugees and teaching the disciples after so long, I found myself seeing all too clearly the things that had been neglected for years.
The disciples have grown ever more removed from the realities of the world, and ever less mindful of their own well-being. And with that, the hard-won wisdom of ordinary folk has been quietly pushed aside. As their master and as an elder of Mohist Hill, that failing is mine. I did not lead them well. I let the years drift past. And now there is so much left tangled and untended, while this old body of mine is already giving out.
Cherish your youth while you still can.

zh:
安西军都知道，将军有一件明光甲，是御赐。
每次战前，将军都要一遍一遍的擦拭。
后来，这件明光甲背铠上遍布箭痕，
鳞甲被斩掉，再用战亡的兵士鳞甲补上。
这件战甲经历了一场又一场战役，
贴上了一片又一片同袍的鳞甲。
第三镇、第七镇……第三十五镇……
那些为振士气，改“队”而成的“镇”，一次又一次的全灭，一次又一次的重组……

后来，当每日无事的时候，将军都会面向长安的方向，
一遍又一遍的擦着这件早已看不出样子的明光甲。
将军说，这件明光甲有袍泽护佑，百战不败。
en:
Every soldier of the Anxi Army knew the general had a piece of armor, bestowed by the emperor. 
Before each battle, he would polish it again and again. 
Later, the backplate was riddled with arrow marks. 
Scales were hacked away, replaced with scales from fallen soldiers. 
The armor endured battle after battle, 
gaining scale after scale from comrades. 
The Third Garrison, the Seventh Garrison... the Thirty-Fifth Garrison... 
Those "garrisons" renamed from "companies" to rally morale—wiped out again and again, reformed again and again... 

Later, in quiet days, the general would face the direction of Chang'an, 
polishing over and over the armor that no longer resembled its original form. 
The general said this armor, blessed by his brothers-in-arms, shall never falter in battle.

郭昕郑重点头，将其牢记心中。
而跟在郭昕马后的小兵陈虎，亦跟着亦郑重点头。

数十年后，当陈虎历尽艰辛，终于在一场又一场的战斗中活下来，终于调至粮道下那距离将军最近的二十五镇时，他望着手中那支在战场上捡到的将军遗落的折箭簪，在心中暗道。
“我要将此簪亲手还给将军。”
“西边路险，当同此箭，宁折不弯。”
“将军做到了，我也做到了。”——但尖锐的哨响突然划破长空。

一场血战过后，是一阵巨大的轰鸣。
没有人从这白头城的粮道走出去。敌军如此，安西军第二十五镇全体兵将，亦如此。
乱石为坟，忠骨长埋。
en:
"Dangerous going west. Be like this arrow—rather break than bend," said Guo Xin's uncle Guo Ziyi, who broke an arrow to see Guo Xin off Chang'an. 
Guo Xin nodded solemnly, engraving them in his heart. 
The young soldier Chen Hu, following behind Guo Xin's horse, also nodded gravely. 

Decades later, after enduring hardship and surviving battle after battle, Chen Hu was finally transferred to the 25th Garrison—closest to the general along the supply route. Holding an unyielding arrow the general had dropped in battle, he thought to himself: 
"I will return it to the general myself." 
"Dangerous going west. Be like this arrow—rather break than bend." 
"The general did it. So did I." But a sharp whistle suddenly pierced the sky. 

After a bloody battle came a tremendous roar. 
No one walked out from the supply route of Whitecrown Fortress. Not the enemy, nor any soldier of the Anxi Army's 25th Garrison. 
A grave of scattered stones buried deep the loyal bones.

扉页标注：
我门弟子避世而非忘世，藏踪行遍四海，以机关暗助苍生。
千虑有失，难免无意暴露墨门身份。诸同门可以此书为戒，反思举止破绽。

第一计·引蛇出洞

在这个纷繁复杂的江湖里，存在着一类特殊人群——墨山道。
和堂堂正正的九流门不一样，墨山道的门规奇奇怪怪，在外游历的弟子，都得把本事藏严实了。
老话说得好，只要是演的，那就一定是假的！
和那些唱唱跳跳的门派、酒蒙子门派不一样啊，九流门的能人，在人群中这么一扫，就能认出谁是墨山道来。
常见墨山道弟子分为两类：一类是明目张胆的显性，一类是深藏不露的隐性。
不论是哪种，他们都有个共同点：见到机关后神情古怪，眼神游移。
如果你问孤云：这题能算出来，算你厉害。他们就会奋不顾身奔向题海。
而墨山道的弟子，要么盯着机关若有所思，要么看见工造斜眼观瞧。此时你拿出一件机关小物大喊：拆得出来，算你厉害！
——墨山弟子十有八九无法抗拒这样的诱惑。
至于认出以后，是真情实感找他们帮忙做做机关，还是见义勇为拆穿伪装，那就各凭心意了。

更多高端辨识技巧，请凭书签前往鬼市古书铺，回复“续阅”，更多精彩等你来！
en:
Title Page:
Our disciples steer clear of the world but don't forget it. They travel far and wide in secret, using mechanisms to quietly help others.
No matter how careful you are, slips happen, and sometimes a disciple's identity is accidentally revealed. Let this book serve as a warning to reflect on your actions and avoid such mistakes.

Strategy One: Lure Them Out

Unlike the Nine Mortal Ways, Mohist Hill has odd rules, and their disciples must keep their skills tightly under wraps in the jianghu.
As the old saying goes: if they're putting on an act, it's bound to be a sham!
Unlike those sects of dancing peacocks or bumbling drunks, the skilled folks of the Nine Mortal Ways can spot a Mohist Hill disciple from a crowd. Mohist Hill disciples come in two types: the overt and the covert. But both share one thing in common: when they see a mechanism, their expressions change, and their eyes dart nervously.
Tell a Lone Cloud disciple, "I'll call you a genius if you solve this," and they'll dive right in. Mohist Hill disciples, however, either stare thoughtfully or scrutinize mechanisms from the corner of their eyes. Most Mohist Hill disciples can't resist the challenge of dismantling mechanical gadgets. Once they reveal themselves, it's up to you to decide whether to ask them for help or to see through their disguise.

For more advanced tips, visit the Antique Bookshop with the bookmark and reply "Continue Reading." More exciting secrets await!

en: There is no single vantage point to admire the moon at West Lake. The waters are boundless, and the moon's grace falls everywhere. Drifting eastward in a skiff, one beholds the twinkling lanterns of the city; gazing west from the Goldsurge Gate, the North and South Peaks stand in silent opposition. Sitting in a boat, face turned toward the moon, cradled entirely by shimmering waters, one feels woven directly into a painting. Yet, the most magnificent stretch of water unfurls around the White Causeway and Lone Hill. When the autumn air is crisp and a full moon commands the sky, the glassy surface perfectly catches the boundless hues of the season. Thus, this quiet expanse alone claims the title, "Autumn Moon over the Calm Lake."
