zh:
傅千里第一次走那么远远的路，是从故乡到天泉。 
朔风凛冽，积雪没膝，她每一步都陷得极深，直到半个身子都被雪吞没，才被回过头的师兄拔出来。
抬头望去，远方白茫茫一片，一直连到天上。天泉，还遥在千里之外。 
师兄却笑着指向天边隐约的灯火：“那儿就是了，快到家了！” 

家，新的家。 
家里的大伙都说，傅千里有个好名字。师兄说这名字大气，师弟师妹们羡慕这名字潇洒。她自己也喜欢。
千里之行回了家，最好的家：春起练刀，炎夏锻体，秋来集皮作袄，冬日围炉煮酒……四季如是，安稳寻常。
她不必再一程一程奔波，不必再走那样远的路了。  

可或许是名字所谶，她终又踏上千里之途。 
滹沱河长一千里，太白山遥隔两千里，天泉弟子们的尸首却只堆在三步之内。
横刀渐沉，血气盈鼻，耳畔却响起师弟师妹们向师父请命时的铿锵之声。 
自有家始，只一件事能让她奔赴千里，也只一件事让她弃家不回—— 
“师父所愿，三百弟子，一个都不能少。” 
“师姐，那要是我们带不回呢？”
“......死战方休，三百弟子，一个都不能少。”
en:
The first time Fu Qianli ever walked such a long road was from her hometown to Well of Heaven.

The north wind cut like a blade, and the snow was deep enough to swallow her to the knees. Every step sank hard. At one point, half her body disappeared into the drift before the senior brother ahead of her turned back and hauled her out.
When she looked up, all she could see was white, stretching far and wide until it seemed to meet the sky.
Well of Heaven was still a thousand li away.

But her senior brother only smiled and pointed toward a faint light far off at the horizon.
"There. That's it. We're almost home."

Home.
A new home.

Qianli means "a thousand li." Everyone there said Fu Qianli had been given a fine name. Her senior brother said it sounded grand. Her junior brothers and sisters envied how free and bold it felt. She liked it too.
That thousand-li journey had brought her home, to the best home she could have hoped for.

In spring they practiced with the blade. In the heat of summer they trained their bodies. When autumn came they gathered hides for winter coats. In winter they sat by the fire and warmed wine.
The seasons passed like that, one after another, steady and ordinary and peaceful.
She no longer had to keep moving from one place to the next. She no longer had to walk such long roads.

And yet, perhaps her name had foretold it all along. In the end, she set out on another thousand-li road.
The Hutuo River ran for a thousand li. Mount Taibai lay two thousand li away.
But the bodies of the disciples of Well of Heaven lay piled within three paces of one another.

Her sword was growing heavier in her hand. The smell of blood filled her nose. And yet in her ears rang the voices of her junior brothers and sisters when they had stood before their master and asked to go.
Ever since she had found a home, there had only ever been one thing that could send her a thousand li from it, and only one thing that could keep her from returning.

"Master's command. Three hundred disciples. Not one can be left behind."
"Senior Sister... what if we can't bring them back?"
"...Then we fight to the death. Three hundred disciples. Not one can be left behind."
I humbly ask for your advice, sir.

en: Ruyi had wandered through many places before finding this fine and most excellent place to settle down. Here, the eaves stood square and true, sheltering it from the rain; and the two-legged folk passing by would even bow their heads and murmur words it could not understand. Whenever it sat perched up high, watching the people bow low before it, Ruyi felt overjoyed, quite certain that it must be the sturdiest, most magnificent cat in the whole place. And though Ruyi could not understand the words that fell from people's lips, it could read their tears well enough. It often wondered: how could a person hold so many tears? Longer, surely, than any river it had ever walked beside. Whenever this happened, Ruyi would climb down from the shrine and sit close beside them. Perhaps, it thought, once the person stopped weeping, the long season of rain would finally pass.

梅岭寒烟藏翡翠，桂江秋水露鰅鳙。

鳙鱼头大体胖，因此俗名“胖头鱼”。其形似鲢，而鲢首细而白，鳙则首大而黑。鳙鱼多栖息于淡水湖泊、河流、池塘中。鳙鱼肉味甘，性温，入药可治风湿头痛。《山海经》中记载：樕蛛之山，食水出焉。中多鳙鳙之鱼，音容。状如犁牛，其音如彘鸣。这里的“鳙鳙之鱼”很可能就是今日之鳙鱼。
en:
Cold mists veil emerald in Mei Ridge's embrace, and autumn waters unveil Yuyong fish in Gui River's grace.

The bighead carp, known colloquially as "fathead," resembles the silver carp but has a larger, darker head. Dwelling in lakes, rivers, and ponds, it's prized for its rich flavor and warming properties in traditional medicine. Cited in The Classic of Mountains and Seas: "On Mount Suzhu, the waters of Shishui emerge. It is home to the yongyong fish, known for their sound and form. They resemble plowing oxen in shape, and their calls are like the grunts of pigs." The yongyong fish is likely referring to the bighead carp we know today.

zh:
从记事起，田齐就是个牢牢跟在兄长身后的小跟屁虫。
他是个最平凡不过的人，没有雄心壮志，也没有人生理想，唯一想做的事，便是跟着兄长，走一样的路。
所以他跟着兄长一起进了文津馆，又在兄长离开时，义无反顾地也选择离开。

当兄长和他回到童年时的秘密洞窟一同隐居时，田齐是很高兴的。
不管怎么样，自己是唯一一个始终陪伴在兄长左右的人。
那个洞窟没有第三人知道，还保留着许多他们幼年留下的痕迹。
初学字时歪七扭八的草稿、小时练剑对招的竹枝、遗失很久不曾找到的那枚棋子……
他惊喜地将这些东西一一给兄长看，但兄长却颜色淡淡，依旧埋头研习他从文津馆带出来的那些藏书。
来到这个洞窟后，兄长总是在读书。
那些书里藏着兄长要做的事，但田齐从未读懂。
读不懂没关系，只要跟着兄长走就好了，田齐这么安慰自己。

直到有一天，兄长读完了那些书，再次决心离开，并毁去了他们过去全部的痕迹。
究竟要做什么样的大事，值得抹去自己所有存在的痕迹？
他从未读懂过兄长。

他终于明白过来，原来这么多年，他从未真正走上同兄长一样的路。他一直注视着那人的背影，却早在一个久远的瞬间将他跟丢。
平庸、渺小、怯懦的他，却固执地以为年少时的相守可以有一生那般长久。
却不知有些在起步时相濡以沫的人，注定要在路的中间分开。
这一次，田齐没有跟上去。
en:
From the moment he could remember, Tian Qi had always been a little tag-a-long clinging to his elder brother's heels.
He was the most ordinary of souls—no grand ambitions, no lofty dreams. The only thing he ever wanted was to follow his brother and walk the same path.
So he joined his brother at Inkbound Order, and when his brother left, he followed without hesitation.

Tian Qi was delighted when his brother took him back to their childhood secret cave to live in seclusion.
No matter what, he was the only one who had always stayed by his brother's side.
That cave, known to no one else, still held traces of their youth:
The crooked scribbles of their first attempts at writing, the bamboo sticks they once used for sword practice, a long-lost game piece they could never find...
Delighted, he showed each relic to his brother. But his brother only gave faint smiles, his attention buried in the books he had brought from Inkbound Order.
Ever since coming to the cave, his brother did nothing but read.
Those books held the purpose his brother sought, but Tian Qi never understood it.
It didn't matter if he couldn't understand—he just needed to follow his brother, Tian Qi comforted himself.

Until one day, his brother finished reading those books, decided to leave again, and destroyed all traces of their past.
What kind of great cause could be worth erasing all signs of their existence?
He had never understood his brother.

He finally realized that all these years, he had never truly walked the same path as his brother. He had always stared at the other's back, but had lost him in a distant moment.
Mediocre, insignificant, cowardly—he had foolishly believed the bond of their youth would last a lifetime.
He never knew that some who start together in hardship are fated to part ways along the road.
This time, Tian Qi did not follow.

"年轻一辈的学子们没人说得清猫儿是什么时候来到文津馆的，有好事之徒去问师长，说辞往往众口不一。
邹师信誓旦旦，长乐老建藏书院时曾在天一楼书架间被这恶兽扑过。范师言语确凿，双元拜入文津馆时那小虎在林文元袍角吐了一滩毛球。董师翻了翻日录，证实自己入稽古斋那年便常见此狸奴盘在案上。众说纷纭，猫儿却不屑一顾。
学子们听了一肚子故事，以讹传讹，都说猫儿吃了长乐老的墨汁成了精，与文津馆同寿，比历任十相博学，乃是文津馆的大前辈，可居十相之外第十一相，故而人人皆称一声“喵相”。
喵相每日在馆中自由来去，饿了去膳堂吃最肥的鱼肚，渴了去洗砚池喝最新鲜的墨水，白天躺在晒书坪的书本子上晒太阳，夜里溜进双元居的榻上取暖，任谁都不敢吱一声。直至那一日，猫儿溜达到了金声岭，拿山顶的老松磨爪子，叫巡林的松风先生一把揪住了后脖颈，这才遇到了命里的煞星。
打那之后，猫儿老实了不少，从此只敢在前庭游荡，再不敢往后山踏入一只小爪子，天一楼的典籍、思危阁的门槛、双元居的卧榻总算历劫完毕。"
en:
None among the younger students could say for certain when the cat first arrived at the Inkbound Order, and those inquisitive souls who asked their elders were met with wildly differing tales. Master Zou swore that when Elder Changle first built the Archive Hall, the little beast had ambushed him from between the Tianyi Tower bookshelves. Master Fan insisted with absolute certainty that when the Twin Mavens joined the Order, the little rascal had hacked up a hairball right onto the hem of Lin Wenyuan's robe. Master Dong flipped through his old diaries and confirmed that the very year he entered Antiquity Hall, this feline was already a fixture curled upon the desks. Accounts varied endlessly, yet the cat paid them no mind.
Having heard their fill of these tales, the students embellished them further, claiming the cat had gained spiritual sentience from drinking Elder Changle's ink. They said it shared the Order's lifespan, possessed more wisdom than all past Ten Sages, and stood as a revered elder of the Inkbound Order, practically an "Eleventh Sage." Thus, everyone affectionately called it "Meowster."
Meowster roamed freely throughout the Order every day. When hungry, it sauntered into the Dining Hall for the fattest fish belly; when thirsty, it lapped the freshest ink-water from the Inkstone Pool; by day, it basked in the sun atop manuscripts on the Book-Drying Terrace, and by night, it slipped onto the couches of Essence Retreat for warmth, with not a soul daring to utter a word of protest. That is, until the day it wandered up to Golden Bell Ridge and began sharpening its claws against the ancient pine at the summit, only to be seized by the scruff of its neck by Master Songfeng on woodland patrol, finally meeting its match.
From that day forth, the cat behaved far better, daring only to roam the front courtyard and never again setting a paw into the back mountain. The precious scrolls of Tianyi Tower, the doorframes of Vigilance Pavilion, and the couches of Essence Retreat were finally delivered from their tribulations.

遇到官员间风平浪静的日子，呛呛还会特意去扒拉那些爱斗嘴的官员的衣摆，并学着他们呛声时的调调，咪嗷乱叫一通，以示催促。

In the entire palace, and maybe all of Kaifeng, you'd be hard-pressed to find a kitten that loves a scene more than Sneeze.

When the bell in Wenming Hall rings, officials start arriving from every direction to wait for the early court hour. Sneeze watches with bright-eyed curiosity.
What color robes will today's arguers be wearing?
Will it turn into a fight?
And if they do fight, will any snacks tumble out of their sleeves?

With questions like that in its head, Sneeze keeps scanning its surroundings, darting this way and that, terrified of missing even a single moment of excitement.

On unusually peaceful days, Sneeze will even trot up and paw at the hems of the officials who love to bicker, then copy their sharp tone with a barrage of messy meows, as if urging them to hurry up and start.

他们再次出现在这里，一定是高山雪水的保佑！为首的将军给了我一张寻水图，只要沿着图上标注的路径挖掘，就一定能找到地下水源，解决当下的困局。
那夜，我向将军献上了一碗珍贵的水，请求他们多留几日，好让我们尽地主之谊。将军抬头望望月亮，告诉我他们要去南方打一场仗。
这场仗，难不难？我不懂这些，只能提出这种问题。
将军说，难也，不难。他的眼神落在水碗上，让我附耳过去。
“待我军胜利之日，再来向你讨一碗水罢。”
en:
I never thought this legendary army still existed. 
The elders in the village said they helped build the Karez Well that runs north-south, diverting snowmelt from the Tianshan Mountains, this is how our village came to be. After the severe sandstorm, the Karez Well began to dry up, and we were all extremely anxious. 
Their reappearance here must be a blessing from the mountain snowmelt! The leading general gave me a water map, if we dig along the route marked on it, we will surely find underground water and resolve the current crisis. 
That night, I offered the general a bowl of precious water and begged them to stay a few more days so we could play host. The general looked up at the moon and told me they were going south to fight a battle. 
Will the battle be difficult? I know nothing about such things. This was the only question I could ask. 
"It will be difficult, yet not," the general replied. His gaze fell on the water bowl, and he told me to lean closer. 
"When my army wins the battle, I will come back to ask you for another bowl of water."

zh:
舞马人没有名字，或者说曾经有过，但是现在已经忘了。因身边常年跟随一匹喜欢跳舞的老马，所以别人将其戏称为舞马人。

他是个很普通的人，曾被绣金楼收养，可惜并没有练武的天赋。因此他被送去了茧房，成为梦傀的试验品。很明显他也没有什么特殊的体质，很快他就因试药失败被扔到了乱葬岗。然而就在他快死的时候，一匹军马救了他。

舞马人一直活得很不真实，没什么道德，也没什么善恶，甚至没想过活，也没想过死。他人生唯一的一点真实也许就是那匹军马。他一直想知道为什么那匹军马会救他。
en:
The Horse Tamer has no name, or perhaps he once did, but has long since forgotten. He is followed everywhere by an old horse fond of dancing, so others mockingly call him the Horse Tamer. 

He was an ordinary man, once taken in by Aureate Pavilion. Unfortunately, he had no talent for martial arts. So they sent him to the Cocoon House, where he became a test subject for Sleeping Puppet experiments. Clearly, he lacked any special traits, he failed the drug trial and was quickly discarded in the mass grave mound. But just as he was about to die, a warhorse saved him. 

The Horse Tamer has never truly felt alive. He has no morals, no sense of right or wrong, no desire to live, and no fear of death. The only real thing in his life may have been that warhorse. He's always wondered, why did the horse save him?

捞起月亮，化为馍馍。
那一刻他终于明白，他需要的不是玄妙的咒语，而是一张特殊的网。
那就继续吧。丹轮子擦干满脸的泪水，询问孩子们歌谣的来处。
月为地魄，食之避疾。这一刻，丹轮子仿佛看到，水中的月华再一次照亮了他不复存在的家。
en:
Crimson Wheel travels west, using his medical skills to heal many along the way. 
Hearing his patients' gratitude, his thoughts return to his hometown, ground to dust by plague. 
He asks for no payment, only inquired about the legend of catching the moon to eat. Even when met with kind shakes of the head, he never loses heart. 
Even with one chance in a million, he would press on. The name Crimson Wheel of the Ice Wheel Palace slowly spreads. 
Until one day, Crimson Wheel hears the children's rhyme about the moon and buns. Their clear voices strikes his heart like a hammer. 
Catch the moon, turn it into a bun. 
In that moment, he finally understands: what he needs isn't a mystical incantation, but a special net. 
So, he continues. Wiping tears from his face, Crimson Wheel asks the children where the song comes from. 
The moon is the earth's soul; to eat it is to ward off illness. In that moment, Crimson Wheel seems to see the moonlight in the water once again illuminating the home that was no more there.

zh: 《凉州曲》 唐代民族乐府第一曲调。本为凉州当地民歌，开元九年之前郭知运所献，现已失传。《敦煌乐谱》，又名唐人大曲谱，现存中国最早的琵琶曲谱，对同时期的《凉州曲》的复原有较大参考价值。《凉州曲》于唐广为流行，民间及诸多诗人均依谱创作诗歌，多达百余首，亦留下了许多脍炙人口的佳作。融合胡汉乐舞的艺术形式与丰富的文学创作，展現了唐代多元文化交汇的盛况。
en: Liangzhou Melody is the earliest known ethnic folk tune from the Tang Dynasty, originally a local song from the Liangzhou region. Widely popular in its time, the melody inspired over a hundred poems by both commoners and poets. Blending musical and dance traditions of Han and Hu, Liangzhou Melody reflects the dynamic cultural fusion of the Tang era.

小小八，虽说现在你只会打更，但我对你可是期盼颇高！若有朝一日你能读书识字，我这封书信也就不算白写。

首先……嗯……还是要感谢你这么多年的陪伴！师父他们不见了之后，我这么一个怪人，又天天想那么多怪事，也就只能和你说说话——虽然你也听不懂。好了，肉麻的话说完，接下来就是对你的鞭策了！

第二，交给你一个学会说话的任务！他们都说不可能，但我把你当朋友，当然想听到你的想法。放心，我会努力调整你的机关结构，用来发声！

第三，给你种了很多花草，希望你守屋子的时候不会无聊。

第四，也别忘了打更，很多人指着你报时嘞。


小小八：
如果你永远也看不懂这封信，那也没什么不好的，这样世上就只有小八一个怪脑袋了。
如果有一天我做到了，你真的看懂了这封信，请永远记得这最后一条：小八和小小八，是最好的朋友！
en:
Little Xiaoba, even though you're only a bell toller for now, I still have high hopes for you. If the day ever comes when you can read and write, then this letter will not have been written in vain.
First off... well... thank you for keeping me company all these years. I'm an oddball with a head full of strange ideas. Ever since Zhang Wanshi and the others vanished, you've been the only one I can talk to, even if you don't understand a single word I say.
But enough of the mushy stuff. Time for some encouragement!
First, when I'm away, watch over Aloft Abode for me. But don't actually hurt anyone who comes by. Just give them a scare. My mechanisms do go wrong all the time, but after hearing me ramble on every night, you must have picked up something by now, right?
Second, I'm giving you a task: learn how to speak. Everyone says it's impossible, but I think of you as a friend, so of course I want to hear what you think. Don't worry. I'll keep working on your inner mechanisms until you can make your own voice.
Third, I've planted lots of flowers and herbs for you, so you won't get bored while guarding the house.
Fourth, don't forget to keep the night watch. Plenty of people count on you to tell the time.
Little Xiaoba, if you never do learn to read this letter, that may not be such a bad thing. That way, there will only ever be one odd little head like Xiaoba in this world.
But if one day I really do manage it, and you can understand this letter at last, then please remember this one final thing: Xiaoba and Little Xiaoba are best friends.

zh:
墨山道有内外门之别，入内门则探渊索珠，为千年计；入外门则专工其器，为万民益。
常人谓：“盖以天赋为别？内门为大才，外门为小才。”余思之非也。
周广顺中，有一漠姓外门弟子。与诸长老以机括之术对战，连下三城而不败，人皆叹服。
其人机括，重实效而形制粗野，原为内门所鄙。经此一战，其声名大噪，粗野之风，竟一时风靡，门人竞相以机关粗陋为傲。
时至今日，旧事渐隐，独此风不坠。
en:
At Mohist Hill, disciples are split into the inner and the outer sects. The inner sect digs into deep, long-term knowledge, while the outer sect focuses on practical device-making to serve the people.
Most assume this division reflects talent: the inner sect as gifted scholars, the outer sect as lesser. But that's a misconception.
During the Later Zhou's Guangshun era, an outer disciple surnamed Mo beat several elders in mechanical contests three times straight, earning their respect.
His mechanisms were built for utility, their forms rugged and unrefined, a style once despised by the Inner Sect. Yet after his triumph, his fame soared, and this "brutalist" aesthetic became an overnight sensation.
Though the story's mostly forgotten now, its influence still remains.

Mother Cat had only Tiny One,

Brother is gone, so do not cry,

One cat wanders on her way,
Two cats follow where they may,
Three cats nowhere to be found,
Mother is tired, her worries cease...

Tiny One let out no more meows,
Tail curled around her mother's feet,
Eyes closed tight until the dawn.

昔年白马祸起，文士尸骨相藉于道。为使文脉弗绝于世，文津馆门人负书奔走，或殁于途，或隐于野，生者舍名姓如弃草芥，甘作尘埃。

藏书中者，岁岁心血。待禾下者，代代新芽。
en:
On the back were several lines of smaller writing:

When the Baima Incident broke out, the roads were strewn with the bodies of scholars. To keep the literary tradition from dying out, disciples of the Inkbound Order fled with books in their arms. Some perished on the road, while others vanished into the wilds. Those who survived cast aside their names as lightly as weeds, willing to live on as dust.
My father lived in Dengzhou and kept a collection of books there. After his death, my elder brother carried on his will, only to die amid the chaos.
After years of hard study, I was finally admitted to the Inkbound Order. Now I return with these books to carry on my brother's wish and fulfill my father's last command.
The worn volumes remain intact, their old ink as fresh as new. So each year I offer lamps and food to the Keeper of Books, and have never once dared neglect the rite.
Within these books lie years of abundance; beneath the grain wait new shoots. Only now do I understand the words my father and brother once left me.
What is stored in these books is the labor of years. What waits beneath the grain is the new growth of generations.

The Gu family has always been known for its learning, and I hear the only little girl old enough to start school has been ill since she was born... You should have a word with your employers. They're hardly short of money. If the child's unwell, why not pay for a good tutor at home? Why send her out to struggle?

zh:
阿冉这个名字，是将军给的。
在那之前，它没有名字，只是一条瘦得骨头都硌手的小流浪狗。
野狗吃人剩下的东西，它只能去吃野狗们吃剩下的。
可就是连半截烂骨头，有时也有别的狗来抢——

呜……它咬着那半根骨头不肯松嘴，
腿在抖，牙也在抖，
松开，就什么都没有了。

直到有一双靴子停在它面前，它听到别人叫那靴子的主人将军。
将军蹲下来，摸了摸它的头，说
“跟我走吧。”
它就成了军营里的一只军犬。

虽然阿冉总是在想，军营里有那么多厉害的狗，
而它只是只没什么用的小流浪，能有什么出息？
但只要将军看向它的时候，它就会把尾巴摇得很用力，很用力。
因为，它不会让将军失望的。汪汪汪！
en:
The name Ran was given by the General.
Before that, he had no name, just a thin stray dog whose bones poked through his skin.
Wild dogs eat what humans leave behind; he could only eat what the wild dogs left behind.
But even for a half-rotten bone, other dogs would sometimes fight him for it.

Grrr... he bit down on that half-bone, refusing to let go,
His legs were shaking, his teeth were shaking,
If he let go, he would have nothing.

Until a pair of boots stopped before him, and he heard others call the owner of those boots "General."
The General knelt down, stroked his head, and said,
Come with me.
And so he became a military hound in the camp.

Although Ran often wondered, there are so many powerful dogs in the camp,
And he was just a useless little stray; what could he possibly achieve?
But whenever the General looked at him, he would wag his tail as hard as he could.
Because he would never let the General down. Woof, woof, woof!

zh:
大侠近来可好？
有一份心意想送与大侠。为免寄送延误，还请先行[<LINK id='link' color='#8c5823' url='https://research-game.163.com/htmls/46rzpk/paper.html?uid={uid}&role_id={pid}&server={hostnum}' is_underline='true'>点此留下信址</LINK>]。待我细细说来：
写这封信，是想给你报个喜。多亏你先前帮忙，我才有了支起摊子的本钱，在开封南郊的麦香集里寻了个落脚处。当初从家里出来时，哪敢想有今日……
爷爷常说，谢人不能只挂在嘴上。想来想去，我把近日攒下的钱寄回富平老家，用大侠的名义承包了五亩柿子地，托爷爷和乡亲们照看。爷爷说，要让你瞧瞧，特意让村里的老画师给画了下来，我都能想象后头红彤彤的模样了！
不过今年老家的天儿有些邪乎……又是旱又是涝的没断过，八成会影响收成……等到了做柿饼的时候，总要送你些尝尝，可能不多，但都是乡亲们的心意。不知大侠住在何处？一定包得仔仔细细的给你送去！
<IMAGE id='im1' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/6937da14adc9b826d105d516qNsfi7bO07' size='1810*1357' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>
en:
Dear Wanderer,
How are you? I have a small token of my gratitude for you. To avoid any delay in its arrival, please press [<LINK id='link' color='#8c5823' url='https://research-game.163.com/htmls/46rzpk/paper.html?uid={uid}&role_id={pid}&server={hostnum}' is_underline='true'> to register your mailing address</LINK>] first. Allow me to explain:
I write with glad tidings. Thanks to your help, I've set up my stall at the Wheatwind Bazaar in Kaifeng Suburbs-South. When I left home, I never dreamed such a day…
Grandfather always said gratitude must be more than words. So I've sent my savings back to Fuping, my hometown, to lease five mu of persimmon groves in your name. Grandfather and the villagers tend them. He insisted on having the old painter paint them for you. I can already imagine the fiery red blaze!
But the weather's been cruel this year, drought and flood by turns. The harvest would likely suffer…
When the dried persimmons come, I'll send you some. Not much, perhaps, but grown from honest hearts. Where do you lodge? I'll package them with care and have them delivered.
<IMAGE id='im1' image_url='https://h72.fp.ps.netease.com/file/6937da14adc9b826d105d516qNsfi7bO07' size='1810*1357' color='255;255;255')'></IMAGE>

世有异物，似玉非玉，佩之则微振若洪钟。若二人长佩此物，双魂犹龙泉太阿同匣而鸣，叠梦互济，如盐入水，不见其形但存其真。
en:
Between living souls runs a hidden current, subtle as breath, vast as the sky. When two are attuned, the air brightens around them, like great bronze and pale jade answering in a single, ringing note. When discord rises, the clash is sharp and bitter, like ice water striking stone, scattering into restless spray.
There exists a relic that wears the face of jade but carries a deeper pulse. Held close, it hums like a buried bell. If two bear it long enough, their souls begin to answer across distance, like twin divine blades sharing one sheath, trembling with shared edge and purpose. Dreams cross over. Boundaries thin. Like salt in water, the form dissolves. Only the presence remains.

zh:
又过了几年，姐妹两个长大了，莫晓云也到了及笄之年。
行过及笄礼，便有媒人上门提亲。
晓云也知道这件事并非自己可以做主。不过爷娘素来疼自己，想必未来夫婿也不会太差。
只是那一天，夕霓很不高兴。

到了熄灯时分，夕霓仍抱着被子坐在床上闷闷不乐。
晓云也没说什么，默默去了发饰，散下头发，和衣睡下。
半晌，夕霓气鼓鼓地吹灯，背对着晓云躺下。
这么多年来，姐妹两个亲密无间，还像小时候一样睡在一起。
“怎么了，是羡慕阿姊要出嫁，有了郎君？”莫晓云还是决定打破沉默。“你也别急，等你及笄了，爷娘也会给你找个好夫婿呢。”
“阿姊，你要是出嫁了，是不是除夕夜就不能……和我我一起过了。”半晌，夕霓的声音闷闷地响起。
她翻过身，两行眼泪扑簌簌地掉在枕头上。
"明明是一起生活一起睡觉的一家人，怎么就一下变成外人了？”
莫晓云也不知该怎么回答。她只好摸了摸妹妹的头。
“自古以来便是这样的。”她轻轻叹一口气。
“可自古以来就是对的吗！”莫夕霓从床上跳起来，气鼓鼓地走出去了。

夜色那么重，莫晓云披上一件罩衣。推开门，她就看到妹妹坐在院子里。手里的草根折了又折。
“阿姊，我……”发现身后的莫晓云，莫夕霓抬起头，眼里的泪花还没有散去。
“阿姊都知道。”莫晓云也坐下来，牵起妹妹的手，就像小时候一样。
“爷娘说，那人住的不远，是同一坊的人。”
“以后你想阿姊，可以来找我。”
“家里以后就要靠你了。多听爷娘的话。”
“自己一个人也要开心。晓夕云霓，快乐无拘。”
莫晓云絮絮叨叨，完全没发现妹妹已经靠在自己的肩头睡着了。
晓云的眼角，一滴珠泪重重跌入夜色。
en:
A few more years passed. The sisters grew up, and Mo Xiaoyun reached her coming-of-age ceremony. 
After the ceremony, matchmakers came with proposals. 
Xiaoyun knew this wasn't something she could decide. But her parents had always doted on her, so surely her future husband wouldn't be too bad. 
Only, that day, Xini was very unhappy. 

When it was time to extinguish the lamps, Xini still sat on the bed sulking, hugging her quilt. 
Xiaoyun said nothing, quietly removed her hair ornaments, let her hair down, and lay down in her clothes. 
After a while, Xini huffily blew out the lamp and lay down with her back to Xiaoyun. 
For so many years, the sisters had been inseparable, sleeping together like when they were little. 
"What's wrong? Jealous that your big sister is getting married and will have a husband?" Mo Xiaoyun decided to break the silence. "Don't worry. When you come of age, Mom and Dad will find you a good husband too." 
"Big sister... if you get married, does that mean you can't... spend New Year's Eve with me anymore?" Xini's muffled voice came after a pause. 
She turned over. Two lines of tears fell onto the pillow. 
"We're a family who lives together, sleeps together... how do we suddenly become outsiders?" 
Mo Xiaoyun didn't know how to answer. She could only pat her sister's head. 
"It's always been this way since ancient times," she sighed softly. 
"But has it always been right?!" Mo Xini jumped up from the bed and stomped out. 

The night was deep. Mo Xiaoyun threw on an outer robe. Pushing the door open, she saw her sister sitting in the courtyard, twisting and breaking a blade of grass. 
"Big sister, I..." Discovering Mo Xiaoyun behind her, Mo Xini looked up, tears still shimmering in her eyes. 
"Big sister knows." Mo Xiaoyun sat down too, taking her sister's hand, just like when they were little. 
"Mom and Dad say he doesn't live far, in the same district." 
"If you miss me, you can come find me." 
"You'll have to look after the family from now on. Listen to Mom and Dad." 
"Be happy on your own too. Morning clouds and evening glories—joy without bounds." 
Mo Xiaoyun rambled on, completely unaware her sister had already fallen asleep leaning on her shoulder. 
A single, heavy tear fell from Xiaoyun's eye into the night.

Half bird, half tooth.

He thought about it and remembered the Skyward City the gentleman mentioned.
The gentleman turned into a bird and flew away.
At that moment, he was certain the gentleman's name must be "Crow"!

农，天下之本，务莫大焉。历朝历代都严禁宰杀耕牛，待牛自然死亡后，方可食其肉，取皮、筋、角等物。五代时期季风线南移，水牛也逐步向南方迁移，故而太宗以后，北方多黄牛，南方多水牛。此外，宋代风俗画鼎盛，“牧牛图”、“耕织图”中常常能见到牛的身影。
en:
Even grass reaching to the brow proves hard to eat, a herdsman tugs at the horns without turning his head. 

Farming is the foundation of the nation, no task is more important. Throughout history, it was forbidden to slaughter oxen. Only after they died naturally could their meat, hide, tendons, or horns be used. During the Five Dynasties period, the monsoon line shifted south, prompting the migration of water buffalo southward. Thus, after Emperor Taizong's reign, the north had mostly yellow ox while the south had water buffalo. Additionally, folk paintings flourished in the Song era, and images of cattle frequently appeared in artworks such as Herding Cattle and Weaving and Farming Scenes.

zh:
方鸿一生沉迷武道，讲得是稳扎稳打的功夫。
直到知天命的年纪，他才觉武功算成了，动了开宗立派的心思。

北边的消息传来时，他正在清河老家，准备给自己要开的新门派题名。
他的老来子一个劲儿在他怀里乱窜，顽皮地把印章的红泥点上了他的鼻梁。
“好旭儿，你爹去去就回！”他猛地亲了他的好儿子一口，和家人交换了一个坚定的眼神。随即丢下笔，拿起自己的老伙计，就往中渡桥去了。

他的门派没立起来，他的旭儿也再没见到他。
一代宗师，最后被如蚁潮般的敌兵杀死。
死前他只教了一个“徒弟”，一个让他想起自己儿子的徒弟。
方鸿想，这一生，也不赖。
en:
Fang Hong spent his life obsessed with the martial path, focusing on steady and solid skills.
Not until his fifties did he feel his martial arts were complete and think of founding his own sect.

When news from the north arrived, he was at his home in Qinghe, preparing to name his new sect.
His young son squirmed in his arms, playfully dotting his nose with red ink from a seal.
"Xu'er, your father will be right back!" He kissed his son, exchanged a firm look with his family, dropped his pen, took up his old weapon, and headed for Zhongdu Bridge.

His sect was never founded, and Xu'er never saw him again.
A grandmaster, killed at last by a swarming tide of enemy soldiers.
Before dying, he taught only one "disciple", a boy who reminded him of his own son.
Fang Hong thought, "This life wasn't bad at all."

zh:
自朋乐堂走出，青石广坪横于身前。左右松柏数株，疏落有致，苍翠如盖。仰首则见孔夫子石像巍然立，高可接云。
初至时，余独立坪中，仰视良久。石像高耸入云，须眉宛然，衣袂凝止，如收万风。同行者皆默然，无人言语。彼时方觉天地之阔，己身之微。余仰首良久，思及昔者夫子周游列国，厄于陈蔡，削迹于卫，犹弦歌不辍。今吾辈坐拥庠序之安，仰其遗像，岂可不勉乎？
后每晨起，必过此坪。或捧书绕像而行，步声轻缓，纸页窸窣，与松风相和；或坐阶上，抬眼见像，心亦随之静。
一日，余立于众人间，仰见圣人垂目，默然无言，忽觉千古之间，斯人已逝，而斯道犹存。其所遗者，非惟此像，乃六经之文，仁义之教，万世之师也。
夫子设教杏坛，弟子三千，七十二贤，所传者何？忠恕，仁爱。今余辈负笈来此，终日读经，若不体此心，则书卷徒陈，何异于市井之贾？遂整衣冠，请示夫子，再拜而去。
暮色四合，松影渐深，像立于暗处，巍然如初。余步出仰止坪，回首望之，灯火初上，石像轮廓隐隐，似在目送。
en:
Stepping out from the Hall of Friendship, a broad stone plaza stretches ahead. Pines and cypresses stand scattered to either side, verdant and towering like a canopy. Raising one's eyes, the stone statue of Confucius looms high, its peak seeming to touch the clouds.
When I first arrived, I stood alone in the plaza, gazing upward for a long while. The statue rose into the clouds, its brows and beard lifelike, its robes frozen mid-motion as though it had gathered in all the winds. My companions fell silent, none speaking a word. Only then did I sense the vastness of heaven and earth, and how small I truly was. I gazed upward for a long time, recalling how the Master once wandered from state to state, besieged in Chen and Cai, driven from Wei, yet never ceased his songs and teachings. Now that we enjoy the peace of scholarly halls, gazing upon his likeness, how could we not strive harder?
After that, I passed by this plaza every morning. Sometimes I walked around the statue with a book in hand, my footsteps soft and slow, the rustle of pages mingling with the breeze through the pines; sometimes I sat upon the steps, looking up at the statue, and my heart grew calm along with it.
One day, standing among the crowd, I looked up and saw the Sage's downcast eyes, silent and wordless, and suddenly felt that though ages have passed and the man himself is gone, his Way remains. What he left behind is not merely this statue, but the words of the Six Classics, the teaching of benevolence and righteousness... truly a teacher for ten thousand generations.
The Master taught at the Apricot Altar, with three thousand disciples and seventy-two worthies among them. What did he pass down? Loyalty, forgiveness, benevolence, and love. Now we who carry our satchels here spend our days reading the classics; if we fail to grasp this spirit, our books become mere ornaments, no different from a merchant's wares. And so I straightened my robe and cap, bowed twice before the Master, and departed.
As dusk gathered and the shadows of the pines deepened, the statue stood in the darkness, as majestic as ever. I stepped out from Aspiration Court, and looking back, saw the first lanterns lit, the statue's silhouette faint in the gloom, as though watching me go.
Frostbone

zh:
玉棠吾弟：

昔日一别，倏忽四载，音书两绝，思念却甚。每忆儿时并辔，驰于幽州之野，未尝不临风涕泣，暗自神伤。
自幽州沦陷，伏马庄始遭劫难，于今八载矣。每以为时局可待，熟料步步临渊，屡遭折辱，至于今日。

契丹非不爱马，不敬人也。其觊觎驯马绝技久矣，以燕北盟之名假意亲近，欲求秘法。竟棠少而聪慧，识破其卑劣技俩后宁死不从，虏人便借私通燕北盟之名将其处决。

彼时举族陷于敌手，得竟棠死讯，方知肃清伊始。幸遇顾盼与一应萤火同胞冒死辗转边关，终得援手脱困。及至奔逃之际，家中尊长为蒙虏人耳目，自愿留守旧宅，待我等尽离契丹之地，方悉诸亲皆殁于幽州，无一幸还。

至滹沱河畔，不及思悲，遂戮力重兴伏马庄。然故土之失、契丹之恨、弑亲之仇，无一日不萦怀锥心。天福七年，新帝践祚，罢臣虏之策，似有规复燕云之志。私以为良机已至，乃经吾妻顾盼引介，领燕北盟之命，继任飞马之首，于边境接应往来游侠，为朝廷贡战马、备征鞍。又更庄名曰“怒马”，一泄积愤，亦期少年怒马鲜衣，雪此深仇。

然汝尝劝阻：“朝廷反复未可恃，晋虏之争旦夕危殆，宜南徙蛰伏，以待来日。”今时观之，弟之明见，胜我远矣。

世间之恨，岂独祁家？奸险之辈，亦非尽在虏人。晋师北征时，杜重威亲临庄上，已初现端倪。身为统帅，专事奢靡，毫无报国之心。然其皇亲贵胄，与朝中亲近，以此相要挟，逼迫我等为其藏匿所掠民财。初不知皆榨自百姓，后彦荣宗弟收养二流民遗孤，方知杜贼夺其父母口粮致馁死。顾盼欲择机密报燕北盟，竟为所扼。

玉棠吾弟，晋军溃势已显，庄中诸人皆旦夕难保，灯下修书，聊作长诀。此番与顾盼携族中一众飞马弟子共赴中渡桥，实为最后一搏。昔尝怨天地不仁，致祁氏三罹浩劫，生者无去路，死者无葬地。今秉笔方悟：世变虽亟，咎实在我，无有远见，愧对亲族。世道无常，幸弟已携幼子南下，愿尔寻得常安所，暗蓄伏枥千里志，且待怒马长嘶时。
en:
To my younger brother, Yutang,

Since we parted, four years have passed in the blink of an eye. No letters have come between us, yet my thoughts of you have only grown stronger. Whenever I remember how we rode side by side across the wilds of Youzhou in our younger days, I cannot help but face the wind in tears, grieving in silence.

Ever since Youzhou fell, Finesteed Hamlet has known nothing but calamity. Eight years have passed now. Time and again I told myself the times might yet turn, yet with every step we only drew nearer the brink, suffering one humiliation after another, until we came to this day.

It is not that the Khitans do not prize horses, nor that they do not value men. They had long coveted our family's art of horse training. Under the banner of the Northern Vow, they feigned goodwill and sought our secret methods. Yet Jingtang, young though he was, was quick of mind. Once he saw through their vile scheme, he refused them even unto death. The northerners then executed him under the false charge of colluding with the Northern Vow.

By that time our whole clan had already fallen into enemy hands. Only when news of Jingtang's death reached us did we understand that the purge had begun. By good fortune, we met Gu Pan and a band of fellow Fireflies, who risked their lives to carry word across the border and bring us aid, and so we escaped. Yet in the chaos of flight, the elders of the family, fearing they would expose us to the enemy's spies, chose of their own will to remain behind in the old house. Only after we had fully left Khitan lands did we learn that all our kin in Youzhou had perished. Not one returned alive.

When we reached the banks of the Hutuo River, there was no time left for grief. We bent all our strength to rebuilding Finesteed Hamlet. Yet the loss of our homeland, our hatred for the Khitans, and the blood debt of our murdered kin have not left my heart for a single day. In the seventh year of Tianfu, a new emperor ascended the throne and cast aside the policy of serving the northerners. It seemed he truly meant to recover Yanyun. I judged the time ripe, and through my wife Gu Pan's introduction, I accepted a charge from the Northern Vow and succeeded to the leadership of Flying Horse. Along the border, I received wandering heroes passing to and fro, furnished warhorses to the court, and prepared saddles and tack for the coming campaign. I also changed the estate's name to Ragehoof Hamlet, to vent the anger long pent up within me, and in the hope that one day furious steeds and bright-clad riders might wash away this deep grudge.

Yet you once tried to dissuade me. You said, "The court is fickle and cannot be trusted. The struggle between Jin and the northern foe may collapse at any moment. Better to move south and lie low, waiting for a better day." Looking at things now, your foresight was far greater than mine.

But whose hatred in this world belongs to the Qi family alone? Nor are treacherous men found only among the northerners. When the Jin army marched north, Du Chongwei came personally to the manor, and even then the signs had begun to show. Though commander of the army, he gave himself over entirely to luxury, with no heart for serving the realm. Yet because he was kin to the imperial house and close to those at court, he used that power to force us to hide away the wealth he had wrung from the people. At first we did not know it had all been squeezed from common folk. Only later, when Yanrong's younger kinsman took in two orphaned vagrants, did we learn that the villain Du had seized the grain from their parents' mouths and left them to starve. Gu Pan meant to find a chance to report this in secret to the Northern Vow, but was seized before she could act.

My brother Yutang, the defeat of the Jin army is already plain to see. Everyone in the manor now stands in peril from one day to the next. By lamplight I write this letter as a final farewell. This time, Gu Pan and I will lead the Flying Horse disciples to Zhongdu Bridge. In truth, it is our final gamble. Once I railed against Heaven's cruelty, that the Qi family should suffer three great calamities, with the living left no road to take and the dead denied even a place to rest. Yet now, brush in hand, I understand at last: though the times have turned with fearful speed, the fault lies with me. I lacked foresight, and I have failed our kin.
The world is in flux; I am heartened that my brother has taken his son south. May you find a sanctuary of peace, awaiting the day to fulfill your ambitions.

zh: 龙泉剑，又名龙渊剑、七星龙渊，相传为春秋战国时期铸剑大师欧冶子所创，是中国古代十大名剑之一，其名源于铸剑处引水成北斗七星池，剑身纹饰如临渊观龙。剑体以折叠锻打工艺制成，从原料到成品须经炼、锻、铲、锉、刻花、淬火等二十余道工序，具有坚韧锋利、刚柔相济、寒光逼人、纹饰巧致四大特色。如今，龙泉宝剑锻制技艺已被列入国家级非物质文化遗产名录。
en: The Longquan Sword, also known as Longyuan or Seven-Star Longyuan, is one of the ten legendary swords of ancient China and is traditionally attributed to the master swordsmith Ou Yezi. Its name is said to come from the seven star-shaped pools formed at the forging site and from the dragon-like patterns on the blade. Made with folded-forging techniques, it goes through more than twenty steps from smelting to quenching. The sword is famed for its toughness, sharpness, balance of hardness and flexibility, cold gleam, and finely patterned surface. Today, Longquan sword-forging is recognized as a National Intangible Cultural Heritage.

zh: 图经以图为主、以经说图，相辅相成，为古典地图的独特形式之一，后图经改称地方志。现存最早图经，即发现于敦煌藏经洞的《沙州都督府图经》，纂写于盛唐时，记录唐代沙州及所辖敦煌、寿昌二县的山川地理、历史风俗等，共667行。
en: Tujings are dominated by maps, with texts explaining the maps, complementing each other. They are one of the unique forms of ancient Chinese maps, later renamed local chronicles. The earliest extant tujing, discovered in the Dunhuang Library Cave, is the Illustrated Treatise of the Shazhou Protectorate. Compiled during the High Tang period, it records the geography, history, and customs of Tang-era Shazhou and its subordinate counties, Dunhuang and Shouchang, comprising 667 lines.

zh: 赛丝绸随着主人漂洋过海，去了很多地方。主人是个年轻天真的青年，有着微卷的头发和碧绿的双眼。主人想要给他的心上人带回罕见的宝物，为此，他去了很多地方，好几次差点消失在风浪里。东方的绫罗绸缎很美，博得了主人的心上人的欢心，但爱人的眼眸很浅，欣喜来的快去的也快，于是主人很快又带着赛丝绸出发了，这次他可能要停留很久，也许再也无法穿过风浪回到爱人的身边。小猫不懂得远航的危险，大船上有很多老鼠窃窃私语，东方的街道也有温暖的太阳可以晒。偶尔做梦，它会想起小时候妈妈带给它的鼠条。
en: Silky journeyed with its master across seas and oceans, visiting many far-off lands. The master was a young, innocent fellow, with slightly curled hair and eyes as green as jade. Wishing to bring back some rare treasure for the one his heart desired, he traveled to many distant places, and more than once nearly vanished into the wind and waves. The fine silks and brocades of the East were beautiful indeed, and won the favor of his beloved's heart. But a lover's affections run shallow at times, and what delight arrives quickly may fade just as fast. And so before long, the master set out once more with Silky at his side. This time, he might be gone for a very long while, perhaps never to cross the wind and waves back to his beloved's side again. The little cat understood nothing of the perils of the long voyage. Aboard the great ship, there were many rats whispering in the shadows, and in the streets of the East, there was always warm sunlight to bask in. Now and then, in its dreams, it would remember the dried mouse-meat strips its mother used to bring it as a kitten.

zh:
如果仇越海十八岁的时候，有人和他说，他日后会成为一个守家为国的大侠客，年轻的仇越海一定会轻飘飘吐出叼着的小麦草，对那人摆一摆手，“去、去别的地儿骗钱去”。

他想过人生的很多种可能，可能是天底下逃得最快的街溜子，是悄悄窃金于闹市的小毛贼，又或者，是个什么也不干的渔夫，每天只钓来一条够吃的鱼。不管哪种，都是小小的、普通的，平凡的人。毕竟他没什么能打的绝世武功，只是腿脚快些，这又不是写话本，哪来那么多凡人的传奇？过好自己的日子就行了呗。

但后来，很多年之后，他明白过来，原来日子不是自己想过好、就一定能过好的。那些冲进你家烧杀抢掠的坏蛋，不会听你的哀求，“求求你了，求求你了，我啥也不想管，只想管好自己”……你谁啊？战马长长嘶鸣，坚硬的铁蹄，踏碎战士的铠甲，也踏碎普通人的屋瓦。
于是他将那条没吃完的鱼，和闭上双眼的人们一同埋进地里，握紧村里最后一杆长枪，向那个叫烈言的人点头，一同向远处走去。
那里已经有一些人在百草野等候，高的矮的、老的少的，唱皮影的，白胡子的。

“喂，我叫仇越海，从今天起，算我一个。”
en:
At eighteen, if someone had told Qiu Yuehai that he would become a heroic swordsman defending his home and country, the young man would have casually spat out the wheat straw in his mouth and waved them off. "Go cheat someone else out of their money."

He had imagined many possibilities for his life: maybe the fastest street runner in the world, a petty thief stealing gold in bustling markets, or a lazy fisherman who only caught one fish a day, just enough to eat. Either way, he'd be small, ordinary, unremarkable. After all, he had no extraordinary Martial Art Skills, just quick legs. This wasn't a storybook. Where did ordinary people get legends? Just live your life, he thought.

But years later, he learned that life isn't something you can simply "live well" if you want to. The raiders who stormed into his home, burning and pillaging, didn't listen to his pleas. "Please, I don't want to meddle in anything—just let me be!" Who did he think he was? Warhorses neighed, their iron hooves shattering soldiers' armor and crushing commoners' rooftop tiles alike.
So he buried the uneaten fish alongside the bodies of those who'd closed their eyes forever, gripped the last long spear in the village, nodded to a man named Lie Yan, and walked into the distance together.
There, in Verdant Wilds, people were already waiting: tall and short, old and young, shadow play singers, and white-bearded elders.

"Hey, I'm Qiu Yuehai. From today on, count me in."

zh:
活者，暂留庙中。
亡者，扎纸为身。
人死异乡，魂不识路。
纸人为身，姓名为引，香火为路。
纸人不可点眼。
有眼，便见人间。见人间，便不肯走。
中元夜，我欲焚纸送魂。
奈何大雨灭香，纸湿不燃。
法事未成。
而我亦染疾，气力日衰，恐不能久守此处。
若后来人见此残庙，愿补一炷火，齐一桌供。
渡一渡这些无归的人。
en:
The living remain temporarily in the temple. For the dead, we bind paper effigies as bodies.
When one dies in a strange land, the soul cannot find its way home. The effigy serves as the body. The name serves as the guide. The incense paves the road.
You must never paint eyes on the effigies. With eyes, they see the mortal realm. Seeing the mortal realm, they refuse to leave.
On the night of the Ghost Festival, I sought to burn the paper and send the souls away. Alas, heavy rain extinguished the incense. The sodden paper would not burn. The ritual failed.
I, too, have caught the sickness. My strength wanes by the day, and I fear I cannot guard this place much longer.
If anyone should arrive later and find this ruined temple, I beg you to light a stick of incense and prepare an altar of offerings.
Grant deliverance to these wandering souls.

zh:
年月日，余闻君丧，因取酒以祭，为文而吊之，其辞曰：嗟我兄弟，天资特挺，朗心聪警，柔情和泰，未逢吉时，突罹厄祸，呜呼上天，捐子中野，呜呼上天，逝者日远。
忆昔竹林把酒夜话，筹谋四域，意欲通商南北。君携我手，言男儿之志，乃定共商之约。而今竹林如故，阶尘未扫，惟人酒两亡，影绝响灭，痛天道之茫昧，予岂无言？而悲来从中，远复抒意，匪祭也，永以为别也。尚飨！
en:
Upon hearing of your passing, I poured wine in your memory and wrote down these words of tribute: Oh, my brother, how remarkable you were—brilliant beyond measure, clear of mind, sharp and kind, gentle and serene by nature. Yet cruel fate struck without mercy. O heavens above, how could you allow him to rest forgotten in the wild? O heavens, the departed slip further from us with each passing day.
I remember those nights beneath the bamboo, sharing wine and dreams and planning ventures to bridge north and south. You clasped my hand as we vowed to walk this path together. The bamboo grove stands unchanged, the stone steps cloaked in dust, yet you are gone—the wine grown cold, your voice forever stilled. I grieve the injustice of it all. Though miles apart, my heart cries out still. This is no ordinary farewell, but a solemn, eternal goodbye. May this tribute find you in peace.

zh:
据传，无患崖上来了个医术高超的毛大夫。
“毛大夫，自打听了爆炸声，俺再没睡过一个好觉……”毛大夫轻轻一跃，在患者身上略施巧劲——揉捏穴位，有助安神。
“毛大夫，我腿脚落下了病根，一到阴雨天就疼得不行……”毛大夫朝患者伸了个懒腰——拉伸肌肉，有助缓解酸痛。
“毛大夫，他已经走了三年了，可我还是忘不掉……”毛大夫主动把身子凑了过去——人，你可以永远倚靠在毛茸茸的怀抱里！
有好事者不信有如此神医，想要一探究竟，可周围并无医箱药篓，只有一地吃剩的小鱼干。
奇也怪哉，猫大夫可不能给人看病，但见到毛大夫的患者，却总觉身子好了几分。
en:
Rumor has it that a highly skilled Dr. Fluffy has arrived at Brighthale Cliff.
Dr. Fluffy, ever since I heard that explosion, I haven't had a good night's sleep... Dr. Fluffy would leap up and apply precise pressure on the patient, massaging acupoints helps calm the mind.
Dr. Fluffy, my legs have a lingering ailment; they hurt terribly whenever it rains... Dr. Fluffy would stretch toward the patient, stretching muscles helps relieve soreness.
Dr. Fluffy, he has been gone for three years, but I still can't forget him... Dr. Fluffy would proactively lean in. Human, you can always lean on a fuzzy embrace!
Skeptics who didn't believe in such a divine doctor came to investigate, but they found no medical kits or herbal baskets, only a pile of leftover dried fish.
Strange indeed. A cat cannot practice medicine, yet patients who see Dr. Fluffy always feel a bit better.

zh:
清河百草野，夜半时分有村民见无头将军于将军祠中舞剑，寒芒毕现。还有人听得将军祠中传来陶器破碎的声音。待到天亮，祠中总会莫名出现不少酒坛子。

将军祠是为纪念抵御契丹的将军所建，本该香火不断。可自从将军像没了头，闹鬼的传言愈演愈烈。

附近村中有好事者意图查清这闹鬼真相，便于深夜潜伏在祠堂附近。可他非但没弄清这闹鬼一事，还说自己在祠堂内见到不同的人影。只是那人影来去得太快，待他进了将军祠，又只剩一片寂静。久而久之，村民们又说那人指不定是编了什么谎话来糊弄别人，其实胆子小的很，压根就没去那将军祠。消息传来传去，早已真假难辨。只余将军祠，在风霜中日益破败。
en:
In Verdant Wilds, strange things stirred at the stroke of midnight. The villagers whispered of a headless general, sword in hand, dancing silently within the General's Shrine. His blade, they said, gleamed like frost in the moonlight. Some claimed they heard the crash of pottery from deep inside the shrine. And in the morning, wine jars would appear within the shrine as if conjured from the air.

The shrine had once been a sacred place, built to honor a general who had stood his ground against the Khitan. It should have echoed with solemn prayers, a place of reverence and remembrance. But ever since the statue within lost its head, whispers of spirits and curses had only grown louder.

Drawn by curiosity or perhaps mere foolishness, a villager from nearby began sneaking out at night, hoping to uncover the truth for himself. He claimed to have seen flickering shadows, more than one, dancing just beyond reach. But by the time he rushed inside, the shrine was empty, silent as a tomb. In time, his story was dismissed. Some said he had imagined it all, too frightened to even step past the gates. Like so many others, his tale was swallowed by doubt, its truth blurred beyond recognition. Now the shrine, worn by time and left to decay, stands alone in the wilderness.
Yuecheng Lake

zh:
今日是苏家老夫人七十寿辰，苏府上下铺红结彩，宾客满席，喜气盈天。熙熙攘攘的客席之间，徐州各家名门的艳羡之声不绝于耳。
众人皆在讨论，这苏府不知从何处得了机缘，竟能搭上那传言中不见首亦不见尾的龙王？只是稍借那龙漕帮之势，经掌了一小程盐运，便是一飞冲天，将他们这些郡县豪族远远甩在了身后。
苏府主家老爷已五十岁，仍未去纨绔之气，他万未想到，苏家能在他之手得以中兴。今日老夫人寿辰，甫一开宴，他便喝得满面红光，目眩神迷。苏家老夫人剜了一眼不成器的儿子，而后看向如今真正当家做主的孙女苏婉，方和缓了神色。只是她的目光甫一触到苏婉身边那外姓人，便如遇蛇蝎，脸上尽是毫不遮掩的嫌恶之色。
“龙云天，今日宴上，苏婉自有她的事情要处置。苏府大事，你一外姓人不必知道，回厢房暂避就是！”
却说那龙云天，剑眉星目，面容瘦削，天然便带一股冷意。今日头发未得打理，随意束起，更带了几分江湖气。这样的男子，听闻大庭广众此等折辱之言，竟未做一声。他即是苏家赘婿，外人皆称，他将成苏婉一生之败笔。
龙云天望向苏婉，昔日百般不入苏老夫人之眼的女流之辈，如今尽得苏家权柄与敬爱的苏家主事，他的那位妻子。她如毫无所闻，仍言笑晏晏，与徐州别驾那私生子罗逢相谈甚欢。苏婉已尽数忘了，她被苏家逐出府去的落魄之时，是谁与她同舟共济。又是谁甘愿背赘婿之名，入府助她掌家族之权。
龙云天抬起眸子，恢复了些昔日的气度，他望向那高座之上的苏老夫人，言语之间尽是讥讽：“老夫人，你这是要给你家孙女，介绍一个私生子夫婿？我龙某是赘婿不假，却也不是死了！”
一时之间，满座哗然。
苏婉立马回身，怒目望向龙云天。望着宾客议论声起，苏婉强压怒气，冷冷劝慰：“夫君何出此言？你为赘婿，老夫人令你回避也无碍古礼。你怎可信口胡言，于这寿宴之上顶撞她老人家？”
“古礼……古礼？哈哈哈哈哈，好一个古礼！你可还记得，你被这老妖婆以女流之辈不得介入家业为由，逐出府外之时，是谁接济于你，甘愿以赘婿之名入苏府，与你共抗这古礼？”
苏老夫人大惊，怒指龙云天，恨不得当场要左右拿其性命：“狂悖之徒！狂悖之徒！我与婉婉皆是苏家人，前尘旧事，心结已解。如今婉婉治理家业，我苏家将成世家，你一外人，竟如此挑拨离间？”
苏老夫人望向苏婉，见苏婉亦现愠怒之色，终于安下心来。
“我与祖奶为一家，血浓于水，其又为长辈，你安敢作此不肖之言？看来我苏婉确实有眼无珠，你若要离府，我便遂你心意！来人，备纸墨，今日我苏婉，便在诸位名门见证之下，休了这不肖狂悖之徒！从此我苏婉，与这龙云天，再无瓜葛！”
————————欲知后事如何，且听下回分解——————————
en:
Today marks the seventieth birthday of Matriarch Su. The entire Homestead is draped in festive crimson, a sea of lanterns and silks radiating joy to the heavens.
Guests huddle in hushed conversation: how did the Sus, of all people, secure the favor of the Dragon King of the Dragon Tide Clan? Word on the street is that by riding the coattails of the Dragon Tide Clan, they've seized a portion of the salt trade. That single move sent them soaring, leaving Xuzhou's local gentry scrambling in their wake.
Patriarch Su, a man of fifty who has yet to outgrow his hedonistic streaks, is lost in a drunken haze, his face flushed with the pride of a family reborn. The Matriarch shoots a scathing look at her useless son and then turns to her granddaughter, Su Wan, the true power behind the family. Only then does her gaze soften. But as her eyes drift to the outsider standing beside Su Wan, they narrow with venomous spite.
"Long Yuntian, Su Wan has serious matters to attend to. No place for an outsider. Withdraw to the guest wing now!"
This Long Yuntian possesses a sharp, ascetic face with eyes like distant stars, radiating a natural, frigid aura. His unkempt hair, bound loosely today, lends him an air of the wild, untamed jianghu. Despite the public humiliation, he remains silent. He is the matrilocal groom of the Sus. To the world, he is the greatest blemish on Su Wan's otherwise perfect life.
Long Yuntian's gaze falls on Su Wan, the woman who has once been cast aside by the matriarch but now stands at the center of power, the de facto head of the Su family. She acts as if he didn't exist, her face bright with charm as she shares a laugh with Luo Feng, the illegitimate son of the Vice-Governor, as if she'd completely forgotten who stood by her when she was thrown out of the Su Homestead in disgrace, who willingly took on the humiliating label of the matrilocal groom just so she could reclaim control of the family.
Long Yuntian raises his head, the suppressed dignity of his past resurfacing. His voice drips with cold irony: "Tell me, Matriarch, is this your plan? To pimp out your granddaughter to a bastard? I'm still Su Wan's husband, whether you like it or not."
A ripple of shock and murmurs sweeps through the hall.
Su Wan spins around, her eyes blazing as they lock onto Long Yuntian. Sensing the guests' prying eyes, Su Wan suppresses her fury. "Enough! For a matrilocal groom, obeying the Matriarch is the highest propriety. How dare you hurl such reckless insults on her very birthday?"
"Propriety? Ha! A fine word for it! Do you forget, Su Wan? When that old crone cast you out, claiming a woman had no place in the family business, who stood by you? Who took the brand of the 'matrilocal groom' just to fight that very 'propriety' by your side?"
The Matriarch trembles, her finger jabbing the air at him. "You insolent cur! Wan and I are of one blood; the past is buried. Now that she leads our house to greatness, how dare you, a mere outsider, to sow discord?"
The Matriarch glances at Su Wan and, seeing the anger flash across her granddaughter's face, finally relaxes.
"Blood is thicker than your lies. How dare you spout such filth against your elders? Bring paper and ink! Today, before all the honored guests, I, Su Wan, sever our ties. We're done from this day forth!"
To find out what happens next, stay tuned for the next episode.

哼，人类就是小气！不给猫吃，猫就自己去找。
树叶苦苦的，咸鱼硬硬的。脆脆找了好久，累得躺在草里，都没有找到脆脆的东西。
暖风吹得猫猫醉，脆脆渐渐觉得睡一觉也是不错的选择。眼睛刚刚闭上，脆脆的脸上好似停了什么东西，走动起来挠得它痒痒的。
脆脆用爪子一抓，把东西拍到嘴里；再咬上一口，猫眼随之瞪大：脆脆的！脆脆赶忙将它吐了出来，仔细端详还剩下半只的小零食。
好，以后脆脆就吃这个了！
en:
What makes it crispy when you bite?
Crispy would watch the humans eat their tiny treats, their mouths making a glorious krrr-unch, krrr-unch sound. It'd beg, but they'd shoo it away. "Not for cats!" they'd say.
Hmph, humans were so stingy! If they wouldn't share, it'd find its own.
But the leaves were bitter. Salted fish was hard. Tired and defeated, it flopped into the grass, ready to give up and nap.
Just as its eyes closed, a tickle landed on its cheek. With a swift paw, it batted the tickle into its mouth. It bit down. Its eyes shot open. CRISPY! It spat it out, staring at the half-a-bug left on the ground.
Aha. Crispy had found his crispy.

zh:
军械库？那是什么地方？
他没有听下去什么石守信的话，也没有看见石守信眼中的一点苦心。
他只知道那是一个不见天日的地方，那是一个见不得人的秘密，而他要去做那个秘密的守门人。

可是，那他的志向呢，他的抱负呢，他的耻辱呢，他的荣誉呢，黑暗是不能洗刷黑暗的，地下是不能为荣誉卫冕的，在推杯换盏中摆弄钱财，在黑暗中交换秘密，如何能抵消肩上的力道。
为什么是我？为什么选我？
可大多事情，不论你是王侯将相，还是平头百姓，最不堪问的一句便是：为何是我？

石贞曾以为他身边还有许多人，他为自己活，也为许多人活，可回头看，他却只能看见自己的脚印，从来没有人站在他这边，他想到，就因为他是降将之子，——就因为他是降将之子。
世上的不平用刀剑尚且可杀，心中的不平又该如何杀呢。
他不会再有那一日了。
他不会再有——

不、能杀，心中的不平能杀。
他看向面前的军械库，里面不摆满了刀剑吗？地下的刀剑，终有一日能回到地面之上。
地下的人，终有一日能回到地面之上。
en:
"The Shadow Arsenal? What kind of place is that?"
He didn't listen to Shi Shouxin's explanations. Didn't see the flicker of deliberate intent in the old general's eyes.
All he knew was that it was a place without sunlight, a shameful secret, and he was being made its keeper.

But what of his ambition? His honor? His shame? Darkness could not wash away darkness. The underground could not defend glory. Manipulating money over drinks, trading secrets in the shadows, how could any of this counter the weight on his shoulders?
Why me? Why choose me?
But for most things, whether you're a lord or a commoner, the most futile question is: Why me?

Shi Zhen had thought he had people beside him, that he lived for both himself and others. But looking back, he saw only his own footprints. No one had ever stood with him. Because he was the son of a traitor, that was why.
The world's injustices could be fought with swords, but how does one battle the injustice in their own heart?
That day will never come.

Never... No. Injustice in the heart can be fought.
He stared at the Shadow Arsenal before him. Wasn't it filled with swords and blades? One day, those underground blades would see the light. One day, those who dwell in the dark would stand in the sun again.
The pain... It's killing me...!

en:
Participate in the 5v5 Arena to make friends through martial arts. In this 5v5 competitive mode, players can form teams of five to engage in strategic battles.
5v5 Arena entry is available from @T[time_19:45] to @T[time_20]. Be sure to join in on time. Once the match begins, up to four teams with similar ranking points will be grouped into a round-robin bracket. Each group will play three matches, with each match using a best-of-three format. Teams that win a match will earn Season Points and Engagement tokens.

In this mode, healing effects are reduced by 70%. After a certain time in battle, players will deal increased damage while healing effectiveness is further reduced. Using the "Deflection" skill consumes Endurance, but successfully executing a finisher restores it.

Most player skills can be countered using "Deflection." However, Armor-Piercing Mystic Skills can't be blocked this way and are especially effective against defensive targets or those using "Deflection"—though they can be interrupted by any skill.

Various player skills (including Mystic Skills and Charged Skills) can interrupt light and heavy attacks, but not the other way around.

Mastering crowd-control removal skills can turn the tide of battle when at a disadvantage.

The side that defeats all players of the other first within the time limit wins. If the timer runs out without a decisive outcome, the winner is determined by the following priorities: 1. The side with more surviving players wins; 2. If the number of surviving players is equal, the side with the higher total damage dealt wins; 3. If the total damage dealt is equal, the side with the higher total healing amount wins.

Alas, I have already arrived in Kaifeng, and shall not make it back in time to try the ice chest, so I intend to visit the Kaifeng Arsenal instead, to see what fine methods they might have for storing fire arrows. 但真正见到寒香寻本人时，千夜却有一瞬的恍惚。
她想不起在哪里见过这张脸，又或者从未见过，只是觉得面善。
这个女子，方才从她身后掷出一枚小小的石子，掷在那个年轻人额头上。
而她竟毫无察觉。
面对功夫了得又藏得这样深的江湖人，刚才她那一瞬间的恍惚，便足以致命。
千夜是从死人堆中摸爬滚打出来的，这道理她不是不知道，只是……
对着面前这个女人，她刚刚依然如初入江湖一般。

那个女人给她斟酒，带来似有若无的梨花香气。
“听说这里叫不羡仙，是愿作鸳鸯不羡仙的不羡仙吗？”
“是人间团圆不羡仙。”
她们一个扮演柔弱的独身酒客，一个扮演泯然众人的客栈老板。一来一回，难辨真心。
千夜突然觉得，面前的人与她很像。
都这样想要隐藏起过去、隐藏起心里的秘密，装作世界上另一个人。
纵使寒香寻确实藏得很好，但千夜就是一眼看穿。
说不上原因，只是仿佛她们之间有丝线相连，注定要相遇、靠近，感同身受、纠缠不休。
千夜低头看寒香寻为她斟的酒。
或许是寒香寻一时不察，将一根发丝落在酒杯和她的手上。乌黑，细碎，轻盈，似乎一吹就可以飘走。
细看片刻，仰头，一饮而尽。
千夜见过许多极美的女子，但这番沉醉其中的感受，还是第一次。
一定是杯中的酒太烈了。
这算什么，一见如故，还是一见倾心？
都无所谓，既然喜欢，那便……毁掉吧。
“这位姐姐，不如坐下来，与千夜共饮一杯。”
千夜讨厌梨花，讨厌这个到处祥和一无是处的客栈，但她决定在不羡仙多待一会儿。
毕竟，这样的酒，来年喝不到了，这样的人，来年也见不到了，真是可惜。
en:
When Qianye first entered Blissful Retreat, the sight of pear blossoms overwhelmed her, like an eternal snowfall that refused to melt.
Beautiful. Yet she hated pear blossoms the most.
She'd heard the Heaven's Pier owner planted them all.
This woman called it the Blissful Retreat for all these pear blossoms in Heaven's Pier.
What a ridiculous wish. What arrogance.
Amusing enough... to make her want to burn every last white petal along with that naive woman.

Yet when she finally faced Han Xiangxun, Qianye froze.
That face? Had she seen it before? Or was it simply familiar?
This woman just flicked a pebble at a young man's forehead from behind Qianye's back.
Without her noticing.
Against a swordsman this skilled and concealed, such hesitation could be fatal.
Qianye knew this for she'd clawed her way from piles of corpses.
Yet before this woman... she'd faltered like a novice.

The woman poured her wine, carrying a whisper of pear blossom scent."
They say this place is called 'Blissful Retreat', like the poem about mandarin ducks preferring love over immortality?"
"No," came the reply. "It's about mortal reunions making immortality worthless."
One played the fragile lone drinker, the other an unremarkable innkeeper, their exchange a dance of concealed truths.
Qianye suddenly realized: this woman was just like her.
Both hiding their pasts and their secrets, pretending to be someone else entirely.
Han Xiangxun's disguise might fool others, but Qianye saw through it instantly.
No reason. Just like an invisible thread pulling them together, they were destined to meet, to understand, to entangle.
Qianye looked down at the wine Han Xiangxun poured.
A strand of Han Xiangxun's hair had fallen between the cup and her hand, black, delicate, ready to vanish with a breath.
She studied it, then drank deeply.
She'd known many beautiful women, but this intoxication was new. Must be strong liquor.
What was this? Kindred spirits at first sight? Or something more?
It didn't matter. When she liked something... she destroyed it.
"Sister, won't you sit and drink with me?"
Qianye hated pear blossoms, hated this idyllic, worthless inn. Yet she'd stay awhile at Blissful Retreat.
After all... such wine wouldn't exist next year. Neither would this woman. What a shame.

zh: 《兰陵王入阵曲》为古代歌舞戏，起于北齐，盛于唐代，为歌颂兰陵王的英勇善战所作。《北齐书·卷十一·列传三》中记载：“突厥入晋阳，长恭尽力击之。邙山之战，长恭为中军，率五百骑再入周军，遂至金墉下，被围甚急，城上人弗识，长恭免胄示之面，乃下弩手救之，于是大捷。武士共歌谣之，为兰陵王入阵曲是也。”
en: The Prince Enters the Formation is an ancient song and dance drama that originated in the Northern Qi and flourished in the Tang Dynasty, composed to praise the bravery of the Prince of Lanling. Book of Northern Qi records: "When the Turks entered Jinyang, Gao Changgong fought them with all his might. In the Battle of Mount Mang, Changgong led five hundred riders into the Zhou army twice, reaching the gates of Jinyong. The siege was urgent, and those on the wall did not recognize him until he removed his helmet to show his face, after which archers were sent to save him, leading to a great victory. The soldiers composed a song for him, which is The Prince Enters the Formation."

zh:
"在她成为青之前，不过是个没有姓名的女娃娃。
生于烽火连天的年月，父母在乱世里奔命，无心亦无力予她名姓。绝境中，生母褪下贴身的青色布衫，将她细细裹好，塞进一方窄小黑匣，放之水上，任其随波漂流。 
一别永别，但被母亲最后的体温拥抱着，竟也温暖。许是天意垂怜，水流未将她送往死路，倒真闯出一片生机来。
河边浣衣的妇人听匣中啼哭清亮，拾其作养女。奈何好景难长，她还没讨来个名字，偏又遇上饥荒。为了能让两个人都活下去，年幼的她寻至传说中万物可估的江湖牙郎处——在那人眼里，人鸟物兽，都有价格。
乱世之中人命轻贱，她的命一开始不过值三根珍禽的羽毛。
她却攥紧稚拳，朝牙郎挥去。她偏要证己之价——武斗之价、卖命之价。最终，她为养母换回一袋钱、一枚莹润白玉。
而她自此随牙郎行走江湖。

牙郎曾说，正因她无姓无名，方生出一身与天相争的胆魄。无名之人，纵使触怒天公，天公欲降罚时也会寻不着人，只得空响几声雷霆罢了。
牙郎赏识她这股不惜命的劲儿，在她九岁那年，交予其一桩无人敢接的买卖——要她去杀墨山道一位至关重要的人物。
她捧着牙郎丢来的行踪图迹，在图注必经之路上苦候半月，饮风露，攀岩壁，终见目标——呀！怎竟也是个孩子，比她尚幼两三岁的模样。人命轻贱，她要随波而下，也做那轻贱人命之事么？
她想着牙郎的恩情，想着昨晚只舍得吃一半的小鲹鱼，稳下心神悄步靠近。却见那男孩正用一柄削尖的木匕，小心翼翼地翻拨着眼前缠结的乱藤。
“哦……木头脑袋，这般要弄到何时？用我的！”
看清他在做什么后，她想也未想，就递出了自己的铁匕。男孩坦然接过，仿佛二人并非初见。他持匕的动作依旧轻缓，只为不伤及那藤中困鸟。
那个午后，两把刀，两个孩子，愣是拆尽了密密匝匝的乱藤。
一只鸟儿冲天而去，两道命数自此交汇。
至于那墨山道重要人物的性命，她自是未能取回……日落时，她见到来接男孩的垂钓客，方才察觉自己找错了人。那钓者似是知道她为何而来，却笑问她名姓，问她愿不愿随他回山。回山是回哪里？是在这样糟烂的世上，却人人都还能费心救鸟的地方吗？

她想去，但她得先偿清这些年牙郎的养育授艺之恩。十五日，再给她十五日便足够。
她替牙郎干了桩更大的买卖，诛了作恶一方的匪寨头领；又到林子里猎了几张豺皮给牙郎过冬，方才离去。
十六日，她赶到约定的城南石桥下，随新的师父去往那能叫世道变好的地方。

只可惜，那些对她有恩的山野之人，纵她后来寻遍四方，也再未见过了。
此后岁月，她历经诸事，件件以血为注，一生不曾停步。
然也因入了这墨山道，她才真正有了名姓。
世人从此称她为——
青。"
en:
Before she became Halcyon, she was a girl without a name.
She was born into the chaos of war. Her parents were too consumed by the struggle to survive to give her a name.
In desperation, her mother stripped off her own azure tunic, wrapped her daughter with tender care, and placed her inside a small dark chest, setting it adrift upon the water to go wherever the current would take it.
A final farewell, and yet, cradled in the last warmth her mother had left behind, she felt something strangely close to comfort.

Perhaps Heaven took pity on her: the current did not carry her to her death, but to a chance at life. A woman washing clothes by the river heard the crying from within the chest and took the infant in as her foster daughter. But fortune is fleeting. Before the child could even be given a name, famine came.
To keep them both alive, the young girl sought out a legendary broker of the jianghu, a man said to place a price on anything in the world. In his eyes, beast and man were worth exactly what they could fetch.

In times of chaos, life was cheap. At first, hers was worth no more than three feathers from a rare bird.
But she clenched her small fists and swung at him. She would prove her worth: the price of her fighting, the price of her life.
In the end, she earned her foster mother a pouch of coins and a sliver of lustrous white jade. From that day on, she traveled the jianghu at the broker's side.

The broker once told her that it was because she had no name that she had the audacity to go against fate. A nameless soul, even if she angered the Heavens, would leave the gods with nothing to strike down, and they'd have no choice but to let the thunder roll and go quiet.
Impressed by her fearlessness, the broker gave her a task at the age of nine that no one else would take: to assassinate a key figure of Mohist Hill.
She took the maps he tossed her and waited half a month along the appointed path, sleeping under open skies, scaling cliff faces, until she finally caught sight of her target.
And then she stopped.

He was just a child, two or three years younger than herself. In a world where life meant so little, was she really going to become someone who treated it the same way?
She thought of the broker's kindness. She remembered how she'd allowed herself only half a small fish the night before.
She steadied herself and crept closer without a sound.
The boy was using a sharpened wooden dagger to carefully pry apart a tangled knot of vines.
"Ugh, you dummy... at this rate you'll be here all day. Here, use mine."
Before she even knew what she was doing, she had handed him her iron dagger.
The boy took it without any surprise, as if they had known each other for years.
Even with the better blade, his movements stayed slow and gentle, taking care not to harm the bird caught inside the vines.

That afternoon, two children and two knives worked through every last tangle. A bird burst into the sky, and two fates became bound together.
She never took that life.

At sunset, an angler arrived to collect the boy, and she realized she had the wrong person entirely.
The angler seemed to know exactly why she had come, yet he only smiled, asked for her name, and asked if she would come back to the mountains with him.

Back where?
To a place where, even in a world this broken, people would still stop to save a single bird?
She wanted to go. But she had to repay the broker first, for everything he had given her.

Fifteen days. Give her fifteen more days.
She completed a bigger job for him, killing a bandit chief who had plagued the region for years.
She hunted several jackals in the forest and brought back the pelts to keep him warm through winter.
Then she left.

On the sixteenth day, she arrived at the stone bridge south of the city and followed her new master toward a place where the world might be made better.
It was a shame: no matter how far she searched in the years that followed, she never found those kind souls from the mountains again.

The years after were hard ones, every step paid for in blood. She never stopped moving. But it was on Mohist Hill that she finally received a name.
From that day on, the world knew her as Halcyon.
Jian Dada

zh:

鸡历来被视为司时之畜，即司掌时间的动物。古时有专人模仿鸡的叫声，来进行报时的职业。这类人被称为鸡人。到了宋代，鸡人发明出了专门的唱词，在作词上兼具了教化的作用，使原本单纯的报时，有了表演的性质。
en:
As the keeper of time, it crows thrice without fail. 

The rooster has long been regarded as the animal that governs time. In ancient times, certain people made a profession out of imitating rooster calls to announce the time. These individuals were known as "chicken-men". By the Song dynasty, chicken-men had developed specific chants that combined education with performance, turning a simple timekeeping task into a stylized act.

zh: 病起萧萧两鬓华，卧看残月上窗纱。豆蔻连梢煎熟水，莫分茶。饮子一词出现在唐代，最早指汤药，到了宋朝演变为养生之水，又称“熟水”。《事林广记》中记载，“白豆蔻壳捡净，投入沸汤瓶中，密封片时用之。”饮之化湿消痞，开胃消食。李清照便是因晚年体弱，常年以“豆蔻饮”代茶，写下了《白豆蔻熟水》一词。

Fuxi Jr. has been with its owner since it was tiny. Time has passed without either of them noticing, until Fuxi's beard turned streaked with gray and Fuxi Jr. itself grew into a big cat.

People say Fuxi was too lazy to give it a proper name. Fuxi Jr. knows that's not it.
Call out "Fuxi", and both the man and the cat come at once. Two hearts pressed close, two lives tied together, and Fuxi Jr. can't help but feel pleased.

When the moon hangs high, Fuxi pours a bowl of wine. He takes a sip, and Fuxi Jr. takes a lick. The warmth spreads through them as they lean into each other.

Night fades into day, then day into night. Junior's life always feels light, as if it could drift.
People say that feeling is called happiness.

Big bruther, a few munths ago, while Muther was cuting weeds in the feild, she looked up at the sun which was very lite, and accidently fell down the slope. Now Muther canot see anithing, and she only thinks of you. The new yeer is almost here. Yur yungest brother asks, will you come home?)

zh:
康宝是一位商人，但是基本上没有人能从他这里买到东西。因为她认为每件物品都有其"命定价值"，不是所有人都有资格拥有它们，因此她的买卖都遵循着一套定律，即售卖的商品都没有明确的价格，顾客必须说出他们认为物品“值多少钱“，只有当顾客说出的价格与康宝心中认定的"真值"完全一致时，交易才能达成。而康宝的估值并非只依据市场价，而是她对于物品的主观情感、商品的内涵和潜在价值的评估。由于这种几乎不可能达成的条件，几乎没有人能从她手中带走商品。

是一些奇怪的出人意料的东西，比如自己的眼泪（廉价，因为自己经常哭）、比如一罐干净的空气（偏贵，因为玉门常起风沙）、比如一位大侠踩过的沙粒（昂贵，因为觉得大侠很酷）
en:
Kang Bao is a merchant, but hardly anyone can buy anything from her. She believes every item has its "destined value," and not everyone is qualified to possess them. Thus, her sales follow a strict rule, her goods have no fixed price, customers must state what they think the item is worth. Only when the customer's stated price exactly matches the true value in Kang Bao's mind will the transaction proceed. Kang Bao's valuation is not based on market price alone but on her subjective emotions toward the item, its intrinsic meaning, and its potential worth. Due to this nearly impossible condition, almost no one ever manages to purchase anything from her. 

They are some strange and unexpected things, like one's own tears (cheap, because one often cries), a jar of clean air (somewhat expensive, because sandstorms are frequent at Jade Gate), or grains of sand stepped on by a great hero (expensive, because heroes are considered cool).

zh:
阿大曾问我：知道为什么我们要一直迁徙吗？
我摇了摇头，阿大摸着我的脑袋，对我说：
因为要活。我们窣利人是为利而生的，哪里有黄金，便到哪里去。
从出生的那一刻开始，就注定要奔忙不息。
我问阿大：那我们就不能停下来吗？
阿大看了看远方，良久才叹息一句：
那样的能停下的地方，再也没有了。
珍珠，你要记住，商队里的人想要吃饱饭，脚要足够勤，心要足够冷。
生意场上，不要生感性的心思，不然你走不远。
我一直牢记着阿大的话。
后来，我遇到了一帮唐军。
他们的铠甲破烂不堪，连刀身都卷了刃。
我在大漠做过多年的生意，一眼便知道，做这样的生意最不易。
这群唐军驻守的河西孤悬已久。而波陈人把这里当成肥肉，耽耽虎视。
生意无利，商人便不会前行。交易的两端，合该有对等的分量。
可我想不到他们坚守的任何理由，坚守至绝境，对他们而言一样是笔做不得的生意。还能有什么比活着更紧要么？
看着那位青年将军，我没忍住，还是向他问了话——
你们怎么不走呢，走了不就能活吗？
他指着不远处的胡杨，眼神坚毅且明亮：
只要根扎得足够深，就能活下去。
胡杨若活下去，更多的人就能活下去。
en:
My patar once asked me, "Marga, do you know why we must wander all our lives?"
I shook my head. He stroked my hair and said,
"To survive. We Sogdians are born to chase profit—where the gold is, that's where we go. From the moment you're born, you are destined for a life of ceaseless travel."
"Then can't we ever stop?" I asked.
He gazed into the distance and, after a long silence, sighed. "A place where we could stop... such places are gone for us."
"Marga, remember this: in a caravan, to keep your belly full, your feet must be swift and your heart must be hard. Business is business. Sentiment will be your ruin. It won't let you get far."
I never forgot his words.

Years later, I came across a troop of Tang soldiers.
Their armor was in tatters, their blades chipped and dull. With my years of trade in the great desert, I knew at a glance: any dealings with them would be utterly profitless.
This troop had been stranded in Hexi for a long time, and the Bodchens watched them like wolves circling a prize. Where there is no profit, a merchant does not go. A trade must have equal weight on both sides of the scale.
I could not fathom any reason for them to hold their ground. To defend a lost cause was, to them, a bargain with no return. Is anything in this world worth more than survival itself?
Looking at the young general, I couldn't hold back my question:
"Why don't you leave? If you leave, you survive."
He pointed to the desert poplars nearby, his gaze unwavering and bright.
"As long as the roots run deep enough, we will live."
"And if the poplars live, more people will get to live because of them."

en:

No one in Mirkvale has ever traveled far, so he comes to you for help. "You've been to so many places," he says. "Have you ever heard a melody, one so beautiful, so unforgettable, that it lingers in your heart forever?"
Yes, of course: #Y[The spring river tide meets the sea level, and the bright moon rises with the tide.] When he hears it, Xiaoba looks up and nods his little bronze head.#E
You begin to sing, and Xiaoba's little bronze head starts swaying gently from side to side, utterly lost in the music.
"It's so, so, so, so beautiful!" he blurts out the moment you finish.
A melody like that belongs in nothing less than his newly upgraded music box.
Not long afterward, Xiaoba invites you to admire his latest masterpiece!
This time, he has fitted the music box into a rocket and then strapped the rocket to himself.

en:
Inkbound Order has opened elementary learning all across the Central Plains, and the results have been striking. But the Mohist arts of construction and the principles of investigating things are obscure by nature, and until now have been passed down only through master-disciple transmission and years of travel and study, so those who learn them remain few. My good friend Meng Liangshi, at Lone Cloud, felt that the methods of mathematics and astronomy in his own school faced the same concern.

In the third year of Tianfu, I came to Dragonbend Mountain. With the support of Inkbound Order and Lone Cloud, Dragonbend Academy was founded. Students were admitted from far and wide, and the learning of patterns and principles was taught, in the hope that all might understand reason, all might possess skill, and thus help learning flourish throughout the realm. This register is set down in the hope that all whose names appear here may one day make something of themselves.

西坊有民，名丁璞，性甚固，人皆恶之。
丁璞者，本侠客也，后娶妻西坊。其人甚刚，万夫莫折；瘦而骨立，志气非凡。开运三年十二月，契丹入汴。丁璞从战，乃入九流门，为契丹所伤，数日间，时昏时醒，遂疯癫。日月逾迈，荏苒十五载有余。
今朝廷以金明池五牙大舰之故，欲改西坊为百工坊，徙工巧于其处。居民悉迁，璞拒之，终不肯徙，为官吏所苦。
en:
In West Market lived a man named Ding Pu, so stubborn that everyone disliked him.
Ding Pu had once been a Swordsman, later marrying into West Market. He was unyielding in spirit, capable of withstanding any pressure; though lean and gaunt, his resolve was extraordinary. In December of the 3rd year of the Kaiyun era, the Khitan forces invaded Bianliang (Kaifeng). Ding Pu joined the battle and became a member of the Nine Mortal Ways, but was wounded by the Khitan. For days, he alternated between delirium and lucidity, eventually going insane. Fifteen years have passed since then.
Now, due to the construction of the Quintadent Warships at Jinming Pool, the imperial court intends to transform West Market into the Imperial Artisan Court and relocate artisans to the area. All residents were ordered to move, but Ding Pu refused to comply and steadfastly refused to relocate, enduring persecution from officials.

zh:
【颂·商颂】

那
猗与那与！置我鞉鼓。
奏鼓简简，衎我烈祖。
汤孙奏假，绥我思成。
鞉鼓渊渊，嘒嘒管声。
既和且平，依我磬声。
於赫汤孙！穆穆厥声。
庸鼓有斁，万舞有奕。
我有嘉客，亦不夷怿。
自古在昔，先民有作。
温恭朝夕，执事有恪，
顾予烝尝，汤孙之将。

烈祖

嗟嗟烈祖！有秩斯祜。
申锡无疆，及尔斯所。
既载清酤，赉我思成。
亦有和羹，既戒既平。
鬷假无言，时靡有争。
绥我眉寿，黄耇无疆。
约軝错衡，八鸾鸧鸧。
以假以享，我受命溥将。
自天降康，丰年穰穰。
来假来飨，降福无疆。
顾予烝尝，汤孙之将。

玄鸟

天命玄鸟，降而生商，宅殷土芒芒。古帝命武汤，正域彼四方。
方命厥后，奄有九有。商之先后，受命不殆，在武丁孙子。武丁孙子，武王靡不胜。
龙旂十乘，大糦是承。邦畿千里，维民所止，肇域彼四海。
四海来假，来假祁祁。景员维河。殷受命咸宜，百禄是何。
……
en:
【Ode·Shang Hymns】 How grand, how glorious! They set up our drums. The drums resound, delighting our forefathers. The descendant of Tang offers prayers, granting us success. The drums rumble deep, the flutes pipe shrill. Harmonious and serene, they follow our stone chimes. Majestic is the descendant of Tang! Solemn is his music. The bells and drums resound, the myriad dances are splendid. We have honored guests, who are filled with joy. From ancient times, our ancestors set the precedent. Gentle and reverent from dawn to dusk, they served with devotion, Looking upon our autumn and winter sacrifices, offered by the descendant of Tang. Glorious Ancestor Ah, glorious ancestor! Boundless is this blessing. Endless gifts bestowed, reaching to your domain. The clear wine is prepared, granting us success. There is also seasoned broth, well-prepared and balanced. In silence we offer prayers, without strife or discord. Grant us longevity, may we live to old age without end. Ornate chariots with jingling bells, eight luan bells chiming.

We come to offer sacrifices, receiving the mandate vast and enduring. From heaven descends peace, bringing bountiful harvests. Come and enjoy the offerings, bestow blessings without limit. Looking upon our autumn and winter sacrifices, offered by the descendant of Tang. Mystic Bird Heaven commanded the Mystic Bird, descending to birth the Shang, dwelling in the vast land of Yin. The ancient emperor commanded the martial Tang, to govern the four corners of the realm. He commanded his successors, who held all nine regions. The former kings of Shang, receiving the mandate without faltering, in the descendants of Wu Ding. The descendants of Wu Ding, the martial king, none could defeat. With dragon banners and ten chariots, they bore the great offerings. The royal domain stretched a thousand li, where the people dwelt, extending to the four seas. From the four seas they came, came in multitudes. The Jing mountains and the Yellow River. Yin received the mandate fittingly, bearing all blessings. ……

世宗年间，时人信佛成风，寺庙三万所，铜佛十万身。清河一带，崇信之风以千佛村最盛，信仰之热烈，几近于疯魔。有名为妙善的远游之僧来此，于村外呼喊，称千佛村所信乃伪善，劝人悔过。村人不信，驱离妙善。然妙善走后，千佛村突降天火，全村陷于火海之中。一村尽焚。
从此，此地便成了一片焦土，了无生机。夜半幽静之时，常有人听到千佛村废墟传来呜呜的哭声，不知是否是当年的村民，亡魂未息。
en:
During the reign of Emperor Shizong, Buddhism flourished to such an extent that there were thirty thousand temples and one hundred thousand bronze buddha statues. Nowhere was this devotion more fanatical than in Thousand-Buddha Village near Qinghe. When Miaoshan, a wandering monk, came here and proclaimed outside the village that their faith was hypocrisy, urging them to repent, the villagers drove him away. But after Miaoshan left, heavenly fire suddenly descended, engulfing the entire village in flames. Not a single house was spared. 
Since then, the area has remained scorched earth, lifeless. On quiet midnight hours, people often hear wailing cries from the ruins of Thousand-Buddha Village—perhaps the restless spirits of the villagers, unable to find peace.
