zh:
【公冶长第五】

子谓公冶长：“可妻也。虽在缧绁之中，非其罪也。”以其子妻之。
子谓南容：“邦有道，不废；邦无道，免于刑戮。”以其兄之子妻之。
子谓子贱：“君子哉若人！鲁无君子者，斯焉取斯？”
子贡问曰：“赐也如何？”子曰：“汝，器也。”曰：“何器也？”曰：“瑚琏也。”
或曰：“雍也仁而不佞。”子曰：“焉用佞也？御人以给，屡憎民，不知其仁也，焉用佞也？”
子使漆雕开仕，对曰：“吾斯之未能信。”子说。
子曰：“道不行，乘桴浮于海。从我者，其由也与？”子路闻之喜。子曰：“由也，好勇过我，无所取材。”
孟武伯问：“子路仁乎？”子曰：“不知也。”又问，子曰：“由也，千乘之国，可使治其赋也，不知其仁也。”“求也何如？”子曰：“求也，千室之邑，百乘之家，可使为之宰也，不知其仁也。”“赤也何如？”子曰：“赤也，束带立于朝，可使与宾客言也，不知其仁也。”
子谓子贡曰：“女与回也孰愈？”对曰：“赐也何敢望回？回也闻一以知十，赐也闻一以知二。”子曰：“弗如也。吾与女弗如也。”
宰予昼寝。子曰：“朽木不可雕也，粪土之墙不可杇也，于予与何诛？”子曰：“始吾于人也，听其言而信其行；今吾于人也，听其言而观其行。于予与改是。”
子曰：“吾未见刚者。或对曰：“申枨。子曰：“枨也欲，焉得刚？”
子贡曰：“我不欲人之加诸我也，吾亦欲无加诸人也。子曰：“赐也，非尔所及也。”
子贡曰：“夫子之文章，可得而闻也。 夫子之言性与天道，不可得而闻也已矣。”
子路有闻，未能行，唯恐有闻。
子贡问曰：“孔文子何以谓之‘文’也？”子曰：“敏而好学，不耻下问，是以谓之‘文’也。”
子谓子产：“有君子之道四焉：其行己也恭，其事上也敬，其养民也惠，其使民也义。”
子曰：“晏平仲善与人交，久而人敬之。”
子曰：“臧文仲居蔡，山节藻棁，何如其知也？”
子张问曰：“令尹子文三仕为令尹，无喜色。三已之，无愠色。旧令尹之政，必以告新令尹，何如也？”子曰：“忠矣。”曰：“仁矣乎？”曰：“未知，焉得仁？”“崔子弑齐君，陈文子有马十乘，弃而违之。至于他邦，则又曰：‘犹吾大夫崔子也。’违之。至一邦，则又曰：‘犹吾大夫崔子也。’违之，何如？”子曰：“清矣。”曰：“仁矣乎？”曰：“未知。焉得仁？”
季文子三思而后行。子闻之，曰：“再，斯可矣。”
子曰：“宁武子邦有道则知，邦无道则愚。其知可及也，其愚不可及也。”
子在陈，曰：“归与！归与！吾党之小子狂简，斐然成章，不知所以裁之也。”
子曰：“伯夷、叔齐不念旧恶，怨是用希。”
子曰：“孰谓微生高直？或乞醯焉，乞诸其邻而与之。”
子曰：“巧言、令色、足恭，左丘明耻之，丘亦耻之。匿怨而友其人，左丘明耻之，丘亦耻之。”
颜渊、季路侍。子曰：“盍各曰尔志？”子路曰：“愿车马，衣轻裘，与朋友共，敝之而无憾。”颜渊曰：“愿无伐善，无施劳。”子路曰：“愿闻子之志。”子曰：“老者安之，朋友信之，少者怀之。”
子曰：“已矣乎！吾未见能见其过而内自讼者也。”
子曰：“十室之邑，必有忠信如丘者焉，不如丘之好学者也。”
en:
【Book V: Gongye Chang】

The Master said of Gongye Chang, "He is a suitable man to marry. Though he was once bound in fetters, it was through no fault of his." He gave him his daughter in marriage.
The Master said of Nan Rong, "When the state is well governed, he is not cast aside; when the state is ill governed, he escapes punishment and disgrace." He gave him his elder brother's daughter in marriage.
The Master said of Zijian, "A true gentleman is this man! If there were no gentlemen in Lu, how could he have acquired this virtue?"
Zigong asked, "What do you think of me?" The Master said, "You are a vessel." "What kind of vessel?" "A sacrificial vessel of jade."
Someone said, "Yong is benevolent but not eloquent." The Master said, "What need has he of eloquence? He who argues skillfully with others is often hated by them. I do not know about his benevolence, but what need has he of eloquence?"
The Master wanted Qidiao Kai to take office. He replied, "I am not yet confident in this." The Master was pleased.
The Master said, "If my principles are not to prevail, I will get upon a raft and float about on the sea. He that will accompany me will be You, I dare say." Zilu, hearing this, was delighted. The Master said, "You is more fond of daring than I am, but he lacks judgment."
Meng Wubo asked whether Zilu was benevolent. The Master said, "I do not know." On being asked again, he said, "In a state of a thousand chariots, You might be employed to manage the military levies, but I do not know whether he is benevolent." "What do you say of Qiu?" The Master said, "In a city of a thousand families, or a clan of a hundred chariots, Qiu might be employed as governor, but I do not know whether he is benevolent." "What of Chi?" The Master said, "With his sash girt and standing in a court, Chi might be employed to converse with the guests, but I do not know whether he is benevolent."
The Master said to Zigong, "Which do you consider superior, yourself or Hui?" He replied, "How dare I compare myself with Hui? Hui hears one point and knows the whole ten; I hear one point and know a second." The Master said, "You are not equal to him. I grant that you are not equal to him."
Zai Yu was sleeping during the daytime. The Master said, "Rotten wood cannot be carved; a wall of dirty earth cannot be plastered. As to Yu, what is the use of reproving him?" The Master said, "At first, my way with men was to hear their words and give them credit for their conduct. Now my way is to hear their words and observe their conduct. It is from Yu that I have learned to make this change."
The Master said, "I have not seen a firm and unbending man." Someone replied, "There is Shen Cheng." The Master said, "Cheng is full of desires. How can he be firm and unbending?"
Zigong said, "What I do not wish others to do to me, I also wish not to do to others." The Master said, "Ci, that is beyond your reach."
Zigong said, "The Master's personal displays of his principles and ordinary descriptions of them may be heard. His discourses about man's nature and the way of Heaven cannot be heard."
When Zilu heard anything, if he had not yet been able to carry it into practice, he was only afraid lest he should hear something else.
Zigong asked, saying, "On what ground did Kong Wen get the title of 'Wen'?" The Master said, "He was of an active nature and yet fond of learning, and he was not ashamed to ask and learn of his inferiors. On these grounds he has been styled 'Wen'."
The Master said of Zichan, "He had four of the characteristics of a superior man: in his conduct of himself, he was humble; in serving his superiors, he was respectful; in nourishing the people, he was kind; in ordering the people, he was just."
The Master said, "Yan Pingzhong knew well how to maintain friendly intercourse. The acquaintance might be long, but he showed the same respect as at first."
The Master said, "Zang Wenzhong kept a large tortoise in a hall, the pillars of which he had carved with the hills, and the rafters painted with the duckweed. Of what sort was his wisdom?"
Zizhang asked, saying, "The minister Ziwen thrice took office and showed no sign of joy; thrice he retired from office and showed no sign of disappointment. He made it a point to inform the new minister of the old administration. What do you say of him?" The Master replied, "He was loyal." "Was he benevolent?" "I do not know. How can he be pronounced benevolent?" "When Cui Zi murdered the prince of Qi, Chen Wenzi, though he was the owner of forty horses, abandoned them and left the country. Coming to another state, he said, 'They are here like our great officer Cui,' and left it. He came to a second state, and with the same observation left it also. What do you say of him?" The Master replied, "He was pure." "Was he benevolent?" "I do not know. How can he be pronounced benevolent?"
Ji Wen thought thrice and then acted. When the Master was informed of it, he said, "Twice may do."
The Master said, "When good order prevailed in his country, Ning Wu acted the part of a wise man. When his country was in disorder, he acted the part of a stupid man. Others may equal his wisdom, but they cannot equal his stupidity."
The Master, being in Chen, said, "Let me return! Let me return! The little children of my school are ambitious and hasty. They are accomplished and complete so far, but they do not know how to restrict and shape themselves."
The Master said, "Bo Yi and Shu Qi did not keep the former wickednesses of men in mind, and hence the resentments directed towards them were few."
The Master said, "Who says of Weisheng Gao that he is upright? One begged some vinegar of him, and he begged it of a neighbor and gave it to the man."
The Master said, "Fine words, an insinuating appearance, and excessive respect—Zuoqiu Ming was ashamed of them. I also am ashamed of them. To conceal resentment against a person and appear friendly with him—Zuoqiu Ming was ashamed of such conduct. I also am ashamed of it."
Yan Yuan and Ji Lu were by the Master's side. The Master said to them, "Why do you not each tell me your wishes?" Zilu said, "I should like to have chariots and horses, light fur dresses, and share them with my friends, and though they should spoil them, I would not be displeased." Yan Yuan said, "I should like not to boast of my excellence, nor to make a display of my meritorious deeds." Zilu then said, "I should like to hear your wishes." The Master said, "They are, in regard to the aged, to give them rest; in regard to friends, to show them sincerity; in regard to the young, to treat them tenderly."
The Master said, "It is all over! I have not yet seen one who could perceive his faults and inwardly accuse himself."
The Master said, "In a hamlet of ten families, there may be found one honorable and sincere as I am, but not so fond of learning."

zh:
封龙山高，最宜观星。
墨山道前辈关山越夫妇大婚当晚，高子安曾献歌一曲。或因五音不全，竟引得天象异动，星雨漫天。山中老少皆仰首称奇，却无人知晓后来，此山中许多人，再未能同时看天。
詹聿抽签前夜，曾与妻风叙在山顶坐至三更。他从不想与她分离，可若与生死较量，他愿先走。心意已决，神色自会有异，他只得仰头看星。后风叙乘灯出逃，一生奉于观星堪舆之业，再未归山。
其余墨门弟子，留守封龙者三十五人。也曾观星于此山各处，或灶房后院、或书阁屋顶。
最后一夜，箭雨遮月。
有人倒下时，眼里依然望得见……星星。
此行可悔？
墨门子弟，为义生，为义死。无悔。
此行何益？
只为后来者夜路时，多几分光明。
en:
Dragonbend Mountain is high, perfect for stargazing.
On the wedding night of Mohist seniors Guan Shanyue and his wife, Gao Zi'an offered a song. Tone-deaf as he was, it somehow triggered a meteor shower. Young and old in the mountains looked up in wonder, never knowing that many among them would never watch the sky together again.
The night before Zhan Yu drew his lot, he sat with his wife, Feng Xu, on the peak until midnight. He never wanted to part from her, but in a choice between life and death, he resolved to go first. His mind made up, he could only look up at the stars to hide his sorrow. Later, Feng Xu escaped by lantern, devoting her life to stargazing and geomancy, never returning to the mountains.
Of the other Mohist disciples, thirty-five remained to guard Dragonbend. They too watched the stars from every corner: the kitchen yard, the library rooftop.
On the final night, a rain of arrows eclipsed the moon. As they fell, their eyes still held the stars.
Any regrets?
Disciples of Mohist Hill live for righteousness and die for it. No regrets.

What was gained?
Only a few more sparks of light for those walking through the night in the future.
Xing Cong
Shu Xuan

zh: 昔墨山道建飞天城，欲上贯云霓，衍算天机，以济苍生。未料宏愿未酬，城郭先颓，倏忽三载矣。今残垣之内，异声渐次，机巧之声，律若心搏。又见虫兽翔集，鸣声各异，青鸟掠影，盘桓故墟，诸猴痴妄，望水捞月。夫水中之影，天上月耶？缥缈梦耶？后之来者，或可于波澜间，探水中月之真假，飞天梦之虚实。
en: In days past, the Mohists built Skyward City, hoping to rise into the clouds, unravel the workings of heaven, and bring salvation to the common people. Yet before that grand vision could be fulfilled, the city had already fallen into ruin. In the blink of an eye, three years have passed. Now, within these broken walls, strange sounds begin to stir. The whir of mechanisms beats like a living heart. Insects and beasts gather, each cry distinct. Azure birds sweep past in fleeting shadows, circling the old ruins, while deluded monkeys reach into the water, trying to seize the moon's reflection. But is that image in the water truly the moon above, or only a drifting dream? Perhaps those who come after may search the ripples and learn whether the moon in the water is real, and whether the dream of flight was truth or illusion.

During the Tianyou era, the Baima Station Incident, orchestrated by Zhu Wen, claimed the lives of all Ten Sages of the Inkbound Order. Legend has it that, in order to preserve their teachings, the disciples spirited away several volumes from the Ten Sages' Collection—treatises on #YYin-Yang Ultimate Arts#E—and vanished into the secluded reaches of Qinghe, leaving no trace behind. Some believe they remained steadfast, founding an academy to keep the sages' wisdom alive despite the threats of the Liang court. Others say they chose seclusion, leading tranquil lives among waterfowl, untouched by worldly matters, as if they had transcended the mortal realm.
Decades later, during the Xiande era, Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou restored the old imperial gardens and #Ybuilt the Peace Bell Tower#E, hoping its chimes would usher in peace for the world. It was then that a villager reportedly discovered fragments of ancient scrolls and cloth on the mountainside, said to be remnants of the Inkbound Order. Could these be the lost books of the Ten Sages? I am inclined to believe so.

黎蓁蓁这辈子好几次都差点死掉。

长大一点，因为没有退路，和野狗抢食，
再到后来，为偿恩情，独自一人，去对敌那整个清河的义士。

但她活了下来。再痛再难，她都咬牙活下来了。
只有这一次，她知道，自己是真的要走了。

若是一切留不住，起码可以穿上这件嫁衣。
她并不是要嫁给谁，只是想让那人知道，这场隐秘的重逢。
en:
Li Zhenzhen came close to death multiple times in her life. 

As a child, she was sold to be a bride in a ghost marriage. 
When she was older, with nowhere to turn, she fought stray dogs for scraps of food. 
Later still, to repay a debt of gratitude, she stood alone against the warriors of Qinghe. 

But she survived. No matter how painful, how hopeless, she gritted her teeth and endured. 
Only this time, she knew for a fact she wouldn't make it. 

If nothing else could be saved, at least she could wear this wedding dress. 
She wasn't marrying anyone. She just wanted him to know that they had finally met again.

zh:
我一直痴迷于蚕的羽化——一条虫子，竟能化蛹成蛾、振翅而飞。听说北高峰深处有个山村至今还在拜蚕神，特意进山来看看，把见闻记下。

入山的路挺难走。不过沿途已见了好几处神龛，龛里供着女子骑马的小像——跟古籍里记的"马头娘"一模一样。方向没走错，再往深处去定有所获。

进村了！果然有东西！
村中立着一尊巨大的女子骑马像，足有两丈多高。跟《搜神记》里的蚕神"马头娘"完全吻合——这里的蚕神崇拜怕是自古就有，一直没断过。这例证太难得了！回去一定要好好写一篇考证。

记一桩怪事。村民好像有吃蛾翼的习惯。起初以为是什么腌制的吃食，凑近才看清——确实是翅翼，而且大得出奇，足有巴掌大小。寻常蚕蛾不过拇指长短，哪来这么大的蛾子？

村子地下有洞穴。我要想办法下去。

蛾仙是存在的。从虫到蛹，从蛹到蛾，从蛾到仙——这种崇拜并非无稽之谈。我亲眼见到了。肉眼估量，仙体大约有小山丘那么大，通体雪白。有许多极美的、如同裙带一样的丝带从仙体上探出，包裹住了整个山洞。洞穴像一个活着的大茧房，而我在茧房内部。
但可能是身在地下的缘故罢，我的头脑有些发热，眼睛也看不太真切了。我想数清一共有几根丝带，但那些丝带重重叠叠地在眼前晃，怎么也数不明白。
写字已经很费力了。
不过我好不容易才下来的。我应该带回最准确的记载。一定要带回去。这是无人见过的东西。我要把蛾仙的样子记下来带回去
蛾仙是雪白的
蛾仙是
我是虫子
en:
I've always been obsessed with the silkworm's metamorphosis: how a simple grub can pupate, sprout wings, and take flight. I heard a rumor about a remote village deep on North Peak that still worships the Silkworm Deity, so I made the trek out here to see it for myself and take notes.

The mountain trail is rough going. Still, I've already passed a few shrines along the way. They all hold little statues of a woman riding a horse, exactly like the "Lady Haya" from the old texts. I'm definitely on the right track. If I keep pushing deeper, I know I'll find something.

I made it to the village! I knew it!
Right in the middle of town stands a massive statue of the horse-riding woman, easily twenty feet tall. It's a dead ringer for the Silkworm Deity in In Search of the Divine. This cult must have survived here since ancient times, unbroken and unchanged. Finding living proof like this is incredibly rare! I can't wait to write a paper on this when I get back.

I need to write down something bizarre I just saw. The villagers seem to eat moth wings. At first, I thought it was some kind of dried meat, but up close, there's no mistaking it. They're wings. And they are freakishly huge, about the size of a human hand. A normal silkworm moth is barely the size of my thumb. Where the hell are they getting moths this big?

There's a cave system under the village. I need to find a way down.

The Moth Immortal is real. From grub to pupa, and from moth to immortal, it's not just a myth. I've seen it with my own eyes. Just eyeballing it, the immortal's body is the size of a small hill, stark white. Countless beautiful, flowing ribbons of silk stretch out from its body, blanketing the entire cavern. The cave is a massive, living cocoon, and I am inside it.
Maybe it's just because I'm underground, but I'm burning up, and my vision is starting to blur. I tried to count the ribbons, but they just keep swaying and overlapping in front of me. I can't focus on them.
It's getting really hard to write.
But it took everything I had to get down here. I need to bring back the most accurate records. I have to bring them back.
No one has ever seen this before. I need to write down exactly what the Moth Immortal looks like and take it back with me
The Moth Immortal is stark white
The Moth Immortal is
I am a bug

The day before yesterday, we entered the mountains to prospect for ore. Upon reaching a flight of stone steps, we saw an object half-buried in the fallen leaves. It turned out to be a mechanical bird. Its wings were broken, its eyes were dim, and it was covered in mud. There is no telling how many years it had been abandoned there.
Xiaoba, who was traveling with us, examined it for a long while and noted that despite the damage, the mechanisms inside were quite extraordinary. He sat down right there and spent a good while taking it apart and fixing it. Finally, when he reattached its feathers, the little bird actually flapped its wings twice and flew up again, landing on Xiaoba's shoulder and refusing to come down.
Xiaoba said that since it's been fixed, we might as well let it fly back on its own. We hope the Faction Master can find a safe place for it, so it won't have to wander the wilderness anymore.

可小说里不只有英雄，还有许多平凡之辈，他们不会武功，也没有好运，面对灾祸，往往只能默然承受。
想到这，秦奋翻了翻身，不由得松了口气。也许此刻，没有大案，没人受伤，便是最好的。
en:
When Qin Fen cannot sleep at night, he always lies with his arms behind his head, recalling the plot of a novel, No Arrest, No Peace, where Li Sandao chases a killer across miles, incomparably brave.
But the novel features not only heroes. It is filled with ordinary souls as well, people without martial skill or great fortune, who can only endure calamity in silence when it falls upon them.
At that thought, Qin Fen turns over and lets out a quiet breath. Perhaps right now, having no major cases and no one getting hurt is the best thing of all.

zh: 灼华馆中自馆主而下，有白夭夭与白蓁蓁两名弟子。据传，二人皆有神通。夭夭可凭一张桃夭帖，牵出千里情缘。而蓁蓁则有天眼，可看出对方的一生作为、一世姻缘。
en: Radiant Pavilion is led by its mistress and her two disciples: Bai Yaoyao and Bai Zhenzhen. Some say both possess mystical gifts. Yaoyao can link distant hearts with a single Peach Note. Zhenzhen, gifted with the Eye of Fate, is said to glimpse an entire lifetime of deeds and desires.

zh: 睁开狗眼看看，你爷爷我可是朝廷的人！
en: Open your eyes! I serve the imperial court!

zh: 优惠券只对单个商品生效
en: Coupons only apply to single item
Slot 3

en: Enough talk, it's not time to change shifts yet. You rest a little longer.
Convert

zh: 少东家的一天玩法，完成一次据点清剿。
en: Young Master's Routine: Clear an Outpost.

zh: 不说我，就是那陈宝来，陈大财人！那边玉佛店的那位！
en: It's not just me. Look at Chen Baolai, the big shot from the jade Buddha shop!
He Zhisheng
Tattered Banner

zh: 施主可否替吾前去#Y白头城#E与#Y英烈冢#E，鸣箫一曲，聊以慰其忠志？
en: Would you go to #YWhitecrown Fortress#E and the #YHeroes' Graves#E? Play for them and honor their sacrifice.

zh: 百生牌位，住的尽是些昔日殁于此地的无名侠客。
en: This spirit tablet honors the nameless wanderers who died here.
What are you doing?

en: There are countless leaves in the world. Without your story, how will I find it?

en: Not in the limited time. Cannot start the mode.

zh: 大地为卷，田垄作纹，引水化镜，以植稻禾。 位于耘丘的风景胜地，游侠可前往此处记述留影。
en:
The earth as a scroll, the field ridges as patterns, drawing water to form a mirror, to plant rice seedlings.
A scenic spot in Plowing Hill where Wanderers can record their memories.

en: Currently in another gameplay. Cannot enter Recall Training.

zh: 只想着若她真的还在，哪怕是鬼魂，我也想要再见一面……
en: I just wanted to see her one more time, even as a ghost, if she was still around...

zh: 不论命数如何，试上一试，总好过讳疾忌医、坐以待毙。
en: No matter what fate has in store, it's better to try something than to just wait for death.

zh: 哎，多谢龟奶奶，要不是你们，我肯定被抓了。
en: Thanks, Granny Turtle. I'd be done for if you hadn't helped.
How was your dream?

en: Fields with cold, heavy soil are perfectly suited for the bone ash method. Simply dip the roots of your seedlings into the burnt bones of any animal or bird, or pack lime around the base of the shoots. However, you should never use this technique in warm, sun-drenched earth.

zh: 小鸢啊，你先跟我回学堂，成不？课业还撂着呢。树这般高，我这四体不勤的，现在也攀不上去啊……
en: Yuan'er, come back to school with me first, won't you? You still have lessons to finish. The tree's too tall, and I'm no good at climbing. I can't get up there...

zh: 海上真有宝贝？有鲛人吗？
en: There really are treasures out at sea? What about merfolk? Have you seen any?
Resource type not set

zh: 游历至佛光顶的游侠，曾误将灌木丛中破戒头陀的脑袋当做石头一屁股坐下，得罪了佛爷寨。
en: A wanderer who traveled to Halo Peak, mistakenly sat on a rogue monk's head in the bushes—thereby offending Buddha Fort.
kronIen

Master of Fragrance
I heard, and saw...

Mi Wuyu

zh: 哼嗯——我就是背地说说，不会怎么样的。哪天我不干了，我就走之前骂他。
en: Uh-heh... I was just saying it behind his back. No harm, no foul. The day I quit, I'll curse him out to his face.

zh: 丰和春因其味清冽甘醇而被江湖人喜爱，可惜此酒产自江南沙海之中鲜有人知。听闻坎尔孜的商人唐奇似乎特意存了几坛。

外形别致，而内中药材配比更是精细，让人一看便知作者在这上面花费的功夫和心思。

en: Wen Bao gave a lazy snort, thinking: Why bother cleaning the bathroom? If it doesn't pay, I'm not doing it!

zh: 这片水泽名叫三涂泽，老办白事，沉过一船又一船的棺材，寻常人不往这地方来。
en: This is Dead Man's Marsh. It's where they hold water burials. Coffin boats have been sunk here for years, so most people know to keep away.

Hidden Mountain - Millennium Crossing & Meandering Bank
Paper Hanging Lamp

你小心地解开了缠在金腰燕身上的绳子，发现绳子另一端挂有一枚玉佩。
脱离绳子纠缠的金腰燕很快飞走了。
en:
You carefully untied the rope wrapped around the Red-humped Swallow, discovering a jade pendant hanging from the other end.
Freed from the rope's entanglement, the Red-humped Swallow quickly flew away.

en: See any umbrellas you like, Young Hero?

Increase affection to become friends. After becoming friends, you can:

zh: 不说了。说了你也不认得。她每日在天一楼看书，我在靠窗的座上看书，中间隔着三排架子，从没说过话。这信写好了也不敢送，但不写，心里又放不下。
en: You wouldn't know her. She reads at Tianyi Tower every day, three rows from my usual spot, never a word exchanged. Even if I finish this letter, I dare not send it, yet without writing it, I can't set my heart at ease.
Don't believe me? Fine... you're next!

zh: 你！你走开！我现在不想和你说话！
en: You! Get away! I don't want to talk to you right now!

zh: 无需担忧。老夫与现麟台使乃故交，已同他打过招呼，你若前往，自不会有人阻挠。
en: Fret not about that. The Secretariat official and I go way back, and we've already spoken on the matter. If you choose to go, no one will stop you.

zh: 郎君说的是。当做则做，能不能成是一回事，做不做是另一回事。

Profession Attribute

en: Master, does Raging Tides have wine comparable to our Parting Tears?

en: Companion cats love being petted! #YSlide your finger across the screen#E and gently pet your companion to make them happier!
Liu Po
Granny's Note 4

en: Lately, the illegal beef trade has spread throughout this city. So many fake an accident while secretly butchering and selling beef! I will not tolerate the smallest speck of dust. You criminals beyond the law, I will arrest every one of you without fail!
Scoop Report

en: If Ding Xiang told us to move early, she had her reasons.

zh: 若继续清修，我或还有机会；如今北上入这纷扰，此境再不可得了。
en: If I'd stayed in quiet cultivation, I might still have reached it. But I came north into this turmoil, and that chance is gone now.
White Day Rat
Love Simplicity

The branch scrawls wildly...

zh:
浮戏山一事，承蒙相助。近来听人说起你回清河，主持重修，想必诸事繁杂，未免劳神。特托人奉上香炉一盏。
焚香可静气凝神，除障祛秽，亦觉睡眠。改日拜访，我再携些我自用的香丸来。
en:
I am most grateful for your assistance regarding the matter at Ethereal Summit. I heard recently that you have returned to Qinghe to preside over the restoration. Such affairs are surely numerous and complex; I trust you are not overly taxed by them. I have taken the liberty of sending an incense burner to you by messenger.

The burning of incense can quiet the spirit, cleanse away impurities, and aid in restful sleep. When I next visit, I shall bring with me some of the incense pellets I personally use for you to try.

en: A peculiar coin pouch embroidered with the character for "Evil." It's hard to tell if it's meant to attract wickedness or ward it off.

It cooks on its own without needing a fire, secures itself without being lifted, and moves on its own without being moved by others. If we use it to offer sacrifices upon the ancient ruins of Kunwu, the heavens above will surely accept and bless our offering!

其筑甘井而聚宝，列金玉以耀空。商通南北，渠贯东西。故而得黄金之名，声彻宇内。
然则波陈兵燹，摧璇室瑶台。沙海罡风，埋鸾箫象板。遂使甘泉涸井，空悬辘轳。锦帐华裀，尽化蒿莱。不见漫天洒金，但见满目尘灰。 
余携康珍珠旧事，访秘寻幽，乃得见旧日面目。
活枯井一口，胡杨一株。待往后来者，以此见从前故事。
en:
The ancient Poplar Bazaar stands on the ruins of a Sogdian merchant dynasty, the Kang family.

They dug sweet wells to gather riches, displayed gold and jade to dazzle onlookers. Trade routes connected north and south; canals stretched east and west. Thus the place earned its nickname, "Land of Gold," its fame echoing across the land.

Yet the Bodchens' wars razed jade halls and jeweled pavilions. Desert gales buried phoenix flutes and ivory clappers. Sweet wells ran dry, its windlass left dangling. Brocade tents and fine carpets withered to weeds and thorns. No golden rain falls from the sky now, only dust and ash fill the view.

Bearing the old tales of Kang Zhenzhu, I sought out hidden depths and glimpsed the settlement's former glory.

One barely living well. One poplar tree. For future travelers to glimpse the stories of the past.

en:
Yellow sand fills the sky, and the journey is arduous. You press on through the endless sea of dunes beyond Jade Gate Pass. Parched and faint with thirst, you come to the shaded side of a dune, where you find an old, dry well. The well is wide enough for a person to descend. You remember this place. Once, you helped the well-digger of Horsehelm Village recover an oil lamp from the depths below. At this moment, the faint murmur of water and human voices echoes from within the well. You decide to... #Y[Take a look, for there are people below.]
You cautiously follow the underground passage and spot a campfire. Several workers are here, using sand shovels to clear and reinforce the waterway. At the sight of you, they greet you warmly and hand you a bowl of water.#E Following the underground watercourse, you come upon a makeshift refuge. The people here speak to you with pride of Horsehelm Village's past, of the might of the Anxi Army's watering grounds, of the generations of well-diggers' efforts, and of the help once given by a wanderer... You know this is only a dream, yet you still believe that as long as that oil lamp burns, clear spring water will forever flow beneath, and human hope will never run dry. "How does the water remain so clear? Only because, through countless generations, lamp-bearers will come."

zh:
好消息是，他发现沈玉喜欢听故事。
坏消息是，他发现沈玉只喜欢听故事。

他在勾栏瓦肆摊位上排到的东西，沈玉却一个也不收，那有什么办法呢，他只好给她讲更多的故事，更好的故事，她听故事时候的笑，和第一次见她时大不相同，他喜欢这种笑，因此想把世上所有的故事讲给她听。
他想了半宿，从萧府逃跑的那时候，他像是一只从笼子里飞出的鸟，只是偏偏在那个夜晚，有人给他投喂了鸟食，所以多停留一下也是可以的吧，人有一饭之恩，但他这算什么？鸟食之恩。
但不管是哪门子的恩，他都想要找些事情来让她开心点儿，他是打心眼里这么想的。
可她不开心会怎么样呢？她的往日看起来都不开心，不也是过来了吗，可现在不一样了。哪儿不一样了，他问自己，但半天得不到什么好答案，只是看见她笑的时候，萧史自己也会开心，他只好说，是为了自己的开心，因此他几日几夜地徘徊在沈府附近。

“你不去江湖了。”
“再等一等。”

只是沈玉的开心似乎只有夜晚的某几个瞬间，偶尔看向他来去的时候，也会失了神。
他迫切地想要弄懂她的不开心，他开始去听沈府丫鬟的碎语，去看这座死气沉沉的院子。
他抬头看了看这座院子，这座院子太过安静，甚至听不见几声鸟鸣，这里太闷了，这样死气沉沉的地方与沈玉不搭。
要是他住在这儿，多少得掀了屋顶，给这个连鸟叫都少有的地方弄出点人气来，“笼中雀掀了头顶的竹字头，就是龙中雀嘛。”他得意地想出了这个说法——然后，龙去江海，雀入青空，也许这样沈玉会多笑一些。

“喂！这次要走了吗？”
“再等一等嘛。”
“那你的故事呢？”
故事重要，可我好像很想把故事，都讲给一个人听。
en:
The good news was, he discovered Shen Yu liked stories.

The bad news? She only liked the stories.

The little trinkets he queued hours for at Fairgrounds stalls, Shen Yu wouldn't take a single one. So what could he do? He told her more stories. Better stories. And the way she smiled while listening was so different from when they first met. He liked that smile. So much so, he wanted to tell her every story in the world.

He thought long and hard about it. Back when he escaped the Xiao estate, he'd felt like a bird let loose from its cage. But that night... someone had tossed him a handful of birdseed. So maybe it was okay to linger a little longer. People say a single meal deserves gratitude. What was this, then? A debt for birdseed?

Whatever kind of debt it was, he just wanted to find ways to make her smile. He meant that, truly.

But what if she stayed unhappy? She'd lived like that before, hadn't she? And she made it through just fine. But now... now it felt different. What was different? He kept asking himself, but no answer came. Only that when she smiled, he smiled too. And so he wandered outside the Shen estate for days, for nights.

"You're not going to the jianghu anymore?"

"Just... waiting a bit longer."

Shen Yu only seemed to smile in fleeting moments at night. Sometimes, when she caught him coming or going, she'd lose focus.

He needed to understand why she was unhappy. He started eavesdropping on the maids' whispers, studying every quiet corner of that lifeless courtyard.

He looked up. This place was far too still. Not even birdsong can be heard. The air itself felt stifled. It didn't suit her.

If he lived here, he'd have torn the roof off just to let some sky in. To breathe some life into a place that barely let birds sing.

"A caged sparrow," he mused, "take the'roof' off the cage, and what do you get? A dragon."

He was very proud of that one. A dragon returns to the sea. A bird soars into open skies. Maybe then, Shen Yu would smile more.

"Hey! Leaving this time for real?"

"Just... waiting a bit longer."

"What about your stories?"

Stories do matter. But lately, it feels like what matters most...is telling them to a specific person.

At the avenue's end stands Shengping Bridge, its arched beams layered like a rainbow spanning the water. Climbing its height, one can gaze south toward the Main South Gate and north toward Xuande Gate, contemplating an era of peace and prosperity.

zh:
很难想象，白茸居然是高门深宅中长出来的女儿。
及笄的那一年，她自己选了一枚桃花玉佩作为纪念。桃花春情之说自古有之，古板循旧的父亲见了，立马露出震怒的迹象。母亲想用“之子于归，宜其室家”来圆场，可白茸年少倔强，顺口就驳了句：“桃花春水渌，水上鸳鸯浴。”结果一顿谩骂责打在所难免。
无奈，她生来便是娇娇夭夭的性子，又有十二分的颜色。在那样的地方生活，很多时候，好些事不管她有心无意，都是她的错。
“既然你们都说我是妖女，我若不知风月，岂不是枉担了虚名？”
她一气之下干脆入了醉花阴，从此与所谓的家人断了联系。
只有她的母亲曾来开封见过女儿。那已是好几年后，阳春花多情又无情的风韵，已让无数人拜倒裙下。母亲对此并未多说多做，她只留下了那枚桃花玉佩，以及一句话：之子于归、两情相悦的故事，也未必都是不好。
不知白茸有没有明白母亲的意思。或许她早已忘了吧？但她又确实将这枚桃花玉佩，搁在了那人必经的花船上。
en:
It's hard to believe Bai Rong was raised in a noble and strict household.
On the day she came of age, she chose a peach blossom jade pendant to mark the occasion. Peach blossoms have long symbolized romantic feelings, and when her rigid, old-fashioned father saw it, he immediately flew into a rage. Her mother tried to smooth things over with a line from the classics—"A daughter marries, bringing harmony to her new home"—but the headstrong young Bai Rong retorted without hesitation: "Peach blossom waters run clear, where mandarin ducks bathe above."
A storm of scolding and punishment inevitably followed.
But Bai Rong was born delicate and willful, blessed with striking beauty. In a place like that, whether intentional or not, she was often blamed for things beyond her control.
"If you all insist I'm a seductress, wouldn't it be a waste of the name if I knew nothing of love?"
Out of spite, she joined the Velvet Shade Society and severed ties with her so-called family.
Only her mother ever visited her in Kaifeng—years later, by then spring's tender charm had already made countless admirers fall at Bai Rong's feet. Her mother said little and did even less. She simply left behind the peach blossom pendant and a single remark: even stories of two hearts in love and a daughter's return home are not always something to be condemned.
Did Bai Rong understand what her mother meant? Perhaps she'd long forgotten. But she did, after all, leave that same peach blossom pendant on the flower boat the man was sure to board.

后来，孩子们散到天南地北，在许多个寂静的夜里，在连风都睡去的凌晨……

On Spring Festival's Eve, the loudest, liveliest spot is always wherever the kids are setting off firecrackers.
The ones covering their ears still inch closer. The ones hanging back complain they can't see. And the ones who get too close jump out of their skin.
Firecrackers have a way of picking their moment. Just when no one's ready—bang!
Years pass. The kids grow up and drift apart. On many silent nights, in those predawn hours when even the wind is asleep, that loud crack still comes back, knocking at their hearts again and again.

en:
On an isle in West Lake a hill stands alone, surrounded by water and clear air, its mist shimmering from afar. People call it Lone Hill.
In the Tang era, incense smoke curled about the ancient temple on the hill, and scholars would visit the isle to admire its beauty and forget the world's cares. In the fifth year of Huichang, Gushan Temple was destroyed, its halls collapsed into ruin.
Though the temple is gone, Lone Hill's spirit endures. Winter plums bloom along the ridge, and white cranes roost at its foot. Travelers gazing across the water still see that singular emerald green in the heart of the lake, alone in its tranquility.

至于为什么——我这一身药味还不明显？
此处叫做清心圃，是个药村，处处都种药材，这儿的百姓是我见过最为温和良善之人，那个被吓晕过去的胆小鬼叫做姜凡，是个在清心圃和长兴集往来收药材的客商，我们喂了他些清心回神的药，便好了！我可没有害人，不过我之后还是请他吃了饭赔罪，他还说要带我去长兴集瞧瞧。
但我有些舍不得走，我见过许多村子，这村子着实特别……炮制地黄之法也特别，只是我对这个了解实在不多，看不出门道来。
en:
What rotten luck! I napped on a roadside cart and woke up here, reeking of herbs. When I jumped off, the carter fainted dead away. What a coward, but to be fair, he fainted in a nice spot.
Why? Isn't the herbal stench obvious?
This place is called Stillheart Grove, a village of medicine, where every field grows remedies. The people here are the gentlest I've ever met. We revived the carter, Jiang Fan, a merchant who trades herbs between Stillheart Grove and Crosswind Bazaar, with some calming pills. I didn't mean to harm him! I even treated him to a meal to apologize. He offered to take me to Crosswind Bazaar.
But... I don't want to leave just yet. I've seen many villages, but this one is special, even their way of curing rehmannia roots is unusual. Though I'll admit, I know too little to grasp the trick of it.

zh:
捞月者蠢人也。
今先生以月教吾，吾亦以月应先生。万师以为天下月分三等，蠢亦分三等。
三等蠢人，不轨正义，不通人情，不慕千金，偏以侠义为月，罪孽为湖，挟勇武而鸣不平，披肝胆而诺千金，摩顶放踵，不爱其躯，所得不过三两浮名。不思畏，此一蠢也。
二等蠢人，不顺大势，不同浊流，不知进退，偏以苍生为月，乱世为湖，上忧天下兴亡，下忧万民生艰，孤身逆势，蚍蜉撼树，所留不过点点涟漪。不思变，此二蠢也。
一等蠢人，不惜生死，不追贤名，不晓荣华，偏以春秋为月，岁月为湖，移千山而图百代，废一时而谋千秋，众猴衔尾，不知其终，所捞不过镜花水月。不思利，此三蠢也。
世间玲珑者何其多也。天地无心，生民无命，祈万世太平者，恰如临渊揽月，智者不为，所为者唯蠢者矣。呜呼，余以为此三蠢者，得其一者为稀，得其三者寥寥，孰料此间竟尽皆如此！
幸甚！幸甚！
en:
To try to scoop the moon from the water is foolishness.
Since Master used the moon to teach me, I will answer him with the moon in turn. To my mind, under Heaven there are three kinds of moon, and three kinds of foolishness to match.
The lowest kind of fool cannot stomach crookedness, knows nothing of worldly ways, and cares nothing for wealth, yet takes chivalry for his moon and a world of wrongs for his water. He throws his courage behind the cause of righting wrongs, bares his heart and guts to keep impossible promises, wears himself down from head to toe without sparing his own body, and in the end gains no more than a scrap or two of empty fame. He does not know fear. This is the first kind of foolishness.
The average kind of fool will not follow the tide, will not drift with the muddy current, and does not know when to advance or when to retreat. He takes the common people for his moon and an age of chaos for his water. He grieves for the rise and fall of the realm, and just as deeply for the hardships of the people. Alone, he pushes against the current, like an ant trying to shake a tree, leaving behind no more than a few faint ripples. He does not know how to change. This is the second kind of foolishness.
The greatest kind of fool does not spare life or death, does not chase fame, and has no use for glory or splendor. He takes history itself for his moon and the passing years for his water. He would move a thousand mountains for the sake of generations yet to come, cast aside the needs of one age to plan for a thousand years beyond it. Like monkeys clutching one another's tails, he does not even know where it all ends. In the end, all he can scoop up is the moon's reflection in the water, flowers in a mirror, nothing that can truly be held. He does not know profit. This is the third kind of foolishness.
There are many geniuses in this world. Heaven and earth have no heart, and the people have no certain fate. To pray for peace for ten thousand generations is like trying to scoop the moon from the water. No wise man would do such a thing. Only fools would.
Alas, I had thought that to possess even one of these three kinds of foolishness was rare, and to possess all three rarer still. Who would have guessed that all here are such fools?
What good fortune indeed.

听着这水声往上头瞧，那段山路其实不算长。可对那时的娃娃们来说，已经是一片望不到边的天地了——
石头是巨人设的陷阱，草木是精怪铺的毛毯，每一次虫鸣都是山林的呼唤，每一声鸟叫都藏着新的暗号。
所以只要听见那轰隆隆的水响，娃娃们的小心脏就会扑通扑通跳起来。
他们知道，那远方又在喊他们了！
新的故事，就要顺着水花，溅进手心啦！

The waterfall behind Evercare Clinic was where every adventure began.
Water came spilling down the cliff in bright, jumping spray and scattered itself across the deep pool below.
If you looked up along the sound of it, the path above wasn't all that long. But to the children back then, it felt endless.
The rocks were traps laid by giants. The grass was a carpet spread by forest spirits. Every insect call was a summons. Every birdsong hid a secret.
So the moment they heard the roar of the falls, their hearts would start pounding.
It meant the world beyond was calling again!
And a new story was already on its way, splashing straight into their hands!

zh:
天不收十次上山采药，有七次身后会跟着三个奶娃娃……而七次里面有六次，这些娃娃是赶也赶不走的。
最后天不收妥协了，他决定送他们一个小礼物——指南鱼。
他心想啊，有了这指南鱼以后，娃娃们只管迈开小脚丫子。
去追蝴蝶也好，去摘野草也罢，反正走再远的路，这指南鱼，总能为他们指明方向。
而这林间的风，也总会牵着他们回家。
en:
Most times Unfated Tian went up the mountain for herbs, he ended up with the same problem: three little kids trailing after him. And once they latched on, they were impossible to shake.
So in the end, he gave up trying. Instead, he made them a small gift: a Compass Fish.
He figured that with something like that in hand, they could wander all they liked.
Let them chase butterflies. Let them pick weeds. Let them run farther than they should. The Compass Fish would point the way back.
And if that failed, the mountain wind would lead them home.

zh:
“哦哟，赛青呀，跑哪里去啦侬！又给自家染了色？”“汪汪！”
每隔几日，染坊里就要上演几乎一模一样的对话。说话的人有时是刚来不久的阿姐阿哥，有时是在这儿干了半辈子的阿婆阿公。而汪汪的小狗一直都是同一只，小花狗赛青。人喜欢漂亮的布，赛青也喜欢。赛青很乖，从不捣乱，每每刚染好的布匹晾起来，它便像得了什么使命般巡逻一圈，把布仔仔细细瞧一遍。别担心，布没事，只是那小花狗身上偶尔会多几处新鲜的花纹。
“赛青呀！今朝晒新布啦！”
染坊是个紧跟时兴的地方，晒布的架子从来没有空闲的时候。天光好时，染制得精致的布料被高高挂起，被风吹起来，五彩斑斓、飘飘摇摇，好像要把天都染上颜色。人有钟爱的颜色，赛青也有。赛青的世界里，蓝色是最最漂亮丰富的。深蓝色像日出前的天空，带着露水的潮意；浅蓝色像夏日晌午的天空，让狗心里热乎乎的……赛青看着身上新沾上的星星点点，觉得自家真厉害，把远远的青天都带在了身边。
en:
"Oh my, Sai Qing, where have you run off to! Dyed yourself again, have you?" "Woof woof!"
Every few days, nearly the same exchange would play out in the dye house. Sometimes it's one of the young new hands, sometimes one of the old timers who'd worked there half their lives. But the dog barking back is always the same one: the little spotted dog, Sai Qing. People love beautiful cloth, and so does Sai Qing. He's well-behaved and never causes trouble. Whenever a freshly dyed bolt of cloth is hung up to dry, he would make his rounds as if on some solemn duty, inspecting every inch of fabric with great care. Don't worry, the cloth is fine, it's only the little spotted dog who sometimes picks up a few new spots on his coat.
"Sai Qing! New cloth going up today!"
The dye house keeps pace with the fashions, and the drying racks are never empty. On a bright day, the finely dyed fabrics are hung up high, catching the wind and rippling in a riot of color, as though they might dye the sky itself. People have colors they love, and so does Sai Qing. In his world, blue is the prettiest and richest of them all. Deep blue is the sky before sunrise, damp with dew. Pale blue is the sky at a summer's noon, and it makes him feel warm inside... Sai Qing looks at the fresh flecks of blue dotting his fur, and decides he's really something, carrying that far-off blue sky around with him.
Days Active:
Tonight, we drink until we fall.
In the brief span of a mortal life, how many such golden moments can we truly hope to hold?

此番留宿马头村，幸识贺老，如见故人。昨日灯下长谈，得知村中井水干涸，乡邻忧心。我随你来此，才知你意在寻水，已有多时。

掘泉引水，非旦夕可成。然贺老心志如磐，村众齐心，假以时日，必得甘霖，昕当遥贺之。此去路远，望贺老珍重。
en:
My stay in Horsehelm Village was made memorable by our meeting, Elder He. Our conversation last night revealed the plight of your village—the well dried, the people anxious—and the true purpose of your long search.

Years of service at Jade Gate Pass have taught me something of locating water. As you read this, my troops and I are already on the move. My departure was sudden, so I have left a map that may aid your quest upon your books.

Drawing water from the earth is no swift task. Yet, with your iron will and the strength of your village, I have no doubt that water will flow again. I will look forward to news of your success. Until then, take good care.

zh:
铁铁收：

之前出门前我还跟你磨叽，说一个人走道儿没意思，想拽你一块儿，偏铁铁你事务多，推三阻四不跟我去。

结果咋样？老天爷都看不下去了！这趟出门没走多远，就硬给我塞了个搭子！

清河有个名叫$C$L#Y$PN#E$C的，铁铁你印识不？

不印识是吧，不印识就对了，因为我也不印识。我这搭子是他门下庄客，叫李来做。（这名字还怪耳熟的，总觉得在哪里听过）但这都不打紧，打紧的是，我这搭子他命苦啊！他家里的少东家不拿他当个人，每天天不亮，就使唤他起床上工，起的比鸡早，睡得比狗晚。

诶嘛这还不算，一个月工钱没有，活儿干不好还得关小黑屋、挨小皮鞭抽屁股！

铁铁你说，都是做少东家的，这叫$C$L#Y$PN#E$C的瘪犊子，同你比咋一个天上一个地下！

反正吧铁子，我这兄弟如今水深火热，我有心救他一把，他却道自个儿的卖身契还攥在那个叫$C$L#Y$PN#E$C手上。要是跑了，被官府抓回去，打死都没处说理去。

说到这儿铁铁你肯定也明白我为啥写信了。你平常不是挺能白乎的嘛，要不铁铁出面，去跟那个$C$L#Y$PN#E$C唠唠，让他放我兄弟自由？

多少钱，让他随便开！先前儿我已给了我那兄弟十万通宝，要是不够，二十万、三十万也行。当然，他要非得拧着不放人，哼，那就别怪我跟他先礼后兵了！

方旭留
en:
To my Bro:
Before I left, I kept nagging you, saying it was boring to travel alone and wanting to drag you along. But you said you were too busy and kept making excuses not to go.
And look what happened? Even the heavens couldn't stand it! Not long after I set out, they practically shoved a partner into my arms!
Bro, do you know a guy from Qinghe named $C$L#Y$PN#E$C?
No? Well, that makes sense, because I don't know him either. My new partner is a retainer under him called Li Laizuo. (That name sounds weirdly familiar, like I've heard it somewhere before.) But that doesn't matter. What matters is that my partner leads a miserable life! His young master doesn't treat him like a human. Every day before dawn, he's ordered out of bed to work, rising earlier than a rooster and sleeping later than a dog.
Man, that's not even the half of it. He doesn't get a penny of wages, and if he doesn't work well enough, he gets locked in a dark room and whipped on his butt with a little leather strap!
Bro, we're both young masters, but this jerk named $C$L#Y$PN#E$C is just a total scoundrel compared to you!
Anyway, Bro, my brother is currently in terrible trouble. I want to save him, but he says his contract is still in $C$L#Y$PN#E$C's hands. If he runs away and gets caught by the authorities, he'll be beaten to death and have no way to seek justice.
At this point, you surely understand why I'm writing. You're usually a good talker, so how about you go talk to $C$L#Y$PN#E$C and get him to set my brother free?
Whatever price he wants, let him name it! I already gave my brother 100,000 coins. If that's not enough, 200,000 or 300,000 is fine too. Of course, if he insists on being stubborn and won't let go... hmph, then don't blame me for trying diplomacy before force!
Yours, Fang Xu

With that, he springs down from the pavilion, spear in hand, and beckons you forward.

zh:
她没有名字。师父捡到她的时候，她正因饥饿误食了毒草，躺在路旁等死。
师父不但救了她，还给她取了名字，秋兰。
秋兰可喻，桂树冬荣。

后来她才知道，师父是鼎鼎大名的医者，救过的人不计其数。大家都叫师父“秋水仙子”。
她想，师父救过这么多人，却只把自己留在了身边。或许，师父对她多少也是有偏爱的吧。

她向师父学习医术，慢慢地也学会了毒术。
师父跟随悬剑辅佐主公，她跟随师父。她的毒也不止一次派上过用场，每每师父都会用赞赏的目光看向她。
直到主公身死，悬剑倾覆。

师父说主公是被下了毒，而那毒发作时的样子与她所制的毒如出一辙。
师父这是在怀疑自己？
不是的！
她大声辩驳。不是自己下的毒。她知道悬剑对师父来说是多么重要，她又怎会去做惹师父不快之事呢？
可师父独自离开，定是不信她的意思。

她不知那天究竟发生了什么，只得一次次找悬剑众人确认原委。从一开始还有人耐心解答，到后来没人再愿意陪她回忆这些细节。
最后，她只得在自己身上试毒，企图证明自己所使的毒药与害死主公的不是一种。
不知过去了多少年月。她终于验出了当年的毒药，终于能向师父证明自己。可师父连同悬剑众人一道，不知去向。
中毒一事真相谓何，或许从来都不是主公遇袭的关键。只有她还独自在荒野徘徊，一遍遍地诉说自己没有犯错，却无人在意。
en:
She never had a name. When her master found her, she was lying by the roadside, starving and half-dead from eating poisonous herbs.
Her master not only saved her but also gave her a name: Qiulan.
Qiulan, like the sweet osmanthus that blooms in winter.

Much later, she learned that her master was the famed doctor known as the "Qiu Shuixian," who had saved countless lives.
Yet, out of all those people, her master only kept her by her side. Maybe, just maybe, her master was a little partial to her.

She learned medicine from her master, and eventually, the art of poisons as well.
Wherever her master went to serve the Lord along with the Hanging Blade, she followed. Her poison was put to use more than once, and each time, her master would look at her with quiet pride.
But then Lord died, and the Hanging Blade was destroyed.

Her master said the lord had died from poisoning, and the symptoms matched her own toxins exactly.
Was her master suspecting her?
No!
She protested loudly. She hadn't done it. She knew how much the Hanging Blade meant to her master. She'd never do anything to hurt her.
Yet her master left alone, clearly unconvinced.

She didn't know what had truly happened that day. She kept asking others in the Hanging Blade, over and over, to help her piece together the events. At first, people answered her patiently. Over time, they lost all interest.
In the end, she started testing poisons on herself, trying to prove that the poison she used wasn't the same as the one that killed the lord.
She didn't know how many years had passed before she finally identified the poison from that day, ready at last to clear her name to her master. But her master and all the others with the Hanging Blade had vanished without a trace.
In the end, maybe the truth about the poisoning never even mattered. She was left wandering the wilderness alone, repeating her innocence to an uncaring world.

"The Nine-Bend Yellow River guards its ford, as treasures from four seas fall from the sky."

国主立子玄喆为皇太子，行册礼于宫城明德门外。仪仗十里，锦幄蔽日，百官皆衣锦绣，马饰金羁。市中结彩楼数十座，教坊乐工鼓吹竟日，观者塞途。太子冠冕饰七宝，珠光射人。

en:
Chengdu Prefecture Secret Report Summary
...
The Emperor named his son Xuanzhe as Crown Prince, holding the ceremony outside the Mingde Gate of the Imperial Palace. The procession spanned ten miles and blocked the sun with silk canopies. Officials wore embroidered garments, and horses wore golden harnesses. Dozens of festive towers were built in the city, with musicians from the Imperial Music Bureau playing all day in crowded streets. The prince's crown was adorned with seven precious gems that shone brightly.
...
The Emperor also ordered a chamber pot inlaid with seven precious gems, shining like stars in the dark. Subordinates competed to offer rare treasures, including jade screens and coral stands, all of which the Lord accepted. Envoy Wang Zhaoyuan was caught whispering, "The entire treasury doesn't have enough to fund even a single day of this extravagance." Anyone who heard him just shook with fear and kept their mouths shut.

One old man in the city sighed, "Wang Yan perished due to luxury, and now we see it again." Before he could finish speaking, guards arrested him and gave him twenty strokes.

Your disciple has personally verified these truths and recorded them for your eyes. Any further developments will be reported immediately.

zh:
【乐记第十九】

凡音之起，由人心生也。人心之动，物使之然也。感于物而动，故形于声。声相应，故生变，变成方，谓之音。比音而乐之，及干戚羽旄，谓之乐。乐者，音之所由生也，其本在人心之感于物也。是故其哀心感者，其声噍以杀；其乐心感者，其声啴以缓；其喜心感者，其声发以散；其怒心感者，其声粗以厉；其敬心感者，其声直以廉；其爱心感者，其声和以柔。六者非性也，感于物而后动，是故先王慎所以感之者。故礼以道其志，乐以和其声，政以一其行，刑以防其奸。礼、乐、刑、政，其极一也，所以同民心而出治道也。凡音者，生人心者也。情动于中，故形于声，声成文谓之音。是故治世之音安以乐，其政和；乱世之音怨以怒，其政乖；亡国之音哀以思，其民困。声音之道，与政通矣。宫为君，商为臣，角为民，征为事，羽为物。五者不乱，则无怗懘之音矣。宫乱则荒，其君骄；商乱则陂，其官坏；角乱则忧，其民怨；征乱则哀，其事勤；羽乱则危，其财匮。五者皆乱，迭相陵，谓之慢。如此，则国之灭亡无日矣。郑卫之音，乱世之音也，比于慢矣。桑间濮上之音，亡国之音也，其政散，其民流，诬上行私而不可止也。凡音者，生于人心者也。乐者，通伦理者也。是故知声而不知音者，禽兽是也；知音而不知乐者，众庶是也。唯君子为能知乐。是故审声以知音，审音以知乐，审乐以知政，而治道备矣。是故不知声者，不可与言音，不知音者，不可与言乐。知乐则几于礼矣。礼乐皆得，谓之有德。德者，得也。是故乐之隆，非极音也；食飨之礼，非致味也。清庙之瑟，朱弦而疏越，壹倡而三叹，有遗音者矣。大飨之礼，尚玄酒而俎腥鱼，大𡙡不和，有遗味者矣。是故先王之制礼乐也，非以极口腹耳目之欲也，将以教民平好恶而反人道之正也。人生而静，天之性也；感于物而动，性之欲也。物至知知，然后好恶形焉。好恶无节于内，知诱于外，不能反躬，天理灭矣。夫物之感人无穷，而人之好恶无节，则是物至而人化物也。人化物也者，灭天理而穷人欲者也。于是有悖逆诈伪之心，有淫泆作乱之事。是故强者胁弱，众者暴寡，知者诈愚，勇者苦怯，疾病不养，老幼孤独不得其所，此大乱之道也。是故先王之制礼乐，人为之节。衰麻哭泣，所以节丧纪也；钟鼓干戚，所以和安乐也；昏姻冠笄，所以别男女也；射乡食飨，所以正交接也。礼节民心，乐和民声，政以行之，刑以防之。礼、乐、刑、政，四达而不悖，则王道备矣。乐者为同，礼者为异。同则相亲，异则相敬。乐胜则流，礼胜则离。合情饰貌者，礼乐之事也。礼义立，则贵贱等矣，乐文同，则上下和矣。好恶著则贤不肖别矣。刑禁暴，爵举贤，则政均矣。仁以爱之，义以正之，如此则民治行矣。乐由中出，礼自外作。乐由中出，故静；礼自外作，故文。大乐必易，大礼必简。乐至则无怨，礼至则不争。揖让而治天下者，礼乐之谓也。暴民不作，诸侯宾服，兵革不试，五刑不用，百姓无患，天子不怒，如此则乐达矣。合父子之亲，明长幼之序，以敬四海之内，天子如此，则礼行矣。
……
en:
【乐记第十九】

凡音之起，由人心生也。人心之动，物使之然也。感于物而动，故形于声。声相应，故生变，变成方，谓之音。比音而乐之，及干戚羽旄，谓之乐。乐者，音之所由生也，其本在人心之感于物也。是故其哀心感者，其声噍以杀；其乐心感者，其声啴以缓；其喜心感者，其声发以散；其怒心感者，其声粗以厉；其敬心感者，其声直以廉；其爱心感者，其声和以柔。六者非性也，感于物而后动，是故先王慎所以感之者。故礼以道其志，乐以和其声，政以一其行，刑以防其奸。礼、乐、刑、政，其极一也，所以同民心而出治道也。凡音者，生人心者也。情动于中，故形于声，声成文谓之音。是故治世之音安以乐，其政和；乱世之音怨以怒，其政乖；亡国之音哀以思，其民困。声音之道，与政通矣。宫为君，商为臣，角为民，征为事，羽为物。五者不乱，则无怗懘之音矣。宫乱则荒，其君骄；商乱则陂，其官坏；角乱则忧，其民怨；征乱则哀，其事勤；羽乱则危，其财匮。五者皆乱，迭相陵，谓之慢。如此，则国之灭亡无日矣。郑卫之音，乱世之音也，比于慢矣。桑间濮上之音，亡国之音也，其政散，其民流，诬上行私而不可止也。凡音者，生于人心者也。乐者，通伦理者也。是故知声而不知音者，禽兽是也；知音而不知乐者，众庶是也。唯君子为能知乐。是故审声以知音，审音以知乐，审乐以知政，而治道备矣。是故不知声者，不可与言音，不知音者，不可与言乐。知乐则几于礼矣。礼乐皆得，谓之有德。德者，得也。是故乐之隆，非极音也；食飨之礼，非致味也。清庙之瑟，朱弦而疏越，壹倡而三叹，有遗音者矣。大飨之礼，尚玄酒而俎腥鱼，大𡙡不和，有遗味者矣。是故先王之制礼乐也，非以极口腹耳目之欲也，将以教民平好恶而反人道之正也。人生而静，天之性也；感于物而动，性之欲也。物至知知，然后好恶形焉。好恶无节于内，知诱于外，不能反躬，天理灭矣。夫物之感人无穷，而人之好恶无节，则是物至而人化物也。人化物也者，灭天理而穷人欲者也。于是有悖逆诈伪之心，有淫泆作乱之事。是故强者胁弱，众者暴寡，知者诈愚，勇者苦怯，疾病不养，老幼孤独不得其所，此大乱之道也。是故先王之制礼乐，人为之节。衰麻哭泣，所以节丧纪也；钟鼓干戚，所以和安乐也；昏姻冠笄，所以别男女也；射乡食飨，所以正交接也。礼节民心，乐和民声，政以行之，刑以防之。礼、乐、刑、政，四达而不悖，则王道备矣。乐者为同，礼者为异。同则相亲，异则相敬。乐胜则流，礼胜则离。合情饰貌者，礼乐之事也。礼义立，则贵贱等矣，乐文同，则上下和矣。好恶著则贤不肖别矣。刑禁暴，爵举贤，则政均矣。仁以爱之，义以正之，如此则民治行矣。乐由中出，礼自外作。乐由中出，故静；礼自外作，故文。大乐必易，大礼必简。乐至则无怨，礼至则不争。揖让而治天下者，礼乐之谓也。暴民不作，诸侯宾服，兵革不试，五刑不用，百姓无患，天子不怒，如此则乐达矣。合父子之亲，明长幼之序，以敬四海之内，天子如此，则礼行矣。
……

zh:
1、本游戏是一款高自由度的武侠大型多人在线角色扮演游戏，适用于年满18周岁以上的用户，建议未成年人在家长的监督下使用游戏产品。

2、本游戏以类似宋初的架空时代作为背景，不会与现实生活混淆。游戏玩法基于肢体操作和益智解谜，设有需要多人配合进行的团队玩法和竞技玩法，鼓励玩家相互沟通、挑战自我。游戏中有基于语音和文字的陌生人社交系统，社交系统的管理遵循相关法律法规的要求。

3、本游戏中有用户实名认证系统，认证为未成年人的用户将接受以下管理：
游戏中部分玩法和道具需要付费。未满8周岁的用户不能付费；8周岁以上未满16周岁的未成年人用户，单次充值金额不得超过50元人民币，每月充值金额累计不得超过200元人民币；16周岁以上的未成年人用户，单次充值金额不得超过100元人民币，每月充值金额累计不得超过400元人民币。
未实名账号不能登录游戏。未成年玩家可在周五、周六、周日和法定假日每日晚20时至21时登录游戏，其他时间无法登录游戏。

4、本游戏将中国传统文化与武侠世界相结合，在美术设计、背景音乐、文案剧情等创作中均融入了大量中华传统文化元素，有助于传播优秀的中国传统文化。玩家之间通过互相交流、配合，共同完成游戏目标，可以获得积极愉悦的情绪体验。玩家在游戏中互相帮助完成游戏任务，有助于培养玩家之间的团队协作能力。
en:
1. This game is a high-freedom Wuxia MMORPG (Massively Online Role-Playing Game) intended for users aged 18 and above. It is recommended that minors play under parental supervision.

2. The game is set in a fictional era inspired by the early Song Dynasty, clearly distinct from real-life events. The gameplay features physical controls and puzzle-solving, with both cooperative and competitive Online Modes. Players are encouraged to communicate and challenge themselves. A social system supporting text and voice interactions is available and subject to relevant laws and regulations.

3. This game has a real-name verification system. Verified minor users are subject to the following restrictions:Some gameplay features and items require payment. Users under 8 years old are not permitted to make purchases. Users aged 8 to 15 may not spend more than 50 CNY per transaction and 200 CNY per month. Users aged 16 to 17 may not spend more than 100 CNY per transaction and 400 CNY per month.

Accounts without real-name verification cannot log in. Verified minors may log in only between 20:00–21:00 on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and official holidays. Access is restricted at all other times.

4. The game blends traditional Chinese culture with the Wuxia world, incorporating rich cultural elements into its visual design, soundtrack, and narrative, which is conducive to disseminating traditional Chinese culture. Cooperative gameplay encourages communication, teamwork, and emotional engagement. Helping each other complete Quests fosters collaboration and team spirit among players.

余石遵度与王崇范、孙绍威、齐平湛、王骥、成昭、李仪安七人，负箧东行，四方来会。
经平襄，城屠三日，隍池尽赤。悬尸于梁者，如期相近，行人掩鼻而趋，莫敢正视。 
次淮阴，岁大饥，米斛五十千，民不得食，父子相鬻，缚儿就屠，刲剔如羊豕。 
野有弃婴，啼于草间，嫠妇泣尽，夜见磷火青荧，行者言人血所化。 
宿空山古寺，闻钟声咽咽，如泣如诉；泊野店荒驿，见灯焰倏起，若亡魂之不去者。 
过临丘，见竹竿零落，老父怆泣。问之，乃知前岁有贵人过，二童以竹竿为戏，竟以妖言惑众，尽斩之，弃骨道旁，至今暴白。 
至泉西故地，颓垣败壁间，闻老妪言：昔有女初嫁，吉服未解，忽刀刃鸣于庭，身首异处。其姊妹赴井以殉，阖门遂绝，墓木已拱矣。 
又见伶人醉中，以瓜置颈为戏，坐客怂恿，拔剑断之，血溅樽俎，众拊掌大笑，若无睹焉。 
吾辈鹑衣骨立，踯躅若鬼，如坠深阱，不觉旦夕。
今秦鹿奔突，见日月之晦冥，知独木之难支，唯将所历所闻，录于简牍。冀后世君子见此，识乱年之酷烈，哀黎元之倒悬。若得九州晏如，景运重开，使民免锋镝，脱冻馁，勿漂沦于离难——则吾辈虽死之日，犹生之年。
伏惟后世，慎勿忘此。
en:
I, Shi Zundu, together with six others—Wang Chongfan, Sun Shaowei, Qi Pingzhan, Wang Ji, Cheng Zhao, and Li Yi'an—shouldering our satchels, journeyed eastward, gathering together from the four directions.
Passing through Pingxiang, we found the city put to the sword for three days, its moats and pools all turned red with blood. Corpses hung from the roof beams at even intervals, and passersby covered their noses and hurried past, none daring to look directly upon them.
Next, at Huaiyin, a great famine had struck that year—a picul of rice cost fifty thousand coins, and the common folk had nothing to eat. Fathers sold their own sons; children were bound and led to slaughter, butchered as one would sheep or swine.
In the wilds, abandoned infants wailed among the grasses; widows wept until their tears ran dry. By night, one could see ghostly blue-green flames flickering—travelers said they were born of human blood.
We lodged at an ancient temple upon a deserted mountain, where we heard the bell toll in low, choking sobs, as though weeping, as though lamenting. We stopped at a desolate roadside inn, where lamp-flames suddenly leapt up of their own accord, as though restless spirits lingered still, unwilling to depart.
Passing through Linqiu, we saw bamboo poles scattered and broken, and an old man weeping in grief. Upon asking, we learned that the year before, a person of noble rank had passed through, and two children, playing with bamboo poles as toys, had been accused of spreading heretical rumors to deceive the masses, and were both beheaded, their bones cast aside along the road, bleached white even to this day.
Upon reaching the old ruins west of Quanxi, amid crumbling walls and broken partitions, we heard an old woman tell her tale: once, a young bride, her wedding finery not yet removed, heard the sudden ring of a blade in the courtyard, and in an instant her head was severed from her body. Her sisters threw themselves into the well to follow her in death. Thus the whole household was extinguished, and now trees already grow tall upon their graves.
We also saw a performer, drunk, who in jest placed a melon upon his neck as a game. The onlookers egged him on, and someone drew a sword and struck it down, splattering blood across the wine cups and dishes upon the table. Yet the crowd only clapped their hands and laughed aloud, as though they had seen nothing at all.
We, ragged and gaunt as skeletons, wandered on like lost ghosts, as though fallen into some bottomless pit, losing all sense of day and night.
Now, in the time of trouble, when the sun and moon themselves grow dim and dark, we know full well that a single lone tree cannot hold up a collapsing mountain. And so we can only set down all that we have witnessed and heard upon these bamboo slips. We hope that men of virtue in ages to come, upon reading this, shall come to know the cruelty of these chaotic years, and mourn for the common people who hung suspended in such suffering. Should the Nine Provinces ever know peace again, should fortune's bright era return once more, sparing the people from blade and arrow, from cold and hunger, from being swept away and lost amid calamity—then even on the day we ourselves perish, it shall be as though we had lived on.
We beseech those who come after us: never forget this.

【深衣第三十九】

古者深衣，盖有制度，以应规、矩、绳、权、衡。
短毋见肤，长毋被土。续衽，钩边。要缝半下；袼之高下，可以运肘；袂之长短，反诎之及肘。带下毋厌髀，上毋厌胁，当无骨者。制：十有二幅以应十有二月。
袂圜以应规；曲袷如矩以应方；负绳及踝以应直；下齐如权衡以应平。故规者，行举手以为容；负绳抱方者，以直其政，方其义也。故《易》曰：坤，“六二之动，直以方”也。下齐如权衡者，以安志而平心也。五法已施，故圣人服之。故规矩取其无私，绳取其直，权衡取其平，故先王贵之。故可以为文，可以为武，可以摈相，可以治军旅，完且弗费，善衣之次也。

en:
Deep Garment (Chapter 39)

In ancient times, the deep garment had established regulations, corresponding to the compass, the square, the plumb line, the balance, and the steelyard.
It was not so short as to reveal the skin, nor so long as to touch the ground. The overlapping front panels were continued, and the hem was curved. The waist seam was half the width of the lower hem; the height of the armhole allowed the elbow to move freely; the length of the sleeves, when bent back, reached the elbow. The sash was worn neither so low as to press against the thighbone, nor so high as to press against the ribs, but rested where there was no bone. The construction consisted of twelve panels, corresponding to the twelve months of the year.
The sleeves were rounded to correspond to the compass; the curved collar was square to correspond to the square; the back seam ran straight down to the ankle to correspond to the plumb line; the lower hem was level, like the balance and steelyard, to correspond to evenness. Thus, the rounded sleeves were for raising the hands in ceremonial posture; the straight back seam and the square collar were for maintaining upright governance and righteous conduct. Hence, the Book of Changes says: Kun, "The movement of the second yin line is straight and square." The lower hem, level like the balance and steelyard, was for settling the will and calming the mind. With these five principles applied, the sage wore it. Therefore, the compass and square represent impartiality, the plumb line represents straightness, and the balance and steelyard represent evenness—thus the former kings valued it. It could be worn for civil affairs, for military affairs, for serving as an attendant in ceremonies, and for commanding troops. It was complete yet not wasteful, and ranked just below the ceremonial robes.

zh:
于杨强而言，世间道理不过“刀快拳硬”四字，凭着一身悍勇，护着弟妹，也守着自己的山头地盘。
那日，他和弟妹三人刚劫了一队商人，本是酒肉庆功时，却被一个衣衫褴褛的逃难老头打断了。
他心情烦闷，本想教训那老头，吃了熊心豹子胆，敢在他的地盘上撒野。
可那老头的话，却如巨石，重重地砸在了他的心口。
“虏人连栾城都攻破了，你这山头又能占到几时？你和你的弟妹也迟早会变成虏人的刀下魂！”
他平生第一次觉得手边的美酒没了滋味......扫兴至极！
他的山，他的地盘……虏人要过来，连他的山头也要占了？还有他的弟妹......
“这还了得？”他猛地站起，将酒碗狠狠摔在地上，他们三人间流动着一股无言的默契......
“走！老子倒要去看看，咱们的刀，和那群虏狗的刀，到底谁更硬！"
en:
The way Yang Qiang sees it, the world runs on four words: sharp blade, hard fist. On sheer nerve and muscle, he keeps his brother and sister safe, and rules over his own patch of hill.
That day, he and his siblings had just robbed a train of merchants and were settling in to celebrate over meat and wine, when a ragged old refugee stumbled in and spoiled it.
Yang Qiang was in a foul mood. He got up, meaning to teach the old man a lesson for daring to make trouble on his turf.
But the old man's words landed like a boulder on his chest.
"The invaders have taken Luancheng. How long do you think this hill of yours will last? Sooner or later, you and your brother and sister will die on a Khitan blade too."
For the first time in his life, the fine wine in his hand lost all its flavor. What a way to kill the mood.
His hill. His turf... The invaders were coming, coming to take even his hill? And his brother, his sister...
"Not a chance." He shot to his feet and dashed the wine bowl to the ground. Between the three of them passed a wordless understanding.
"Move out! I'd damn well like to see whose blade is stronger, ours or those Khitan dogs'!"

zh:
孙弃从小便视物不清，还落了一身治不好的怪病。
他一直觉得，自己就是因为这身怪病，才被遗弃。
所幸上天给了他异常灵敏的味觉，哪怕是最相近的药草，他只要尝一口，就能分清彼此的性味。
当归入口甘中带一点辛香，质地绵柔温润；
川芎的辛味会在舌侧游走，入口劲利干脆；
茯苓尝起来近乎无味，细品才有一丝淡淡的清甜。
靠着这天赋，他近乎偏执地以身试药，用鬼画符般的字迹记在随身的小册子里。
久而久之，缠身多年的怪病，竟被他一点点试药试好了。
一次偶然，他同时服下枸杞和蔓荆子，眼前常年不散的雾气突然散开，他第一次看清了这个世界。

他能看得清的第一样东西，便是这村里那棵人人称作“万岁长生树”的古树。
这树生得奇怪，一半枝干早已枯死，乌鸦在枯枝上筑巢，另一半则枝繁叶茂，结满密密匝匝的果实。
他尝过，长生树的果子并不能让人长生。能得此名，大抵是因为树活得足够久。
也因这被时疫侵染的村子里，人人都可渴盼着能活得久一点。

这场时疫来得诡异，他眼见病患接连倒下，本地郎中束手无策，只能摇头离去。
只有敢跟着孙弃以身试药的人，才能在绝境里挣得一线生机。
村中有个少女，病势深重却求生心切，愿意依他的吩咐试药。她忍着病痛问孙弃：
“阿牛哥前几日发热不退，他的病是好了吗？”
孙弃应道：“嗯，不烧了。”
阿牛早已被他埋在长生树枯干之下，自然是凉透了。
“狗子哥前些阵子满身红疹，痛得彻夜哭喊，他也痊愈了吗？”
“嗯，他很安静。”
狗子也在树下陪着阿牛呢，再也不会叫嚷。
“神医哥哥，你当真厉害。等我哥回来，知道你医好了他的兄弟，定会满心感激。”
孙弃心底藏着一丝无人知晓的快意，这些人从前欺他眼盲体弱，如今走投无路，又来求他给他们试药治病。他只要略施小计，便能报复往日的欺辱。
抬眼望去，长生树枯槁的枝干上，竟冒出几点新芽。

少女的病日渐好转，她的兄长也回来了。
自然不是来感激的，她兄长领着一群壮汉破门而入，认定是孙弃在害妹妹，将他按在地上，强行逼他吞下他随身携带的所有草药。
他味觉素来异于常人，辨认得出那是乌头、狼毒、藜芦、生南星……皆是烈性毒物。
剧痛翻涌，孙弃的脸埋在泥土里，耳目昏沉，只剩濒死的麻木。
他不觉得自己有错，自然也不会向人辩解。
昏沉间，他听见乌鸦的叫声，摸到了自己留下标记的石块。
再摸索下去，是松软新翻的泥土，还有残破衣料——他埋人的地方，被刨开了。
他早该明白，这些人只是为了寻仇。这满村之人，或许只有他，真正在意能不能把少女的病医好。
不知是求生的执念支撑着他，还是实在不愿与这群蠢人埋骨一处，他拼尽余力向前爬行。
一颗“长生果”从枝头坠落，正好砸中了他。
微涩的果汁淌入喉间，他心里想着，往后，他一定要种出真正的长生果。

可要想求得真正长生，不知要先死过多少回。
一次次遭人记恨寻衅，一次次被逼至濒死绝境。
他早已记不清，这是他第几次在鬼门关边来回挣扎。
有人用清水拭净他脸上的泥污，又娴熟地将银针刺入他周身穴位。
施针救人——他曾在医书上见过，知道是救他，并无歹意。
“好些了吗？”
竟是个清脆稚嫩的声音。
孙弃嗓子干哑，艰难道：“眼睛……还是看不见。”
“你识药辩药的本事极好，以后莫要再以身试毒了。你要草药，只管寻我。”
孙弃摸向周身，原是那本手记早已悄然掉落。
可听着女孩小大人般的语气，他还是忍不住贫了一句：
“你瞎说的吧，我那字，只有我自己看得懂。”
话音刚落，眉间便被重重扎了一针。
双目骤然酸胀，眼泪夺眶而出。
他又能看见了。阳光，太刺眼了。
en:
Sun Qi had been half-blind since childhood, and burdened with a strange illness that no cure could touch. He had always believed it was because of that illness that he had been abandoned.
Fortunately, Heaven had given him an extraordinarily keen sense of taste. Even with the most similar herbs, one taste was enough for him to tell their properties apart.
Angelica root was sweet on the tongue with a faintly pungent warmth, soft and gentle in texture; Chuanxiong carried a sharp pungency that ran along the sides of the tongue, brisk and forceful the moment it touched the mouth; Poria tasted almost of nothing at all, only revealing the slightest trace of clean sweetness on closer savoring.
Relying on this gift, he became almost obsessive about testing medicines on himself, jotting down every result in a little notebook he kept on him, in handwriting like ghostly scratches. Over time, the strange illness that had plagued him for years was gradually cured through trial after trial.

Then, by chance, he took goji berry and vitex fruit together. The fog that had clouded his sight for years suddenly cleared, and for the first time in his life, he saw the world as it was.

The first thing he saw clearly was the ancient tree in the village, the one everyone called the "Tree of Eternal Life."
It was a strange tree. Half its branches had long since withered, with crows nesting in the deadwood, while the other half remained lush and flourishing, heavy with dense clusters of fruit.
He had tasted them before. The fruit of the Tree of Eternal Life could not grant long life at all. It was probably called that simply because the tree itself had lived so long.
And perhaps because, in this village ravaged by pestilence, everyone longed to live just a little longer.

The plague had arrived in a way that felt deeply unnatural. He watched the sick collapse one after another while the local physicians could do nothing but shake their heads and leave.
Only those willing to follow Sun Qi and test medicines on themselves had any chance of clawing out a sliver of hope.

Enduring her pain, she asked him, "Brother A'Niu had a fever that wouldn't break a few days ago. Is he better now?"
Sun Qi replied, "Mm. The fever's gone."
A'Niu had long since been buried beneath the withered half of the Tree of Eternal Life. Of course he was cold now.
"And Brother Gouzi? He was covered in rashes not long ago, crying in pain all through the night. Has he recovered too?"
"Mm. He's quiet now."
Gouzi was under the tree as well, keeping A'Niu company. He would never make another sound.
"You're incredible, divine healer. When my brother comes back and finds out you cured his brothers, he'll be so grateful."
A secret thrill stirred in Sun Qi's heart. These people had once mocked him for being blind and weak. Now, with nowhere else to turn, they came to him begging for medicines, begging to be healed.
With only the slightest trick, he could repay all the humiliation they had once dealt him.

When he looked up, he saw that a few fresh buds had sprouted from the withered branches of the Tree of Eternal Life.
The girl's condition improved day by day, and her brother finally returned.
He did not come to give thanks.
He came with a band of strongmen, broke down the door, and decided that Sun Qi had been harming his sister. They pinned him to the ground and forced every herb he carried down his throat.

His sense of taste had always been far sharper than other people's. He knew at once what he had swallowed: aconite, langdu, li lu, raw arisaema... all of them violent poisons.
Pain surged through him. His face was pressed into the dirt, his senses dim and unsteady, until all that remained was the numbness of someone on the verge of death.
He did not believe he had done anything wrong, and so he did not bother to defend himself.

Through the haze, he heard crows calling and felt the marked stone beneath his hand.
When he groped farther, he found freshly turned loose soil, and scraps of ruined cloth—the place where he had buried them had been dug up.
He should have understood it earlier. These people had only come for revenge.
In this whole village, perhaps he alone had truly cared whether the girl's illness could be cured.

Whether it was sheer stubbornness to survive, or simply that he could not bear the thought of being buried alongside such fools, he dragged himself forward with the last of his strength.
A "longevity fruit" dropped from the branch above and struck him squarely.
Its faintly bitter, astringent juice slid down his throat.
And in that moment he thought: one day, he would grow a true fruit of long life.

But if one sought true immortality, who knew how many times one would have to die first.
Again and again, people came to hate him, to make trouble for him.
Again and again, he was driven to the brink of death.He had long since lost count of how many times he had clawed his way back from the gates of death.

Someone wiped the mud from his face with clean water, then skillfully drove silver needles into the acupoints all over his body.
He had read of such lifesaving needling in medical texts. He knew this person was trying to save him, not harm him.

"Feeling any better?"
The voice was unexpectedly bright and young.
Sun Qi's throat was dry and hoarse. With difficulty, he said, "My eyes... I still can't see."
"You're exceptionally gifted at recognizing and judging herbs. Don't test poisons on yourself again. If you need herbs in the future, just come to me."

Sun Qi felt around himself and realized that his notebook had somehow slipped away without his noticing.
Still, hearing the girl speak in such a solemn, grown-up tone, he could not help teasing her.

"You're making that up. My handwriting's so bad, only I can read it."
The instant the words left his mouth, a needle drove hard into the spot between his brows.
His eyes flooded with sudden soreness, and tears burst out.
He could see again.

The sunlight was blinding.

zh:
陇州的地下武场内，比武者斗志昂扬，看戏人欢呼雀跃。但薛丑心不在焉。
他对这地儿早有耳闻，几年前便存了心思要来瞧瞧。奈何那时九流门初立，他根本无暇抽身。
而眼下嘛，其实也不是什么太好的时机……他脚下未停，闪身躲过对面那壮汉的拳风，心里还在想着九流门的那摊子事。

几番躲闪后，那壮汉漏了破绽，被薛丑一掌击倒。
薛丑搓了搓手，有些兴奋。这场局，他押了好大一笔钱，赌自己赢。接下来半年的酒钱应当是不愁了。
“换我来。”然众人的欢呼声中，一道怪异的声音响起。场内肃静。
薛丑眯起眼睛，看向那身穿黑袍，三头六臂的怪物。
是陇州老怪，陈三。
陇州素有传闻，老怪陈三身法诡异莫测，出招诡谲狠辣，是比武场上令所有武者闻风丧胆的怪物。
但薛丑仰起头，露出一个饶有趣味的笑。
是人是鬼，在他这个精通变换之术的术师面前，自见分晓。
en:
Inside Longzhou's underground fighting arena, the competitors were fired up, and the crowd roared with excitement. But Xue Chou's mind was elsewhere.  
He'd heard about this place for years and had wanted to come check it out ever since. Back when the Nine Mortal Ways was just getting started, though, he was too busy to make the trip.  
And even now, it wasn't exactly the perfect time... As he dodged a heavy punch from a burly opponent, his thoughts kept drifting back to the problems brewing at the Nine Mortal Ways.  

After a few well-timed moves, the strongman slipped up, and Xue Chou sent him crashing down with a single palm strike.  
As Xue Chou rubbed his hands together, a spark of excitement flickered in his eyes. He'd placed a hefty bet on himself. It looked like his drinks for the next half year were covered.  

"Let me handle it from here." A strange voice cut through the cheers, silencing the arena.  
Squinting, Xue Chou turned toward the figure cloaked in black, Chen San, Longzhou's legendary old beast.  

Longzhou was rife with stories about Chen San: a terrifying fighter with superhuman powers, whose unpredictable and ruthless moves made him a nightmare to face in the ring.  

But Xue Chou leaned back, a wry smile playing on his lips.  
Ghost or man, he thought, a master of transformation like him would see right through it all.

璇玑感到遗憾：它不敢沾水时，有许多人在水里、水边玩，如今它懂得了玩水的乐趣，水边和水中却几乎看不到人了。
难道，人们都成功从水中捞走了月亮，所以不再来了吗？
璇玑活力四射地在水中扑腾，或小心翼翼地将爪子伸入水面，活力四射或小心翼翼，月亮的倒影都会在它接触水面的瞬间破碎成千万片。
一片都捞不起来，真是太让猫生气了。
璇玑不屈不挠地捞着月亮。被安一飞捡到时，它醉倒在了酒里。
en:
Polaris loved the water, spending endless hours at its edge. 
It once felt sorrow: when it feared water, many people frolicked along the banks. Now that it had learned to embrace the water's joy, the shore had fallen silent. 
Had they at last caught the moon from the water's surface, so no one returned? 
With boundless energy or tender care, Polaris dove and pawed at the rippling reflection, shattering the moon's image into countless shining fragments each time. 
Not a single piece could be gathered—frustration no cat could bear. 
Yet Polaris never ceased reaching, and when An Yifei found it, the cat was gently sleeping in a cup of wine.
Sir, what is this…?

zh: 心不静，就再也回不去安宁。 这串佛珠陪伴着有明。 从一个喜欢佛理的世家子，到被迫遁入空门避祸，成为一代高僧。 他从没放下它。 邙山约战时，他又被迫想起阖门覆灭的痛苦，株连横行的惶恐。本已被经文磨钝的仇恨，在有心人的几句挑拨下，重新如烈火般燃起，灼得他再难安宁 。他做出了那个判决，冤枉了那个人。 那天，这串佛珠就丢了。有明没有去找。  几十年后，有明在临终前用药水将真相写下，将自己的罪孽写下。 但他不曾将这手书昭示，只是藏在佛经之中。 他到死也没放下那串佛珠。不管是之前的仇，还是后来的悔。
en: Once the heart loses its stillness, true peace can never return. The prayer beads had been Youming's lifelong companions. From a young lord dabbling in the Dharma, to a refugee forced into the monastic order to escape his family's ruin, and finally to an eminent monk, he had never once set them down. Yet, during the duel at Mount Mang, the buried agony of his slaughtered clan and the suffocating terror of their extermination were violently unearthed. His hatred, worn smooth by decades of chanted sutras, flared back into a roaring inferno, stoked by the poisoned whispers of schemers. Consumed by a fire that burned away his hard-won peace, he delivered that verdict. He condemned an innocent soul. On that day, the prayer beads were lost, and Youming never sought to find them. Decades later, upon his deathbed, the monk used a secret tincture to pen the truth and confess his sins. But he never offered his confession to the world, choosing instead to entomb the parchment within the Buddhist scriptures. Until his final breath, he never truly let go of those prayer beads, shackled forever to the bitter hatred that came before, and the suffocating remorse that followed.

Not long ago, for reasons unknown, Buddha Fort broke ties with Mercyheart Monastery, and under Huiyong's leadership, the ascetic monks have been stirring up trouble... Lately, they've been stockpiling gunpowder and kidnapping skilled artisans, though their true motives remain unclear.
